title: RHCE in Ansible on AlmaLinux 10
description: Prepare for EX294 after RHCSA with two AlmaLinux 10 guests. Build and recover repeatable automation for services, security, storage and scheduled backups. Includes original two-host practicals, graded knowledge checks, spaced-repetition cards and reviewer-scored work orders.

modules.title: A repeatable change and its evidence
Git, Navigator and the development container
One playbook for two different hosts
Deploy and operate a local web service
Manage service identities, templates and encrypted credentials
Publish and maintain a private HTTP service
Release reusable automation and recover from failure
Provision storage, archive records and schedule recovery

lessons.title: Translate a support ticket into a testable state
topics: Translate a support ticket into a testable state
lessons.body:
If a server were rebuilt tonight, how would the next administrator know which changes to put back? Your RHCSA skills let you fix the running machine. In this course you also keep the instructions that can rebuild it. Start with a small request from the evening shift: put a handoff notice on one server and make sure a later run can restore it if somebody edits it.

## From one guest to an inventory

In RHCSA you checked a machine with hostname, inspected ownership with stat and changed one machine at a time. Here the client becomes the **control node**. You describe the desired state in a playbook, run it against the server, and use those same RHCSA checks on the server to prove the result. Before starting, you should be comfortable identifying a guest, reading file modes and using an authorized sudo account.

A leading `> ` marks what you type at the shell. Leave that first marker out. The unmarked line beneath each command shows its output or describes what to look for. A greater-than sign **inside** a command is part of the command. In a multiline example, enter the marked lines in order.

## Practice on AlmaLinux 10.3

In Erudior Desktop choose **Open practice terminal**, then **Start lab**. The client is your control node and the server is your managed node. Use **Server console** to check the target independently. For a manual pair, use the downloads below.

[AlmaLinux 10.3 x86_64 DVD installer (10.82 GB)](https://repo.almalinux.org/almalinux/10.3/isos/x86_64/AlmaLinux-10.3-x86_64-dvd.iso) · [Practice kit ZIP](https://app.erudior.com/downloads/Erudior-AlmaLinux-10.3-Practice-Kit.zip)

The **Practice kit** sets up a private server and client. Open **Set up and reset the AlmaLinux 10.3 lab** in this lesson’s references for installation steps. The **Offline copy of the practice kit** reference also contains the complete ZIP. Choose the **rhce** profile. The client runs Ansible and the server receives changes over SSH. Stage the execution environment before disconnecting for Navigator practicals.

If you built the pair manually with the kit, once both guests pass their readiness checks, power them off and run the following command on the host.

```text
> python3 lab.py capture rhce
The kit records the powered-off pair as the requested baseline. An active
guest can prevent capture.
```

During a manual reset, both practice disks revert to the saved state. Copy out evidence first. When you want that fresh state, run the following on the host.

```text
> python3 lab.py reset rhce --start --offline
The selected kit baseline is restored and the guests start with offline
networking. Check the consoles after boot.
```

The kit starts the restored machines on their private network.

## Decide what counts as success

A request to “set up the file” leaves several decisions open. For the guided job the destination is `/etc/erudior-shift.conf`, the line is `shift=evening` followed by a newline, the owner and group are both `root`, and the mode is `0644`. Other users need to read the notice. Only root needs to edit it. A successful run recreates the same result on a clean target. A second run on a correct target reports zero changes. This property is called [[Idempotence]].

**Predict.** An administrator types the right line into the server once. Another writes a playbook that appends the line on every run. Whose work meets the whole request? Neither does. The manual change leaves no executable recipe. Repeated appends introduce duplicates. A task that manages the whole contents of this lab-owned file can satisfy both requirements.

## Set up the two machines

Use two disposable AlmaLinux 10 VMs with different hostnames and a shared private virtual network. You can reuse the **manual** client/server pair from Zero to RHCSA. Use normal VM terminals for this course. If you are starting fresh, install AlmaLinux 10 Minimal on two guests, choose different hostnames in the installer, and create a `learner` account with administrator privileges on each. Give both a private adapter on the same virtual switch. Use the addresses below on that adapter, or substitute your own throughout. Each guest needs access to its installation media or enabled AlmaLinux package repositories for setup.

| Machine | Example private address | What lives here |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Client, the [[Control node]] | 192.168.77.20/24 | Inventory, source files, playbooks and private SSH key |
| Server, the [[Managed node]] | 192.168.77.10/24 | SSH service, Python and the configuration your team requested |

On **each** console, run these commands. Record the distribution ID, major version, hostname, username and private address. Both guests should report `almalinux` and a version beginning with `10`. If the names or addresses match each other, fix the duplicate before continuing.

```text
> cat /etc/os-release
Look for ID="almalinux" and VERSION_ID beginning with 10. Other lines
describe the same installation.

> hostnamectl --static
The guest's configured static hostname, client or server on the kit pair.
```

```text
> id -un
learner

> ip -br -4 address
The private IPv4 address is 192.168.77.20 on client or 192.168.77.10 on
server.
```

On the **client** install the automation tools. On the **server** install the remote prerequisites and start the service. Use the administrator password when prompted.

**Client**

```text
> sudo dnf install ansible-core openssh-clients
DNF lists the named packages in a transaction or reports that they are
already installed. Check for completion.
```

`ansible-playbook` reads a YAML playbook and runs its tasks against the selected inventory hosts. The --version option only reports the controller toolchain.

```text
> ansible-playbook --version
The ansible-core version, active configuration file and Python interpreter
path.
```

**Server**

```text
> sudo dnf install python3 openssh-server sudo
DNF lists the named packages in a transaction or reports that they are
already installed. Check for completion.

> sudo systemctl enable --now sshd
The service starts and is enabled at boot. systemd can print the new
enablement link.
```

```text
> systemctl is-active sshd
active

> sudo -v
May prompt for your sudo password. On acceptance it returns to the prompt
with no further output.
```

If the client cannot find `ansible-core`, check `dnf repolist --enabled` for AlmaLinux AppStream and BaseOS.

```text
> dnf repolist --enabled
Enabled repository IDs and names.
```

If the virtual switch is isolated, install from the AlmaLinux DVD repositories or while a package-network adapter is connected. The already-installed tools will run over the private link. The server needs no Ansible installation for these tasks.

## How this fits the credential

This is Erudior's RHCSA-to-RHCE **in Ansible** course. EX294 is the Ansible exam for that path. Red Hat also has an Enterprise Linux troubleshooting path through EX342. Here you practice automation on AlmaLinux 10. The exam uses Red Hat Ansible Automation Platform. You can read and take the quizzes in Erudior, then carry out the work on your two VMs.

[Red Hat RHCE in Ansible](https://www.redhat.com/en/services/certification/red-hat-certified-engineer-in-ansible) · [EX294 objectives](https://www.redhat.com/en/services/training/ex294-red-hat-certified-engineer-rhce-exam-red-hat-enterprise-linux) · [AlmaLinux installation images](https://almalinux.org/get-almalinux/)

lessons.title: Prove who is on each end of SSH
topics: Prove who is on each end of SSH
lessons.body:
The server accepts connections, but which server answered, who did you log in as, and who may write under `/etc`? You will answer those three questions separately before giving Ansible the job.

## Establish the identity of the server

At the **server console**, display its SSH host key fingerprint. On the **client**, start a login to the server's private address. The first connection asks whether you trust the host. Compare the displayed SHA256 fingerprint with the server console's value. Accept only a match. If this address already has a different recorded key, verify the address, VM and key change at the server console before updating its individual entry.

**Server console**

```text
> sudo ssh-keygen -lf /etc/ssh/ssh_host_ed25519_key.pub
A SHA256 fingerprint and algorithm. Compare the full fingerprint through the
trusted console.
```

**Client**

```text
> ssh -o HostKeyAlgorithms=ssh-ed25519 learner@192.168.77.10
On first contact, SSH asks you to verify the fingerprint. A match and
successful login open the server shell.
```

With password login enabled for this lab account, use the server account password, check `hostname` and `id -un`, then `exit` to return to the client.

```text
> hostname
server on the kit pair.

> id -un
learner
```

```text
> exit
The current shell closes. In a nested login this returns you to the calling
shell.
```

With a key-only cloud image, use the existing provisioned key for this first connection or install the public key below through the server console. The host fingerprint identifies the machine. Your user key proves your right to log in to its `learner` account.

## Give the controller a lab key

Work as `learner` on the client. Run the key generator only for a new lab key. If this filename already belongs to the lab, reuse it. Choose a passphrase when creating it. Load the private key into an agent in this terminal. Use the same terminal for the following lessons.

```text
> install -d -m 700 ~/.ssh
No output. ~/.ssh exists with permissions restricted to the account.

> ssh-keygen -t ed25519 -f ~/.ssh/erudior_rhce
Prompts for a passphrase, then reports the new private key, public key and
fingerprint.
```

`eval` asks Bash to interpret the text returned by the command inside the quotation marks. Here the trusted local ssh-agent supplies its own socket and process variables. `ssh-agent` starts a process that holds unlocked SSH identities. The -s option prints shell assignments that connect this shell to the agent.

```text
> eval "$(ssh-agent -s)"
Agent pid followed by a number. This shell now knows the agent's socket.
```

`ssh-add` loads a key into the current agent or lists loaded identities with -l.

```text
> ssh-add ~/.ssh/erudior_rhce
Identity added followed by the lab key path. A protected key prompts for its
passphrase.

> ssh-copy-id -i ~/.ssh/erudior_rhce.pub learner@192.168.77.10
A key-added count or a notice that the public key is already installed.
```

For a key-only image where `ssh-copy-id` cannot bootstrap a login, use the server console as `learner`. Create `~/.ssh` with mode 0700, append the single line from the client's `erudior_rhce.pub` to `~/.ssh/authorized_keys`, set that file's mode to 0600 and run the following command.

```text
> restorecon -RFv ~/.ssh
No output if labels already match. Changed labels can be reported with the
verbose option.
```

The private key stays on the client.

## Test login and privilege separately

```text
> ssh -o BatchMode=yes -o IdentitiesOnly=yes -i ~/.ssh/erudior_rhce learner@192.168.77.10 'hostname; id -un; python3 --version'
Three lines from the server, normally server, learner and Python 3 followed
by its version.

> ssh -t -o IdentitiesOnly=yes -i ~/.ssh/erudior_rhce learner@192.168.77.10 'sudo id -u'
0 after the remote sudo check succeeds.
```

The first command should identify the server, the user `learner` and a Python 3 version, with no login prompt. The second should print `0` after sudo authorization. If it asks for a password, use the server learner's sudo password. A successful login with denied sudo tells you exactly which permission to investigate. In Ansible, [[Privilege escalation]] is requested by `become: true`. The `-K` option asks for the become password. With working passwordless sudo on a prepared lab VM you may omit `-K`.

**Try it.** Start a second client terminal. Check `ssh-add -l`.

```text
> ssh-add -l
The fingerprint of the loaded lab identity. An empty agent reports that it
has no identities.
```

A new terminal may not inherit the agent socket. Return to the original terminal or start an agent and reload the key in this one. Predict what `BatchMode=yes` will do when only a locked private key is available, then try the first command. It must succeed without prompting before you move on.

## Configure a managed-node privilege rule

At the **server console**, practise granting one read-only privileged operation to a separate, temporary account. Use this disposable account so your existing learner access stays available. Check `getent passwd erudior_probe` and `sudo test ! -e /etc/sudoers.d/erudior-probe` first. Continue on a clean guest if either name is already in use. This small rule demonstrates sudo policy. Ansible modules use temporary programs, so the learner's separately authorized general become access is still needed for ordinary administration.

```text
> sudo useradd --system --no-create-home --shell /sbin/nologin erudior_probe
The practice account exists outside the wheel group.

> rule=$(mktemp)
The shell records the pathname of a temporary file.

> printf '%s\n' 'erudior_probe ALL=(root) NOPASSWD: /usr/bin/id -u' > "$rule"
The rule allows one executable and that exact argument as root.

> sudo visudo -cf "$rule"
Continue only if the temporary file parses successfully.

> sudo install -o root -g root -m 0440 "$rule" /etc/sudoers.d/erudior-probe
The validated rule is installed in the drop-in directory.

> sudo visudo -c
The effective policy, including the installed rule, should parse successfully.

> sudo -u erudior_probe sudo -n /usr/bin/id -u
0

> sudo -u erudior_probe sudo -n /usr/bin/id -g
The invocation is refused with nonzero status. The argument is outside the rule.
```

Remove just these exercise objects with `sudo rm /etc/sudoers.d/erudior-probe`, `sudo userdel erudior_probe` and `rm "$rule"`. Check `sudo visudo -c` again. Record the authorized identity, command and observed refusal without including any authentication material.

lessons.title: Select the right machines before running a task
topics: Select the right machines before running a task
lessons.body:
A colleague asks you to update “the operations servers.” Ansible needs a precise list of machines before that phrase can be used safely in a play. A static [[Inventory]] gives a machine a stable name and puts it in groups. Here, `node1` is the inventory name, `192.168.77.10` is its SSH destination, and `ops` is the group you will target.

## Make a project with a predictable scope

On the client, as `learner`, create a private working directory. Use it for every remaining client command. In each file block, copy only the contents of the block.

```text
> mkdir -p -m 700 ~/rhce-work/files
No output. The project contains a files directory.

> cd ~/rhce-work
No output. The shell now works in the named project directory.
```

```text
> chmod 700 .
No output. Access to this project directory is restricted to its owner.
```

Create **inventory.ini**. Replace the address if you chose another one.

```ini
[ops]
node1 ansible_host=192.168.77.10
```

Create **ansible.cfg** in the same directory. `remote_user` selects the login account. The key is the one you tested earlier. Host key checking uses the trusted entry that you verified when connecting to this address.

```ini
[defaults]
inventory = ./inventory.ini
remote_user = learner
private_key_file = ~/.ssh/erudior_rhce
host_key_checking = True
```

## Prove what will run where

`ansible` runs a single module against an inventory host pattern. The -m argument names the module.

```text
> ansible --version
The ansible-core version, active configuration file and Python interpreter
path.
```

`ansible-inventory` shows how Ansible resolved inventory groups, host aliases and variables before you run tasks.

```text
> ansible-inventory --graph
The graph places node1 under @ops.

> ansible ops --list-hosts
Exactly one host, node1, under the ops group.
```

```text
> ansible ops -m ansible.builtin.ping
node1 reports SUCCESS with ping set to pong.
```

Read the `config file` line of the first command. It should identify your project's `ansible.cfg`. The graph places `node1` under `@ops`. The host list should show exactly one target. These first three checks use local data. The last command opens an SSH session and asks remote Python to run an Ansible [[Module]]. A successful `pong` demonstrates that the transport, account and Python interpreter worked together. You have yet to test a privileged write.

**Fault exercise.** Run the following command.

```text
> ansible opx --list-hosts
A host-pattern warning and zero matching hosts. Compare the group spelling
with the graph.
```

Expect a warning about the pattern and zero hosts. Then run the following command from the project and confirm the target reappears.

```text
> ansible ops --list-hosts
Exactly one host, node1, under the ops group.
```

Why would a successful shell exit or a lack of failed hosts give you false confidence here? No remote work can fail if the selection is empty.

| Observation | First thing to check |
| --- | --- |
| Unexpected or empty list | Working directory, config file path, group spelling and inventory graph |
| Host listed, SSH timeout | Server address, private adapter, sshd listener and SSH access in the active firewall zone |
| Host key verification failed | Compare the fingerprint with the server console |
| Permission denied (publickey) | Remote username, agent, selected key and authorized public key |
| SSH works, module reports interpreter error | Run python3 --version on the managed node |

[Ansible inventory guide](https://docs.ansible.com/projects/ansible/latest/inventory_guide/intro_inventory.html) · [Ansible ping module](https://docs.ansible.com/projects/ansible/latest/collections/ansible/builtin/ping_module.html)

lessons.title: Deploy the shift notice and repair drift
topics: Deploy the shift notice and repair drift
lessons.body:
Evening shift has confirmed the desired file. Keep its text on the controller alongside the instructions for installing it. A replacement server can then be configured from the same two files.

## Write the play

From `~/rhce-work` on the client, create the source file. The newline is part of its contents.

```text
> printf 'shift=evening\n' > files/shift.conf
No output. files/shift.conf contains exactly the evening line with its final
newline.
```

Create **shift.yml** in the project directory. A [[Playbook]] is a YAML list of plays. The first dash starts this play. The second dash starts a task within its `tasks` list. Keep the indentation in spaces. Read it aloud: “On the hosts in ops, become an administrator and copy this project file to this path with these attributes.”

```yaml
---
- name: Maintain the shift notice
  hosts: ops
  become: true
  gather_facts: false
  tasks:
    - name: Install the evening shift notice
      ansible.builtin.copy:
        src: files/shift.conf
        dest: /etc/erudior-shift.conf
        owner: root
        group: root
        mode: '0644'
```

`src` names a file on the controller. `dest` is on the managed node. The module compares the desired bytes and attributes with the remote file and corrects differences. Quoting the octal mode keeps it a string when YAML is read. This play needs no host facts, so the recap reflects just the copy task. Use `ansible-doc ansible.builtin.copy` on the controller to look up the defaults for `remote_src` and the meaning of `mode`.

`ansible-doc` opens the installed documentation for a named Ansible module, including its parameters and examples.

```text
> ansible-doc ansible.builtin.copy
Module documentation opens. Find src, dest, owner and mode. Press q if a
pager opens.
```

## Predict, apply, run again

At the server console, confirm `/etc/erudior-shift.conf` is unused on this disposable server. Start the following sequence in the client project directory. On passwordless lab VMs you may omit `-K`.

```text
> ansible-playbook --syntax-check shift.yml
A successful syntax check identifies the playbook. A syntax error instead
identifies the affected file and location.

> ansible-playbook --list-hosts shift.yml
Exactly node1 in the target list. No tasks run.
```

```text
> ansible-playbook -K --check --diff shift.yml
On a fresh node the preview shows the file addition, changed=1, failed=0 and
unreachable=0. The remote file is still absent.
```

For a clean server expect one listed host and a predicted change. At the server console, verify `test ! -e /etc/erudior-shift.conf && echo absent`.

```text
> test ! -e /etc/erudior-shift.conf && echo absent
absent on a fresh server after the preview.
```

Check mode predicted what this module would do. Apply the change, then run the same play again.

```text
> ansible-playbook -K shift.yml
On a fresh node, the recap for node1 has changed=1, unreachable=0 and
failed=0.

> ansible-playbook -K shift.yml
node1: changed=0, unreachable=0, failed=0 on the immediate repeat.
```

On the first live run expect `node1` with `changed=1`, then `changed=0` on the second. Both recaps should have `failed=0` and `unreachable=0`. If the first run says `changed=0`, inspect whether the exact state already existed. A syntax check can pass with a misspelled group. A green recap alone cannot show that you selected the right machine.

## Challenge the result

On the **server**, inspect the outcome and then introduce one small error into this lab file.

```text
> cat /etc/erudior-shift.conf
shift=evening

> stat -c '%U:%G %a' /etc/erudior-shift.conf
root:root 644
```

```text
> sudo chmod 0600 /etc/erudior-shift.conf
No output. The mode is now 600, creating drift for the next play to repair.
```

A learner who only reads the file as root would miss this fault. From the **client**, preview and apply the same play again. The contents already match, but `mode` has drifted. On the server, check that the owner, group and mode are `root:root 644`, and that `learner` can once again read the exact line. Run the play once more and record its change count.

[Copy module parameters](https://docs.ansible.com/projects/ansible/latest/collections/ansible/builtin/copy_module.html) · [Check mode and diff mode](https://docs.ansible.com/projects/ansible/latest/playbook_guide/playbooks_checkmode.html)

lessons.title: Independent practical: the morning handoff
topics: Independent practical: the morning handoff
lessons.body:
**Work order.** The morning operator needs a separate handoff file on the operations server. Its text is one line, `queue=morning`, ending with a newline. Put it at `/etc/erudior-handoff.conf`. Root should own the file and group. Its mode must be 0640. Only the owner may write. Users outside the owning group get no access. The evening file must still be correct.

Use your manual AlmaLinux pair. Keep the inventory, configuration and key from earlier lessons. If you are restarting here, first complete the project setup and evening shift exercise. Save a new playbook as `handoff.yml` and a new controller-side source file. Make the play target only the `ops` group. You can use installed module help. Try the job before opening the **Practical answer and scoring guide** in Study tools.

## Give the next operator evidence

1. **Scope and preview, 2 points.** Record the sole target of `--list-hosts`. Preview the play on a clean lab path and verify at the server console that the path is still absent after the preview. 2. **Deployment, 2 points.** Apply the play. Record its recap and inspect the remote bytes, owner, group and mode. Check the evening file's contents and permissions as well. 3. **Repeatability, 2 points.** Run the same unmodified play a second time. Record the target and the changed, failed and unreachable counts. 4. **Recovery, 2 points.** At the server console use `printf 'queue=late\n' | sudo tee /etc/erudior-handoff.conf` to change the contents.

```text
> printf 'queue=late\n' | sudo tee /etc/erudior-handoff.conf
queue=late
```

Preview, then apply your original play. Independently check the restored bytes and mode. 5. **Persistence, 2 points.** At the server console record `cat /proc/sys/kernel/random/boot_id`, then run `sudo systemctl reboot` on this lab guest.

```text
> cat /proc/sys/kernel/random/boot_id
A boot identifier with five groups of hexadecimal characters. Compare it
with your earlier reading to detect a reboot.

> sudo systemctl reboot
The guest restarts. Reconnect, then compare its new boot ID with the one
recorded earlier.
```

After login, record the new boot ID. Check both files before running any configuration play. Finish with an unchanged run from the client.

For the exact byte check, use the following on the **server** as the ordinary learner. The comparison includes the trailing newline. `cmp` prints nothing on a match, and the success message appears only when it returns zero.

```text
> printf 'queue=morning\n' | sudo cmp - /etc/erudior-handoff.conf && echo morning-ok
morning-ok

> printf 'shift=evening\n' | cmp - /etc/erudior-shift.conf && echo evening-ok
evening-ok
```

```text
> stat -c '%n %U:%G %a' /etc/erudior-{handoff,shift}.conf
/etc/erudior-handoff.conf root:root 640
/etc/erudior-shift.conf root:root 644
```

Award each pair of points when you have evidence for the whole row. Record your own score out of 10 and repeat any missing row. Erudior scores the written quiz separately. A corrected file after reboot is useful evidence only if you checked it before running the play again.

**Debrief.** A teammate wants to use `--check` as the only release test. Use your own preview and first live recap to describe one observation that only a live run gave you. Then explain how a play that appends a duplicate line on every run would fail your evidence checks.

```assignment
lab: morning-handoff-evidence
```

lessons.title: Hand a reproducible project to a teammate
topics: Hand a reproducible project to a teammate
lessons.body:
On Monday a release worked from your home directory. On Tuesday a teammate cloned the project and got “file not found.” The playbook was committed, but its source file existed only on your machine. In this unit the handoff succeeds when another checkout contains everything needed to make the change.

## Prepare a private remote

Use the same AlmaLinux 10 **client** and **server** from the first unit. The examples use the server address `192.168.77.10`, your `learner` account and the key already authorized there. Substitute your own server address in every example. Use fresh lab directories for this first pass. The course estimates assume the VMs are installed. Allow extra time and disk space to download two container images on the client.

On the **server console**, initialize the repository as learner. A [[Bare repository]] stores Git history and branch names. It needs no working copy because its job here is to receive pushes.

```text
> sudo dnf install git-core
DNF lists the named packages in a transaction or reports that they are
already installed. Check for completion.

> mkdir -p ~/repos
No output. The server's learner home has a repos directory.
```

`git` records versions of project files. Its subcommand selects an operation such as init, add, commit or push.

```text
> git init --bare --initial-branch=main ~/repos/handoff.git
Git reports an initialized empty bare repository at ~/repos/handoff.git.
```

On the **client**, install Git, then start a dedicated SSH agent. Navigator and the editor will each need access to the same lab identity. Use this agent only for your lab key. The socket directory below will be shared with the development container.

```text
> sudo dnf install git-core
DNF lists the named packages in a transaction or reports that they are
already installed. Check for completion.

> install -d -m 700 ~/.local/share/erudior-rhce-agent
No output. The private agent directory exists with mode 700.
```

```text
> eval "$(ssh-agent -a "$HOME/.local/share/erudior-rhce-agent/socket" -s)"
Agent pid followed by a number. This shell now knows the agent's socket.

> ssh-add -t 4h ~/.ssh/erudior_rhce
Identity added followed by the lab key path. A protected key prompts for its
passphrase.
```

```text
> ssh-add -l
The fingerprint of the loaded lab identity. An empty agent reports that it
has no identities.
```

If you open another terminal, set `export SSH_AUTH_SOCK="$HOME/.local/share/erudior-rhce-agent/socket"` and run `ssh-add -l`.

`export` makes a shell variable available to programs launched from this shell.

```text
> export SSH_AUTH_SOCK="$HOME/.local/share/erudior-rhce-agent/socket"
No output. SSH clients launched from this shell now use the specified
socket.

> ssh-add -l
The fingerprint of the loaded lab identity. An empty agent reports that it
has no identities.
```

Reuse a working agent. If the key has expired, load it again. Keep the private key and any passphrase outside the project.

## Make the first commit

On the **client**, create a new project beside the first unit's directory. Reuse your inventory. Give this checkout a Git identity. The name and email label the commit. SSH separately authenticates the push.

```text
> mkdir -p ~/rhce-release/ssh ~/rhce-release/files
No output. The project directories named on the command line now exist.

> cd ~/rhce-release
No output. The shell now works in the named project directory.
```

```text
> cp ~/rhce-work/inventory.ini .
No output. The named project files have been copied into the destination
directory.

> git init -b main
A new Git repository is initialized in this directory with main as its
starting branch.
```

```text
> git config user.name 'Lab Operator'
No output. The setting is saved in this repository's local Git
configuration.

> git config user.email 'operator@example.test'
No output. The setting is saved in this repository's local Git
configuration.
```

Carry over the server identity that you verified at its console in the first unit. The following command uses that existing trust to read the server's **public host key**. Compare the resulting fingerprint with the one displayed on the server by `sudo ssh-keygen -lf /etc/ssh/ssh_host_ed25519_key.pub` before proceeding.

```text
> sudo ssh-keygen -lf /etc/ssh/ssh_host_ed25519_key.pub
A SHA256 fingerprint and algorithm. Compare the full fingerprint through the
trusted console.
```

```text
> ssh -o StrictHostKeyChecking=yes learner@192.168.77.10 'cat /etc/ssh/ssh_host_ed25519_key.pub' | awk '{print "192.168.77.10", $1, $2}' > ssh/known_hosts
No terminal output. ssh/known_hosts now has a verified public host-key entry
for 192.168.77.10.

> ssh-keygen -lf ssh/known_hosts
A SHA256 fingerprint for each public host key in the file. Compare with the
trusted guest consoles.
```

Save **ansible.cfg** below. The SSH agent supplies the user identity. The project carries only the trusted public host key, so the same configuration can run inside an environment with a different home directory. Run from the project root so the relative trust file can be found.

```ini
[defaults]
inventory = ./inventory.ini
remote_user = learner
host_key_checking = True

[ssh_connection]
ssh_common_args = -o StrictHostKeyChecking=yes -o UserKnownHostsFile=./ssh/known_hosts
```

Save **.gitignore** below. Logs and retry files are local run output. Review the staged file list even when ignore rules are present.

```text
ansible-navigator.log
.ansible/
*.retry
*-artifact-*.json
```

```text
> git add .gitignore ansible.cfg inventory.ini ssh/known_hosts
No output. Git staged the current versions of the named files for the next
commit.

> git diff --cached --stat
A short summary of staged changes, including the affected filenames.
```

```text
> git commit -m 'Define and verify the operations target'
A commit summary with branch, abbreviated commit ID and message. Save the ID
for comparison.

> git remote add origin learner@192.168.77.10:repos/handoff.git
No output. origin now identifies the bare repository on the server.
```

```text
> git push -u origin main
Git reports the updated remote branch or that it is already up to date.
Compare the destination branch with the intended one.

> git status --short --branch
A line beginning with ## names the current branch and upstream. Additional
lines indicate local changes.
```

```text
> git ls-remote origin refs/heads/main
A full commit ID followed by the requested remote branch ref.
```

The [[Staging area]] holds the version that the next commit will contain. A commit records that snapshot locally. A push makes the named branch available at the remote. Compare `git rev-parse HEAD` with the first field from `git ls-remote`.

```text
> git rev-parse HEAD
The full commit ID currently checked out in this directory.
```

If the two IDs differ, your teammate will receive a different revision.

**Try it.** Add a comment line to your working copy of `inventory.ini`. Compare `git diff`, `git diff --cached`, and `git show HEAD:inventory.ini`.

```text
> git diff
The unstaged changes. No output if the working files match the index.

> git diff --cached
A diff of the staged changes that the next commit would record. Press q if a
pager opens.
```

```text
> git show HEAD:inventory.ini
The inventory as recorded in the current commit, including its group and
alias.
```

Explain why a fresh clone cannot see that comment. Remove just your practice comment in the editor before moving on.

[Git staging and commits](https://git-scm.com/book/en/v2/Git-Basics-Recording-Changes-to-the-Repository)

lessons.title: Identify the Ansible runtime that will execute your play
topics: Identify the Ansible runtime that will execute your play
lessons.body:
Two people can clone the same Git commit and still run different versions of Ansible. An [[Execution environment]] packages the Ansible runtime, Python and supported content in a container image. Navigator starts that image on the client. The AlmaLinux server continues to receive tasks over SSH. Which machine needs Podman? Only the client in this lab.

## Install the client tools

As learner on the AlmaLinux client, install Podman and a separate Python environment for Navigator. This unit uses the x86-64 VMs from unit one. Reserve several GiB of free space in the client user's container storage. Software emulation can make the first image unpack slow.

```text
> sudo dnf install podman python3-pip
DNF lists the named packages in a transaction or reports that they are
already installed. Check for completion.

> python3 -m venv ~/.venvs/rhce-nav
No routine output. ~/.venvs/rhce-nav now contains an isolated Python
environment.
```

`source` reads a file of shell instructions into the current shell, allowing an activation script to change its environment.

```text
> source ~/.venvs/rhce-nav/bin/activate
No routine output. The shell now resolves Python and pip through the virtual
environment.
```

`python` runs the interpreter selected by the current environment. With -m pip it runs that interpreter's package installer.

```text
> python -m pip install 'ansible-navigator==26.11.0'
Installation progress or an already-satisfied message for the requested
Navigator release.
```

`ansible-navigator` runs and inspects Ansible content using the configured execution environment. Its own version and the ansible-core version inside the image can differ.

```text
> ansible-navigator --version
The installed Navigator version. Compare with the version pinned for this
unit.

> podman info --format '{{.Host.Security.Rootless}}'
true
```

Expect `true` from Podman. Pull the course image as this same **ordinary user**. Rootless Podman keeps a per-user image store. A copy pulled with sudo would be in a different store. If you have been given an offline archive, use `podman load -i /path/to/archive.tar` as learner and verify its name and digest.

```text
> podman pull ghcr.io/ansible-community/community-ee-minimal:2.21.6-1
Image layer download or reuse messages followed by the image identifier in
this user's store.

> podman image inspect --format '{{.Digest}}' ghcr.io/ansible-community/community-ee-minimal:2.21.6-1
A digest beginning with sha256:. Compare the complete value for the selected
image and architecture.
```

For this x86-64 release the tested image manifest digest is `sha256:6c6a9fcd93420d3b75f38f29ed239069dfcb2a6e13376163f7d1fc4ac943f6b9`. A tag is a name. A [[Manifest digest]] identifies a particular manifest by its contents. If the value differs, check the image name and architecture before treating the toolchains as equivalent.

## Configure and inspect the runtime

In `~/rhce-release`, save **ansible-navigator.yml**. The policy `never` makes this exercise use the locally staged image. A misspelled image name now fails early. The Ansible configuration from the previous lesson still controls the remote login and inventory.

```yaml
---
ansible-navigator:
  mode: stdout
  execution-environment:
    enabled: true
    container-engine: podman
    image: ghcr.io/ansible-community/community-ee-minimal:2.21.6-1
    pull:
      policy: never
  playbook-artifact:
    enable: false
```

```text
> cd ~/rhce-release
No output. The shell now works in the named project directory.

> ansible-navigator inventory -i inventory.ini --graph
The execution environment's inventory graph with node1 under @ops.
```

```text
> ansible-navigator doc ansible.builtin.copy
The copy module reference supplied inside the execution environment.

> ansible-navigator exec -- ansible --version
The ansible-core and Python versions from inside the selected image.
```

The graph should put only `node1` in `ops`. Find `src` and `dest` in the module help and identify which side owns each path. Record the Ansible version printed by the final command. This is the Ansible binary inside the selected container. `ansible-navigator --version` identifies the launcher on the client.

```text
> ansible-navigator --version
The installed Navigator version. Compare with the version pinned for this
unit.
```

The two version numbers answer different questions.

**Diagnose a failure.** If the image cannot be found, compare the exact configured name with `podman images` as learner.

```text
> podman images
Locally available images with repository, tag and image ID.
```

If the graph is empty, inspect the current directory and inventory. Neither failure has yet tested the server's SSH service.

[Navigator settings](https://docs.ansible.com/projects/navigator/settings/) · [Community execution environments](https://docs.ansible.com/projects/ansible/latest/getting_started_ee/run_community_ee_image.html)

lessons.title: Prove a fresh checkout can deploy the release
topics: Prove a fresh checkout can deploy the release
lessons.body:
**Release request.** Deliver one line, `release=alpha`, followed by a newline to `/home/learner/erudior-release.txt` on the operations server. The file should belong to learner, use mode 0644 and remain unchanged on a second run. Use an unused path on this lab server. The existing shift and handoff files belong to the earlier work orders.

## Put the entire recipe under version control

On the client in `~/rhce-release`, run the following command and save **release.yml** below.

```text
> printf 'release=alpha\n' > files/release.txt
No output. The tracked source file contains release=alpha followed by a
newline.
```

The learner owns its home, so the task can create the new file using the ordinary SSH account. A sudo prompt here would be a reason to inspect which configuration is active.

```yaml
---
- name: Publish the operator release note
  hosts: ops
  gather_facts: false
  tasks:
    - name: Deliver the selected release
      ansible.builtin.copy:
        src: files/release.txt
        dest: /home/learner/erudior-release.txt
        mode: '0644'
```

```text
> git add ansible-navigator.yml release.yml files/release.txt
No output. Git staged the current versions of the named files for the next
commit.

> git diff --cached
A diff of the staged changes that the next commit would record. Press q if a
pager opens.
```

```text
> git commit -m 'Deploy the alpha release note with the pinned lab toolchain'
A commit summary with branch, abbreviated commit ID and message. Save the ID
for comparison.

> git push
Git reports the updated remote branch or that it is already up to date.
Compare the destination branch with the intended one.
```

```text
> git clone learner@192.168.77.10:repos/handoff.git ~/rhce-rehearsal
Cloning progress, then a checkout at ~/rhce-rehearsal.

> cd ~/rhce-rehearsal
No output. The shell now works in the named project directory.
```

```text
> git rev-parse HEAD
The full commit ID currently checked out in this directory.

> git ls-files
Tracked filenames, including release.yml, files/release.txt and the
inventory and trust files.
```

Compare the commit ID with the first checkout. Look for both the playbook and its input file in the tracked list. Use this new checkout for the remaining runs. If another operator only receives Git history, this is what they get.

## Preview, apply, verify

Ensure your lab agent is loaded with `ssh-add -l` and the Navigator virtual environment is active on the **client**.

```text
> ssh-add -l
The fingerprint of the loaded lab identity. An empty agent reports that it
has no identities.
```

Check the private server path is initially unused at the **server console**. Then run from the new clone.

```text
> ansible-navigator run release.yml --syntax-check
A successful syntax check identifies the playbook. A syntax error instead
identifies the affected file and location.

> ansible-navigator run release.yml --check --diff
A predicted diff from the current release note to the tracked candidate. The
target file is untouched by this copy preview.
```

Expect one predicted change for `node1`. At the server console run the following command.

```text
> test ! -e ~/erudior-release.txt && echo still-absent
still-absent when the file was absent before preview.
```

Continue on the client.

```text
> ansible-navigator run release.yml
An absent or different release note gives changed=1. A second successful run
on the same commit gives changed=0.

> ansible-navigator run release.yml
An absent or different release note gives changed=1. A second successful run
on the same commit gives changed=0.
```

Expect one change on the first live run and zero on the second, with zero failed or unreachable hosts. At the **server console** run the following checks as learner. `cmp` checks the trailing newline as well as the visible text.

```text
> printf 'release=alpha\n' | cmp - ~/erudior-release.txt && echo alpha-ok
alpha-ok

> stat -c '%U:%G %a' ~/erudior-release.txt
learner:learner 644
```

Expect `alpha-ok` and, on the course VMs, `learner:learner 644`. A correct file in the client checkout proves only that you prepared the source. The remote comparison proves delivery. If an SSH host key fails inside the container, check its working directory, `ssh/known_hosts` and the trusted fingerprint. If public-key login fails, inspect the loaded agent key.

**Try it.** From the rehearsal clone run the following command after the play.

```text
> git status --short
No output for a clean checkout. Modified or untracked files appear as rows.
```

Explain why a working tree can be clean even though the server changed.

[Navigator, SSH agents and execution environments](https://docs.ansible.com/projects/navigator/faq/)

lessons.title: Author and run an inspection play in VS Code
topics: Author and run an inspection play in VS Code
lessons.body:
A release reviewer wants a play that can inspect the server without changing it. You will write that play inside a [[Development container]], run it from the editor terminal, then send the change to a review branch. The project directory is shared with the client. The editor's tools come from the dev image. The operator's file still lives on the server.

## Open the workbench

Use desktop VS Code on the AlmaLinux client, or use VS Code's **Remote - SSH** on your workstation to open `~/rhce-release` on the client. Install Microsoft's **Dev Containers** extension for VS Code. In the settings for the window connected to the client, set **Dev › Containers: Docker Path** (`dev.containers.dockerPath`) to `podman`. The extension and its VS Code Server components may require an initial download. The browser course reader can stay open alongside the editor.

In a regular **client terminal** pull the x86-64 development image and give that verified copy the name used by the workspace. This image includes the editor tools and Git. The smaller image from the last lesson remains the release runtime.

```text
> dev_image=ghcr.io/ansible/community-ansible-dev-tools@sha256:e416af142ddf3af7f88bca5867077a5cf87e09c551e62ef1d651658a2ae9f952
No output. dev_image holds the full digest-pinned image reference.

> podman pull "$dev_image"
Image layer download or reuse messages followed by the image identifier in
this user's store.
```

```text
> podman tag "$dev_image" localhost/erudior/rhce-dev:unit2
No output. The local image also has the tag
localhost/erudior/rhce-dev:unit2.

> cd ~/rhce-release
No output. The shell now works in the named project directory.
```

```text
> mkdir -p .devcontainer
No output. The .devcontainer directory exists in this project.
```

Create **.devcontainer/devcontainer.json** in that project. The client paths are resolved on the machine running Podman. The two shared mounts are the project and the dedicated lab agent socket. A shared SELinux label allows these two lab directories to be used by the workbench. Keep the mounts scoped to those directories. The `root` username in this rootless container maps to the unprivileged learner launching Podman.

```json
{
  "name": "Erudior RHCE workbench",
  "image": "localhost/erudior/rhce-dev:unit2",
  "workspaceFolder": "/workspaces/rhce",
  "workspaceMount": "type=bind,source=${localWorkspaceFolder},target=/workspaces/rhce,relabel=shared",
  "mounts": [
    "type=bind,source=${localEnv:HOME}/.local/share/erudior-rhce-agent,target=/run/course-agent,relabel=shared"
  ],
  "containerEnv": { "SSH_AUTH_SOCK": "/run/course-agent/socket" },
  "remoteEnv": { "SSH_AUTH_SOCK": "/run/course-agent/socket" },
  "remoteUser": "root",
  "overrideCommand": true
}
```

Open the command palette and select **Dev Containers: Reopen in Container**. The lower-left remote indicator should identify **Erudior RHCE workbench**. Open a **new integrated terminal**. Confirm that `pwd` is `/workspaces/rhce`, `git --version` and `ansible --version` work, and `ssh-add -l` shows the same lab key fingerprint as on the client. 

```text
> pwd
/workspaces/rhce inside the development container.

> git --version
git version followed by the installed version.
```

```text
> ansible --version
The ansible-core version, active configuration file and Python interpreter
path.

> ssh-add -l
The fingerprint of the loaded lab identity. An empty agent reports that it
has no identities.
```

**Headless rehearsal.** With Microsoft's Dev Containers CLI installed, you can exercise the same workspace definition from a terminal on the client. From `~/rhce-release`, run the two commands below, then use the resulting shell for the inspection play. In the exam preparation sequence, also practice opening the project, creating a file and using Source Control in the editor.

`devcontainer` starts a development container from the project's configuration or executes a command inside it.

```text
> devcontainer up --docker-path podman --workspace-folder "$PWD"
The CLI returns a successful outcome and identifies the running development
container.

> devcontainer exec --docker-path podman --workspace-folder "$PWD" bash
An interactive Bash prompt opens inside the development container.
```

From the editor terminal or the headless shell, check that the agent has the lab key. Configure Git to use the project's trusted host key from this checkout.

```text
> cd /workspaces/rhce
No output. The shell now works in the named project directory.

> export SSH_AUTH_SOCK=/run/course-agent/socket
No output. SSH clients launched from this shell now use the specified
socket.
```

```text
> git config core.sshCommand 'ssh -o StrictHostKeyChecking=yes -o UserKnownHostsFile=./ssh/known_hosts'
No output. The setting is saved in this repository's local Git
configuration.

> git ls-remote origin refs/heads/main
A full commit ID followed by the requested remote branch ref.
```

```text
> git switch -c review/beta
Git confirms it switched to the new review/beta branch.
```

If the socket is missing, verify the agent directory and socket on the client. If `ssh-add -l` reports no identities, reload the lab key on the client. The agent can sign a login while the key is loaded. Close only this lab agent when you finish the practical.

## Create, run and push from VS Code

Use **New File** in the Explorer to create **inspect.yml** in the repository root. Save it. The first task collects information from `node1` and assigns it the name `note`. The second displays one field from that result. You will use registered results in more depth in the next unit.

```yaml
---
- name: Read the delivered release note
  hosts: ops
  gather_facts: false
  tasks:
    - name: Inspect the release path on the server
      ansible.builtin.stat:
        path: /home/learner/erudior-release.txt
      register: note

    - name: Report whether the release was delivered
      ansible.builtin.debug:
        var: note.stat.exists
```

```text
> ansible-playbook -i inventory.ini inspect.yml
The stat result reports whether the note exists on node1. Expect true after
the alpha release and changed=0.

> git add .devcontainer/devcontainer.json inspect.yml
No output. Git staged the current versions of the named files for the next
commit.
```

```text
> git diff --cached --stat
A short summary of staged changes, including the affected filenames.

> git commit -m 'Add the editor workbench and inspect the deployed note'
A commit summary with branch, abbreviated commit ID and message. Save the ID
for comparison.
```

```text
> git push -u origin review/beta
Git reports the updated remote branch or that it is already up to date.
Compare the destination branch with the intended one.
```

Expect `note.stat.exists` to be true and `changed=0` for `node1` after the alpha deployment. A successful play run against localhost would answer a different question. Check the recap for the inventory alias. In VS Code's **Source Control**, verify the current branch and that no source changes are pending. On the client, `git ls-remote origin refs/heads/main refs/heads/review/beta` should show different commits.

```text
> git ls-remote origin refs/heads/main refs/heads/review/beta
Two remote refs, each with its commit ID, after the review branch has been
pushed.
```

Main still identifies the alpha release.

[VS Code development containers](https://code.visualstudio.com/docs/devcontainers/containers) · [Podman settings for VS Code](https://code.visualstudio.com/remote/advancedcontainers/docker-options) · [Dev Containers CLI](https://containers.dev/supporting#devcontainer-cli) · [Red Hat Ansible extension and development containers](https://marketplace.visualstudio.com/items?itemName=redhat.ansible)

## Change Navigator settings inside VS Code

In the connected VS Code Explorer open **ansible-navigator.yml** from the project root. In a temporary copy named **navigator-inspect.yml**, keep the existing top-level ansible-navigator mapping and set its mode to stdout and execution-environment.enabled to false. Save it. This one inspection uses the editor workbench's own Ansible installation. Keep the regular release settings available for execution-environment runs.

In the editor terminal, from the project root, run `ANSIBLE_NAVIGATOR_CONFIG="$PWD/navigator-inspect.yml" ansible-navigator settings --effective -m stdout`. Verify the effective execution-environment setting is disabled. Then use the same environment prefix with `ansible-navigator run inspect.yml -m stdout`. Inspect the node1 result and recap. Compare with the regular client-side Navigator run that uses the staged image. Remove only the temporary settings file after recording your evidence.

lessons.title: Independent practical: promote a tested revision
topics: Independent practical: promote a tested revision
lessons.body:
**Work order.** The operations team has approved a preview of the beta note. Deliver exactly `release=beta` plus a newline to the same server path with mode 0644. Demonstrate the change from a second checkout, show that preview leaves alpha in place, and advance main only after the remote checks pass. Use your private lab Git server.

Start with the editor checkout on `review/beta`, the rehearsal checkout on `main`, and the alpha note on `node1`. If alpha is absent, run the alpha play from the previous lesson first. Use the Navigator virtual environment and loaded lab agent for the execution-environment run. Keep the original evening and morning configurations intact.

| Evidence | Points | What to record |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Reviewable change | 2 | Edit only the release source for this ticket in the editor, inspect the staged patch, commit and push to the review branch. Show that main still points at its previous commit. |
| Independent checkout | 2 | Fetch in the second checkout and select the exact review commit. Show matching local and remote commit IDs and the `ops` target from the containerized inventory. |
| Preview | 2 | Show the predicted alpha-to-beta diff. Read the remote file separately and prove it is still alpha after the preview. |
| Delivery and repeatability | 2 | Apply once, verify exact beta bytes, owner, group and mode on the server, then show zero changes and zero failed or unreachable hosts on the repeat. Confirm both earlier configuration files still have their required contents. |
| Promotion | 2 | Fast-forward main to the tested commit, push it and compare the final remote main ID with the tested ID. Explain what you would investigate if the fast-forward were refused. |

Use `git status --short --branch` at each checkout before switching branches.

```text
> git status --short --branch
A line beginning with ## names the current branch and upstream. Additional
lines indicate local changes.
```

Compare exact bytes with `printf 'release=beta\n' | cmp - ~/erudior-release.txt` on the server.

```text
> printf 'release=beta\n' | cmp - ~/erudior-release.txt
No output and status 0 for an exact beta line, including its newline.
```

Check permission metadata with `stat`. If either the target or the diff differs from the request, correct the source on the review branch and repeat your preview before applying.

Award two points per row when you can show all its evidence. Erudior scores the written quiz separately. The **Beta promotion answer and scoring guide** gives a reference transcript. After recording the results, close the development container. Stop your dedicated agent from the shell where you started it using `ssh-agent -k` once you have finished all Git and SSH work for this unit.

```text
> ssh-agent -k
The agent reports that its process was killed. Future SSH commands need a
new or different agent.
```

```assignment
lab: promote-beta-evidence
```

lessons.title: Give two managed hosts different policies
topics: Give two managed hosts different policies
lessons.body:
The operations team runs two desks. Dispatch works days and takes pager duty. Archive works nights and has no pager duty. The same playbook needs to configure both. Put the differences in inventory data so that a shift change can be reviewed as a small policy edit.

## Give the existing pair two inventory identities

Keep the two AlmaLinux 10 VMs from the release lab. In this unit the client has two jobs: it launches Ansible and also provides the second SSH target. Both targets use SSH. This matters from an execution environment, where a local connection would run tasks inside the container.

| Inventory alias | Guest | Example private address | Starting policy |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| dispatch | server | 192.168.77.10 | day, on call |
| archive | client | 192.168.77.20 | night, off call |

On the **client**, as learner, start an agent in the terminal you will use for the exercises. Load your existing lab key. The first command creates a new temporary agent for this unit.

```text
> eval "$(ssh-agent -s)"
Agent pid followed by a number. This shell now knows the agent's socket.

> ssh-add -t 4h ~/.ssh/erudior_rhce
Identity added followed by the lab key path. A protected key prompts for its
passphrase.
```

```text
> sudo dnf install openssh-server python3
DNF lists the named packages in a transaction or reports that they are
already installed. Check for completion.

> sudo systemctl enable --now sshd
The service starts and is enabled at boot. systemd can print the new
enablement link.
```

```text
> install -d -m 700 ~/.ssh
No output. ~/.ssh exists with permissions restricted to the account.

> touch ~/.ssh/authorized_keys
No output. The authorized_keys file exists and existing entries are
preserved.
```

```text
> chmod 600 ~/.ssh/authorized_keys
No output. Only the account owner can read or write authorized_keys.

> grep -qxF -f ~/.ssh/erudior_rhce.pub ~/.ssh/authorized_keys || cat ~/.ssh/erudior_rhce.pub >> ~/.ssh/authorized_keys
No output. The lab public key appears as a complete line and an existing
identical entry is left alone.
```

```text
> restorecon -RF ~/.ssh
No routine output. The SSH files have their default policy labels.
```

The client already holds the private key that lets it manage the server. Adding its **public** key to its own learner account lets Ansible authenticate to the client as a managed node too. Use a fresh directory so the release project retains its own inventory.

```text
> mkdir -p ~/rhce-desks/{ssh,group_vars,host_vars,files}
No output. The project directories named on the command line now exist.

> cd ~/rhce-desks
No output. The shell now works in the named project directory.
```

```text
> cp ~/rhce-release/{ansible.cfg,ansible-navigator.yml} .
No output. The named project files have been copied into the destination
directory.

> cp ~/rhce-release/ssh/known_hosts ssh/known_hosts
No output. The named project files have been copied into the destination
directory.
```

```text
> awk '{print "192.168.77.20", $1, $2}' /etc/ssh/ssh_host_ed25519_key.pub >> ssh/known_hosts
No output. The public host key for 192.168.77.20 is appended to the
project's trust file.

> ssh-keygen -lf ssh/known_hosts
A SHA256 fingerprint for each public host key in the file. Compare with the
trusted guest consoles.
```

The first trust entry came from the previous unit. Compare the new fingerprint with `sudo ssh-keygen -lf /etc/ssh/ssh_host_ed25519_key.pub` at the client console.

```text
> sudo ssh-keygen -lf /etc/ssh/ssh_host_ed25519_key.pub
A SHA256 fingerprint and algorithm. Compare the full fingerprint through the
trusted console.
```

Substitute your actual private addresses throughout the unit if they differ. Check both SSH paths from the project root.

```text
> ssh -o BatchMode=yes -o StrictHostKeyChecking=yes -o UserKnownHostsFile=./ssh/known_hosts learner@192.168.77.10 hostname
server

> ssh -o BatchMode=yes -o StrictHostKeyChecking=yes -o UserKnownHostsFile=./ssh/known_hosts learner@192.168.77.20 hostname
client
```

## Write the policy

Save **inventory.ini**. Under **group_vars**, a file named after the group supplies shared settings. Under **host_vars**, the filename follows the inventory alias, even when the guest's actual hostname differs.

```ini
[desks]
dispatch ansible_host=192.168.77.10
archive ansible_host=192.168.77.20
```

**group_vars/desks.yml**

```yaml
---
desk_shift: day
desk_pager: false
desk_channels:
  - name: board
    mode: '0644'
  - name: roster
    mode: '0640'
```

**host_vars/dispatch.yml**

```yaml
---
desk_pager: true
```

**host_vars/archive.yml**

```yaml
---
desk_shift: night
```

`desk_channels` is a list. Each entry is a dictionary with a name and a quoted Unix mode. `desk_pager` is a YAML boolean. The unquoted `false` means off duty. The quoted string `'false'` is text, and later the play will explicitly reject it.

## Predict before connecting

```text
> ansible-inventory --graph
The graph places dispatch and archive under @desks.

> ansible-inventory --host dispatch
JSON showing the variables resolved for this inventory alias. Compare
desk_shift and desk_pager with the host's policy.
```

```text
> ansible-inventory --host archive
JSON showing the variables resolved for this inventory alias. Compare
desk_shift and desk_pager with the host's policy.

> ansible desks --list-hosts
Exactly two aliases, dispatch and archive.
```

Find both aliases under the desks group. Dispatch inherits the day shift and overrides pager duty to true. Archive inherits false for its pager and overrides the shift to night. Both inherit the channel list. These inventory commands can succeed while a guest is powered off because they read controller-side data.

**Try it.** Predict the result of `ansible-inventory --host archive -e '{"desk_shift":"day"}'`, then compare the output with a second invocation without `-e`.

```text
> ansible-inventory --host archive -e '{"desk_shift":"day"}'
The displayed desk_shift is day for this invocation. The host_vars file is
unchanged.
```

For this example the extra variable wins for that invocation. The override changes neither the YAML on disk nor the server.

[Ansible inventory and host/group variables](https://docs.ansible.com/projects/ansible/latest/inventory_guide/intro_inventory.html) · [Using variables](https://docs.ansible.com/projects/ansible/latest/playbook_guide/playbooks_variables.html)

lessons.title: Separate requested policy from observed state
topics: Separate requested policy from observed state
lessons.body:
An inventory can say a machine is on pager duty even when its notice is missing. You need three kinds of evidence to explain that discrepancy: the requested policy, the operating system Ansible reached, and the current file state. Each comes from a different source.

| Question | Value to inspect | Origin |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Which alias did the play select? | inventory_hostname | Controller inventory |
| Which machine answered? | ansible_facts['hostname'] | Facts gathered from that guest |
| Is pager duty requested? | desk_pager | Resolved inventory policy |
| Does the notice exist now? | prior_pager.stat.exists | Result of a stat task on that guest |

## Stop early on the wrong input

In `~/rhce-desks`, create **validate.yml**. It is a task list that another play imports. The first two assertions check the connected operating system. The last two check a policy value and its type.

```yaml
---
- name: Verify the platform and desk policy before writing
  ansible.builtin.assert:
    that:
      - ansible_facts['distribution'] == 'AlmaLinux'
      - ansible_facts['distribution_major_version'] == '10'
      - desk_shift in ['day', 'night']
      - desk_pager is boolean
    fail_msg: "Check the guest OS, desk_shift and the YAML type of desk_pager."
```

Create **observe.yml**. A [[Gathered fact]] describes a managed host. The minimum fact set supplies the hostname and distribution used here. With `gather_subset: ['!all']`, Ansible omits the full collection and still gathers its minimum subset. A [[Registered result]] captures one task's return data for each host for this run. The nested field `stat.exists` comes from the stat module.

```yaml
---
- name: Read each desk's identity and prior pager state
  hosts: desks
  gather_facts: true
  gather_subset: ['!all']
  any_errors_fatal: true
  pre_tasks:
    - ansible.builtin.import_tasks: validate.yml
  tasks:
    - name: Inspect the optional pager file
      ansible.builtin.stat:
        path: /home/learner/rhce-pager.txt
        get_checksum: false
      register: prior_pager

    - name: Compare the requested shift with this guest's observations
      ansible.builtin.debug:
        msg: >-
          {{ inventory_hostname }} reaches {{ ansible_facts['hostname'] }}
          on {{ ansible_facts['distribution'] }} {{ ansible_facts['distribution_major_version'] }}.
          Shift={{ desk_shift }}. Pager requested={{ desk_pager }}.
          Pager present={{ prior_pager.stat.exists }}.
```

```text
> ansible-playbook --syntax-check observe.yml
A successful syntax check identifies the playbook. A syntax error instead
identifies the affected file and location.

> ansible-playbook observe.yml
Each desk reports its alias, OS hostname, shift and observed pager state.
The inspection has changed=0.
```

On the course pair, expect dispatch to reach **server** and archive to reach **client**. If you chose other guest hostnames, compare with those names. Both should report AlmaLinux 10. On a fresh pair both notices are absent even though dispatch requests one. The recap should show zero changes. If these lab paths already contain anything from another project, use fresh practice guests for this exercise.

**Break one assumption.** Run the following command.

```text
> ansible-playbook observe.yml --limit archive -e '{"desk_pager":"false"}'
The validation assertion fails on archive because the supplied pager value
is a string.
```

Predict which test fails. Then replace the quoted string with the JSON boolean using `-e '{"desk_pager":false}'` and rerun. The text and the boolean can look alike in a message. The assertion distinguishes their types before later tasks depend on them.

**Explain your result.** What would you inspect if inventory displayed the expected alias but the gathered hostname belonged to a different VM? Start with that alias's connection address and host identity. Editing the requested shift would leave the connection unchanged.

[Ansible facts and magic variables](https://docs.ansible.com/projects/ansible/latest/playbook_guide/playbooks_vars_facts.html) · [The stat module](https://docs.ansible.com/projects/ansible/latest/collections/ansible/builtin/stat_module.html)

lessons.title: Deploy and repair a list of files
topics: Deploy and repair a list of files
lessons.body:
Each desk needs a public board and a roster with restricted access. Both need the right shift printed in the file. Writing separate tasks for day board, night board, day roster and night roster makes it easy to fix one and forget another. Instead, each loop iteration can take the channel name and mode from inventory and select a source file using the host's effective shift.

## Prepare the source files

Use the same project root. The loop below creates four small controller files. For example, `files/board-night.txt` contains `board=night` followed by one newline.

```text
> for shift in day night; do
>   for channel in board roster; do
>     printf '%s=%s\n' "$channel" "$shift" > "files/$channel-$shift.txt"
>   done
> done
No output after the final done. There are four source files, one for each
channel and shift combination.

> printf '[]\n' > pager.yml
No output. pager.yml contains an empty YAML list.
```

The empty YAML list in **pager.yml** reserves a place for the next lesson. Ansible may warn that the file has no tasks to include. The channel tasks still run. Create **channels.yml**. Read the source and destination expressions with dispatch's variables substituted, then repeat for archive. For either desk, the roster destination is the same absolute path **on its own guest**. Mode 0640 gives the owner read and write access and the group read access. Mode 0644 also lets other users read the board. On these clean lab guests the ordinary learner account starts with primary group learner and creates the files in its own home. The practical checks those ownership assumptions independently.

```yaml
---
- name: Install the channels for the selected shift
  ansible.builtin.copy:
    src: "files/{{ channel.name }}-{{ desk_shift }}.txt"
    dest: "/home/learner/rhce-{{ channel.name }}.txt"
    mode: "{{ channel.mode }}"
  loop: "{{ desk_channels }}"
  loop_control:
    loop_var: channel
    label: "{{ channel.name }}"
  register: channel_run

- name: List the channels that differ on this host
  ansible.builtin.debug:
    msg: "{{ channel_run.results | selectattr('changed') | map(attribute='channel.name') | list }}"
```

The loop variable is named `channel`. Each element supplies two related fields. Registering the loop returns a list under `channel_run.results`. Each result includes that iteration's `channel` and whether it changed. The final task shows only the names of changed channels on the current host. In check mode those names describe predicted changes.

Create **desks.yml**, the entry point. It imports the policy checks before either task list runs. Under the default linear strategy, `any_errors_fatal: true` stops this play across the selected hosts if a host fails the preflight.

```yaml
---
- name: Maintain the operations desks
  hosts: desks
  gather_facts: true
  gather_subset: ['!all']
  any_errors_fatal: true
  pre_tasks:
    - ansible.builtin.import_tasks: validate.yml
  tasks:
    - ansible.builtin.import_tasks: channels.yml
    - ansible.builtin.import_tasks: pager.yml
```

## Read the evidence at two levels

```text
> ansible-playbook desks.yml --check --diff
A per-host diff predicting the required changes. The two guests retain their
pre-preview file contents.

> ansible-playbook desks.yml
The first run repairs differences on the targeted desks. An immediate repeat
should report changed=0 and failed=0 for both.
```

```text
> ansible-playbook desks.yml
The first run repairs differences on the targeted desks. An immediate repeat
should report changed=0 and failed=0 for both.
```

Before the first live run, check each guest console to verify the two destination files are still absent after preview. On a clean pair the first live run should name **board** and **roster** for each host. The recap reports one changed task per host because both file writes came from one looped task. The next run should show an empty list for each host and zero changes. On each guest run `cat ~/rhce-{board,roster}.txt` and `stat -c '%n %U:%G %a' ~/rhce-{board,roster}.txt`.

```text
> cat ~/rhce-{board,roster}.txt
Two lines, board and roster, each naming the shift assigned to this host.

> stat -c '%n %U:%G %a' ~/rhce-{board,roster}.txt
A row for each file. On the configured learner home expect board mode 644
and roster mode 640.
```

Compare the bytes and modes with the inventory.

**Repair drill.** At the **server** console run the following command.

```text
> chmod 0600 ~/rhce-roster.txt
No output. The roster mode is now 600. The next apply should repair just
that item's mode.
```

Predict the host, iteration and attribute that the next live run will change. Run the following command on the client.

```text
> ansible-playbook desks.yml
The first run repairs differences on the targeted desks. An immediate repeat
should report changed=0 and failed=0 for both.
```

Only dispatch's roster should appear in the changed-channel list. Its final mode should be 640. Archive should report no changes. This is a case where looking only at file contents would miss the fault.

[Ansible loops and registered results](https://docs.ansible.com/projects/ansible/latest/playbook_guide/playbooks_loops.html)

```example fade=1
title: Read a loop report at the right level
problem: Dispatch reports board changed and roster changed in the same copy loop. Archive reports neither item changed. What goes into each host's recap?
step: Count changed iterations on dispatch. There are two.
step: Find the task that owns the iterations. Both belong to the same copy task.
step: Count changed tasks separately on each host. Dispatch has one and archive has zero.
answer: Dispatch changed=1, archive changed=0. The per-item results tell you which files were affected.
```

lessons.title: Make both branches reach the requested state
topics: Make both branches reach the requested state
lessons.body:
Archive came off pager duty last week. Its operator can still see an old pager notice. The previous play only installed a file when a desk was on call. Once the condition became false, it skipped that task and left the old file in place. Your job is to make both possible policies converge on the correct state.

| Requested duty | Current notice | Required outcome |
| --- | --- | --- |
| On | Missing | Install the notice |
| On | Present | Ensure exact contents and mode 0600 |
| Off | Present as a regular file | Remove the stale notice |
| Off | Absent | Leave the path absent |

## Use evidence and policy in one decision

At the **client** terminal, from `~/rhce-desks`, run the following command.

```text
> printf 'duty=on-call\n' > files/pager.txt
No output. files/pager.txt contains duty=on-call.
```

Replace the empty **pager.yml** with this task list.

```yaml
---
- name: Observe the current notice without following links
  ansible.builtin.stat:
    path: /home/learner/rhce-pager.txt
    follow: false
    get_checksum: false
  register: pager_before

- name: Verify that an existing notice is a regular file
  ansible.builtin.assert:
    that:
      - not pager_before.stat.exists or (pager_before.stat.isreg | default(false))
    fail_msg: "Inspect the unexpected object at the pager path."

- name: Install the pager notice at an on-call desk
  ansible.builtin.copy:
    src: files/pager.txt
    dest: /home/learner/rhce-pager.txt
    mode: '0600'
  when: desk_pager

- name: Remove a stale notice at an off-call desk
  ansible.builtin.file:
    path: /home/learner/rhce-pager.txt
    state: absent
  when:
    - not desk_pager
    - pager_before.stat.exists
```

A [[Conditional]] is evaluated per host. In `when`, write an expression such as `desk_pager` directly. A list of conditions requires every listed expression to be true. The removal task therefore runs only on an off-call host where stat observed a notice. The file-type assertion makes a directory or symbolic link at this lab path an issue for the operator to inspect. The task reads an absent path safely because the first part of its assertion is already true.

## Reproduce the stale notice

Use fresh, course-owned paths. At the **client VM console**, acting as the archive target, create the deliberately stale file with `printf 'duty=retired\n' > ~/rhce-pager.txt`.

```text
> printf 'duty=retired\n' > ~/rhce-pager.txt
No output. The stale local pager file contains duty=retired.
```

The dispatch server should still have no pager file from the channels-only lesson. Back at the **client project terminal**, predict which conditional task will run on each desk, then apply the change.

```text
> ansible-playbook observe.yml
Each desk reports its alias, OS hostname, shift and observed pager state.
The inspection has changed=0.

> ansible-playbook desks.yml
The first run repairs differences on the targeted desks. An immediate repeat
should report changed=0 and failed=0 for both.
```

```text
> ansible-playbook desks.yml
The first run repairs differences on the targeted desks. An immediate repeat
should report changed=0 and failed=0 for both.
```

After the first live run, check the server console for the exact `duty=on-call` line and mode 600. At the client console check `test ! -e ~/rhce-pager.txt && echo pager-absent`.

```text
> test ! -e ~/rhce-pager.txt && echo pager-absent
pager-absent on the off-call desk after reconciliation.
```

The second run should report zero changes on both machines. A “skipping” line on one host tells you that particular task's condition was false. Read the other branch and verify the end state.

**Try the failure on paper.** Suppose archive is off call and someone replaces the absent file with a directory of the same name. Predict which task stops the play. Would the pager file-type guard undo a channel update that ran earlier in the play? Ansible does not automatically roll back earlier tasks. The policy preflight runs before channel updates, whereas the file-type guard runs inside the pager task list.

[Ansible conditionals](https://docs.ansible.com/projects/ansible/latest/playbook_guide/playbooks_conditionals.html) · [File state options](https://docs.ansible.com/projects/ansible/latest/collections/ansible/builtin/file_module.html)

lessons.title: Independent practical: rotate duty across two desks
topics: Independent practical: rotate duty across two desks
lessons.body:
**Work order.** Starting from dispatch on day shift with pager duty and archive on night shift without it, swap the shifts and transfer pager duty to archive. Bring the incoming desk on call and verify it before taking dispatch off call. Use the same playbook and channel list. The requested deployment change belongs entirely in the two host variable files.

| Target | Final board and roster | Final pager |
| --- | --- | --- |
| dispatch (.10 server) | board=night and roster=night | Absent |
| archive (.20 client) | board=day and roster=day | duty=on-call, mode 0600 |

Each text file ends with one newline. Both boards are mode 0644 and both rosters are 0640. All managed files belong to learner:learner. Keep the beta release note from the previous unit intact. Practice in the two course VMs.

## Run the handoff as the change owner

1. **Baseline, 2 points.** Record each resolved host policy, the two actual guest hostnames, and independent checks of the starting board, roster and pager. Explain why the inventory alias and real hostname can differ. 2. **Reject a bad policy, 2 points.** Prepare the proposed changes but give archive the quoted text `'true'` for pager duty. Run the entry play against both desks. Show that validation failed before any file changed on either desk. Check both original states again. 3. **Rehearse on one desk, 2 points.** Correct the YAML type. Preview the change for archive with `--limit archive --check --diff`. Inspect both machines before applying. Apply with the same limit. Prove that archive is ready for pager duty while dispatch still has its original day/on configuration. 4. **Finish the rotation, 2 points.** Run the corrected play on both desks with `ansible-navigator` in the execution environment from the last unit. Prove the requested final contents, ownership and modes independently on both machines, including the absent pager on dispatch. 5. **Prove repeatability, 2 points.** Repeat the play and show zero changed, failed or unreachable tasks on both hosts. On the server compare `~/erudior-release.txt` with the exact beta line from the preceding unit. Explain why the loop recap can report one changed task even when both the board and roster differed.

The **Desk state checker** reference supplies a read-only script. Save it as **check-desk.sh** in the client project. The checker reads the target you connect to.
