Give it the expected shift and pager state from the work order, independently of the inventory data you are testing. Use the **Duty rotation answer and scoring guide** after your own attempt.

For each row, award its points when all requested evidence is present. Erudior scores the written knowledge check separately. If a task recaps as successful but your checker fails, keep the observed result with your evidence and correct the policy or task before claiming that row.

```assignment
lab: rotate-pager-duty-evidence
```

lessons.title: Define trusted software sources for dispatch
topics: Define trusted software sources for dispatch
lessons.body:
Dispatch needs a local HTTP status page. You have an AlmaLinux 10 server and a working SSH identity from the desk rotation. The first change request authorizes two software sources. It does not yet authorize installing or starting Apache. Your evidence for this step is a repository definition on the server.

## Establish the scope

Use the **client** as the Ansible control node and the **server** as the web target. The checker will connect to the server’s own loopback interface. Archive keeps its desk assignment from lesson 15. This lab uses a dedicated stock server with port 80 free, no installed httpd, and no pre-existing erudior-web repo file. Take a VM snapshot if you want to rehearse the first install twice.

At the **server console**, inspect the image, the signing key that came with it, and the starting state. An empty listener listing and “package httpd is not installed” are the expected initial observations.

```text
> cat /etc/almalinux-release
An AlmaLinux release line with major version 10.

> uname -m
x86_64 on the supplied image.
```

```text
> rpm -qf /etc/pki/rpm-gpg/RPM-GPG-KEY-AlmaLinux-10
The installed RPM that owns the AlmaLinux signing key.

> rpm -q httpd
The installed httpd version, or package httpd is not installed on the fresh
baseline.
```

```text
> ss -H -ltn 'sport = :80'
No rows when port 80 has no listener. After the loopback-only service
starts, expect its loopback address on port 80.

> test ! -e /etc/yum.repos.d/erudior-web.repo && echo course-repos-absent
course-repos-absent on the fresh baseline.
```

At the **client** make a new project. Keep the private key on the control node. Start the lab agent in this shell if it no longer holds the key.

```text
> mkdir -p ~/rhce-web/{ssh,group_vars}
No output. The project directories named on the command line now exist.

> cd ~/rhce-web
No output. The shell now works in the named project directory.
```

```text
> cp ~/rhce-desks/{ansible.cfg,ansible-navigator.yml} .
No output. The named project files have been copied into the destination
directory.

> cp ~/rhce-desks/ssh/known_hosts ssh/
No output. The named project files have been copied into the destination
directory.
```

```text
> eval "$(ssh-agent -s)"
Agent pid followed by a number. This shell now knows the agent's socket.

> ssh-add -t 4h ~/.ssh/erudior_rhce
Identity added followed by the lab key path. A protected key prompts for its
passphrase.
```

Create **inventory.ini** and **group_vars/web.yml** from these two blocks. Keep your verified server address if it differs. The project uses the lab learner account with sudo on dispatch. If your practice sudo policy requires a password, add `-K` to the Ansible playbook invocation and enter it at the prompt.

```ini
[web]
dispatch ansible_host=192.168.77.10
```

```yaml
---
mirror_root: https://repo.almalinux.org/almalinux
release_track: blue
release_teams:
  blue: operations
  green: support
```

## Declare where software comes from

A [[Package repository]] publishes a catalog and the RPMs named in it. DNF reads the catalog to resolve a package request and its dependencies. This machine needs BaseOS and AppStream. The two course IDs go in one file under **/etc/yum.repos.d** so you can inspect what the play owns. The stock AlmaLinux entries remain available for other work. A disabled-by-default course entry can still be selected explicitly for one transaction.

For offline practice with the AlmaLinux 10.3 kit, use `baseurl: "file:///mnt/erudior-dvd/{{ item }}/"` in the repository task below. The attached DVD supplies both package trees on the server. Keep the repository names and signature checks. For a networked attempt, use the mirror URL shown.

Save **supply.yml** on the client. The loop creates the two entries. Jinja supplies the mirror and repository names on the controller. The literal `$basearch` is for DNF to expand on the target. `gpgcheck: true` requires package signature checking against a trusted key. The HTTPS mirror also authenticates the network connection. A classroom mirror may supply the same signed RPMs and directory layout. In that case set `mirror_root` to its lab-provided root and keep signature checks enabled.

```yaml
---
- name: Define the web lab software sources
  hosts: web
  gather_facts: false
  become: true
  tasks:
    - name: Register the official AlmaLinux repositories for this exercise
      ansible.builtin.yum_repository:
        file: erudior-web
        name: "erudior-{{ item | lower }}"
        description: "Erudior AlmaLinux 10 {{ item }}"
        baseurl: "{{ mirror_root }}/10/{{ item }}/$basearch/os/"
        enabled: false
        gpgcheck: true
        gpgkey: file:///etc/pki/rpm-gpg/RPM-GPG-KEY-AlmaLinux-10
        state: present
      loop:
        - BaseOS
        - AppStream
```

```text
> ansible web --list-hosts
Only dispatch should appear in the web group's host list.

> ansible-playbook supply.yml --check --diff
A predicted repository-file change on fresh dispatch. No file is created by
this preview.
```

Confirm only dispatch appears. After the preview, repeat the server-side absence check. Then run `ansible-playbook supply.yml` and inspect `cat /etc/yum.repos.d/erudior-web.repo` on the server.

```text
> ansible-playbook supply.yml
On first application the course repository file appears. A repeat on the
same configuration gives changed=0.

> cat /etc/yum.repos.d/erudior-web.repo
Two course repository sections with the expected sources, enabled=0 and RPM
signature checks enabled.
```

Find both sections, the architecture variable, the key URI, and the enabled and signature flags. Repeat the play. What evidence distinguishes a repository being configured from a package being installed? Answer by checking both the file and `rpm -q httpd`.

[AlmaLinux repositories](https://wiki.almalinux.org/repos/AlmaLinux.html) · [Ansible repository module](https://docs.ansible.com/projects/ansible/latest/collections/ansible/builtin/yum_repository_module.html)

lessons.title: Install a package from the approved repositories
topics: Install a package from the approved repositories
lessons.body:
You have two repository definitions and a new work order to install Apache on dispatch. You still need to establish **which repositories can satisfy this transaction**, **what was installed**, and **whether anything is listening**. Each question requires its own observation.

## Resolve and install a named package

On dispatch, DNF can enable the two course entries just for the current command. The options in this query also keep other configured repositories out of its results. Quoting the asterisk stops the shell from expanding it into filenames.

```text
> sudo dnf --disablerepo='*' --enablerepo=erudior-baseos,erudior-appstream list --available httpd
An available httpd package from the selected AppStream repository on the
prepared guest.
```

Read the package name, architecture, version and repository column. Record the version you actually see. The catalog can change between lab sessions. The play declares that httpd must be installed. A later run can satisfy that policy with the already-installed version. Upgrading all available software would be a different work order.

At the **client**, save **install.yml**. Its first playbook import reuses the same repository definition. In the second play, DNF handles the dependency transaction on the managed machine. The control node needs Ansible. The Python used on dispatch needs the DNF bindings, present on the standard lab image. Limiting optional dependencies keeps the practice installation small.

```yaml
---
- name: Configure course repositories
  ansible.builtin.import_playbook: supply.yml

- name: Install the web software on the selected guest
  hosts: web
  gather_facts: false
  become: true
  tasks:
    - name: Install Apache and its required dependencies
      ansible.builtin.dnf:
        name: httpd
        state: present
        disablerepo: '*'
        enablerepo:
          - erudior-baseos
          - erudior-appstream
        install_weak_deps: false
```

Run the following command **after** the live repository configuration from lesson 16.

```text
> ansible-playbook install.yml --check
The preview predicts installation if httpd is absent. The RPM database still
shows the original state.
```

A preview can predict an installation using metadata and may read or populate a metadata cache. Now verify with `rpm -q httpd` at the server that the package is still absent.

```text
> rpm -q httpd
The installed httpd version, or package httpd is not installed on the fresh
baseline.
```

Check mode cannot create a repository for a later task to use in that same dry run on a fresh machine.

Run the following command on the client.

```text
> ansible-playbook install.yml
The first successful apply installs a missing httpd package. A repeat
reports changed=0.
```

Check these results at the **server**.

```text
> rpm -q httpd
The installed httpd version, or package httpd is not installed on the fresh
baseline.

> rpm -qi httpd
An installed RPM information record with name httpd, version, release and
architecture.
```

```text
> systemctl is-enabled httpd.service
disabled on the prepared package-only baseline, enabled after service
configuration.

> systemctl is-active httpd.service
inactive before the service is started, active after the service play
succeeds.
```

The RPM query should identify an installed version. Inspect the signature block in its details. On AlmaLinux 10 the signing information can continue below the Signature label. The clean lab image leaves the new web service inactive and disabled here. Record both service readings even if an image has different presets. Rerun the installation play, then explain how an installed package and an inactive service can both satisfy this particular play.

## Diagnose a failed installation by layer

| Symptom | First observation | What it distinguishes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Repository metadata cannot be loaded | Compare the saved base URL, release path and architecture with the mirror, then test reachability from dispatch | An unavailable catalog prevents package resolution |
| DNF says no package matches | Run the scoped available-package query and check that AppStream participates | Repository selection changes the candidate set |
| Package signature verification fails | Check the RPM source, the trusted key supplied by the OS image, and the repository key setting | A reachable mirror alone cannot establish trust in an RPM |
| Ansible cannot load the DNF Python bindings | Check the managed interpreter and the target’s python3-dnf package | A control node with working Ansible does not supply the guest’s libraries |

**Explain the difference.** Why would inspecting only return code 0 from the second install be weak evidence for a web service work order? Specify one additional check for running now and one for starting after reboot.

[Ansible DNF module](https://docs.ansible.com/projects/ansible/latest/collections/ansible/builtin/dnf_module.html)

lessons.title: Trace a request through systemd and Apache
topics: Trace a request through systemd and Apache
lessons.body:
The httpd package is installed. Dispatch’s operators want a status page readable by local monitoring on that guest. Before writing the play, inspect how this service reads its configuration and how a request reaches it.

## Follow the request from socket to response

| Layer | Evidence on dispatch | Question it answers |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Package | `rpm -q httpd` | Which RPM is installed? |
| Boot policy | `systemctl is-enabled httpd.service` | Will systemd try to start it through its normal boot target? |
| Current process | `systemctl is-active httpd.service` | Is it running now? |
| Socket | `ss -H -ltn 'sport = :80'` | Where could a client connect? |
| Application | Response status, response headers and exact body from /erudior-status.txt | Did the running application deliver the requested release? |

A [[Loopback listener]] bound to **127.0.0.1:80** accepts connections through dispatch’s IPv4 loopback address. A request to that address on the Ansible client would test the client itself. The class uses SSH to manage dispatch and runs the HTTP probe on dispatch. No firewall opening is required for this local-only service.

On the **server**, inspect the stock installation. The rest of the unit assumes one active stock Listen directive and no extra port 80 listeners. If you find a pre-existing website or additional listeners, use the fresh practice server.

```text
> systemctl cat httpd.service
The httpd unit definition, including its startup command.

> sudo grep -nE '^(Listen|IncludeOptional|DocumentRoot)' /etc/httpd/conf/httpd.conf
Numbered configuration lines for Listen, IncludeOptional and DocumentRoot
where those directives occur.
```

`httpd` is the Apache server program. Its -t option checks configuration syntax and -M lists loaded modules.

```text
> sudo /usr/sbin/httpd -M | grep headers_module
A module listing line containing headers_module.

> sudo /usr/sbin/httpd -t
Syntax OK
```

Locate the stock Listen setting, the document root, and the inclusion of **conf.d** files. The headers module provides the **Header** directive. A configuration test can report **Syntax OK** before the service has ever started. A server-name warning can appear alongside that success. Check the command’s exit status as well as its message.

**Fault drill.** Supply a deliberately unknown directive to a single configuration test. The extra directive lives only in this command. Run the regular test again immediately afterward.

```text
> sudo /usr/sbin/httpd -t -C 'ErudiorUnknownDirective on'
An intentional syntax error names ErudiorUnknownDirective. The saved
configuration has not been edited.

> echo "$?"
A nonzero status for the intentional parser error.
```

```text
> sudo /usr/sbin/httpd -t
Syntax OK

> echo "$?"
0
```

The first invocation should fail and the second should succeed. Neither starts the service. A disk file, a syntactically valid configuration, a running process and a correct HTTP response are four different observations.

## Make acceptance criteria before starting anything

On paper, predict the results for a clean **blue** deployment. Port 80 should have exactly one listener, at 127.0.0.1. The URL **http://127.0.0.1/erudior-status.txt** should return status 200, exactly `desk=dispatch` and one newline, a release header of **blue**, and a team header of **operations**. The unit should be enabled and active. A response code alone would also accept an old release.

If the service is active but the URL returns 404, first inspect the URL path and document root. If the body is right but an old header remains, inspect the configuration snippets and whether a reload has taken effect. A second package installation would give little information in either case.

[Ansible systemd service module](https://docs.ansible.com/projects/ansible/latest/collections/ansible/builtin/systemd_service_module.html) · [Apache address binding](https://httpd.apache.org/docs/2.4/bind.html)

lessons.title: Reload Apache when its configuration changes
topics: Reload Apache when its configuration changes
lessons.body:
Operations wants to know that a release change has actually reached the running server. Apache reads its header configuration at startup or reload. It reads the static status page when handling a request. The play needs to tell these changes apart.

## Follow the first live deployment

On the **client**, save **service.yml** from the complete block below. Read it in three passes.

1. **Predict the file changes.** The play validates the track against a small approved mapping. It binds the stock listener to loopback and writes two independent configuration snippets. Blue should yield the literal release header blue and the team header operations. The status page has one line and one trailing newline. 2. **Trace the notification.** A changed configuration task queues the named [[Handler]] for dispatch. Several tasks can queue the same handler during this interval. A static page change alone needs no reload. The syntax test runs on a live application of the play and has `changed_when: false` so its successful observation never counts as a configuration change. 3. **Find the proof.** Enabling the unit controls boot behavior. Starting it controls its current state. The play flushes queued handlers before sending an HTTP request on dispatch. It gives the new release a short time to become visible after a graceful reload, then compares both headers and the full body. In check mode it skips that live probe.

```yaml
---
- name: Apply the desk's HTTP configuration
  hosts: web
  gather_facts: false
  become: true
  vars:
    status_page: "desk=dispatch\n"
  tasks:
    - name: Check that the release has an assigned team
      ansible.builtin.assert:
        that:
          - release_track in release_teams
        fail_msg: Choose a release track from the approved mapping.

    - name: Bind the stock HTTP listener to loopback
      ansible.builtin.lineinfile:
        path: /etc/httpd/conf/httpd.conf
        regexp: '^Listen\s+'
        line: 'Listen 127.0.0.1:80'
      notify: Reload Apache

    - name: Install the release header
      ansible.builtin.copy:
        dest: /etc/httpd/conf.d/erudior-release.conf
        content: |
          Header always set X-Erudior-Release "{{ release_track }}"
        owner: root
        group: root
        mode: '0644'
      notify: Reload Apache

    - name: Install the team header
      ansible.builtin.copy:
        dest: /etc/httpd/conf.d/erudior-team.conf
        content: |
          Header always set X-Erudior-Team "{{ release_teams[release_track] }}"
        owner: root
        group: root
        mode: '0644'
      notify: Reload Apache

    - name: Install the static status page
      ansible.builtin.copy:
        dest: /var/www/html/erudior-status.txt
        content: "{{ status_page }}"
        owner: root
        group: root
        mode: '0644'

    - name: Check the assembled Apache configuration
      ansible.builtin.command: /usr/sbin/httpd -t
      changed_when: false

    - name: Start Apache now and enable it for boot
      ansible.builtin.systemd_service:
        name: httpd.service
        state: started
        enabled: true

    - name: Apply queued configuration changes before the probe
      ansible.builtin.meta: flush_handlers

    - name: Read the running server over loopback
      ansible.builtin.uri:
        url: http://127.0.0.1/erudior-status.txt
        use_proxy: false
        return_content: true
        status_code: 200
      register: live_status
      until: (live_status.x_erudior_release | default('')) == release_track
      retries: 5
      delay: 1
      when: not ansible_check_mode

    - name: Compare the live response with the work order
      ansible.builtin.assert:
        that:
          - live_status.content == status_page
          - live_status.x_erudior_release == release_track
          - live_status.x_erudior_team == release_teams[release_track]
      when: not ansible_check_mode

  handlers:
    - name: Reload Apache
      ansible.builtin.systemd_service:
        name: httpd.service
        state: reloaded
```

Create **site.yml**, the entry point that installs prerequisites before configuring the service.

```yaml
---
- name: Prepare repositories and packages
  ansible.builtin.import_playbook: install.yml

- name: Configure and verify the running server
  ansible.builtin.import_playbook: service.yml
```

```text
> ansible-playbook site.yml --syntax-check
A successful syntax check identifies the playbook. A syntax error instead
identifies the affected file and location.

> ansible-playbook site.yml
The first apply reports changes needed for the web policy. An immediate
repeat on the correct server reports changed=0, failed=0.
```

```text
> ansible-playbook site.yml
The first apply reports changes needed for the web policy. An immediate
repeat on the correct server reports changed=0, failed=0.
```

During the first live run, find each changed configuration task and the single **RUNNING HANDLER [Reload Apache]** line. In the second run, look for an HTTP probe again, zero changes and no handler invocation. Compare this with placing `state: reloaded` in an ordinary task that executes on every run.

On the **server**, inspect the response. The header names are case-insensitive. The values and the page bytes are part of this work order.

```text
> curl --noproxy '*' -fsS -D - http://127.0.0.1/erudior-status.txt
Look for HTTP 200, both X-Erudior headers with the configured values and a
body containing desk=dispatch.

> systemctl show httpd.service -p MainPID -p ActiveState -p UnitFileState
A nonzero MainPID, ActiveState=active and UnitFileState=enabled.
```

```text
> ss -H -ltn 'sport = :80'
No rows when port 80 has no listener. After the loopback-only service
starts, expect its loopback address on port 80.
```

**A release observed between tasks.** During the lab promotion, the file on dispatch already contained `Header always set X-Erudior-Release "green"` while an independent request still returned blue/operations. After the handler ran, another request returned green/support. That gap can be short. This is why the play places its acceptance request after the handler flush.

**Reason through a failure.** If the syntax test fails, the new snippets may already be on disk. The queued reload has not yet run. Read the parser’s filename and line number, fix the source, rerun, and compare the live response. A later run only queues a handler when a notifying task changes. If valid files were corrected outside the play and the process still serves an old response, verify `sudo /usr/sbin/httpd -t`, apply one deliberate `sudo systemctl reload httpd`, then run the play and its endpoint checks again.

```text
> sudo /usr/sbin/httpd -t
Syntax OK

> sudo systemctl reload httpd
No routine output on a successful reload. Recheck the response headers
afterward.
```

```example fade=1
title: Separate a file repair from a reload
problem: An operator edits only the static status page. Both header files still match inventory. What should the next live run change?
step: Identify which task owns the wrong bytes. The static copy task restores the status page.
step: Check its notification list. The static task does not queue Reload Apache.
step: Inspect the application after the repair. The live probe reads the restored bytes from the document root.
answer: The page copy changes, the handler stays idle, and the live probe should return the expected body and both headers.
```

[Ansible handlers](https://docs.ansible.com/projects/ansible/latest/playbook_guide/playbooks_handlers.html) · [Apache response headers](https://httpd.apache.org/docs/2.4/mod/mod_headers.html)

lessons.title: Independent practical: promote and recover the status service
topics: Independent practical: promote and recover the status service
lessons.body:
**Work order.** Promote the dispatch status endpoint from blue to green. The service must remain local to dispatch, report the new support team, recover from a stopped and disabled unit, and answer after a reboot. Archive keeps its existing desk assignment. The application release change belongs in the web group’s inventory data.

| At the endpoint on dispatch | Baseline | Final acceptance |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Listener and URL | 127.0.0.1:80, /erudior-status.txt | Same listener and URL |
| HTTP result and exact body | 200, desk=dispatch plus one newline | Same status and bytes |
| X-Erudior-Release | blue | green |
| X-Erudior-Team | operations | support |
| httpd.service | Enabled and active | Enabled and active after reboot |

Use the **Web service checker** reference on the server. Give it the expected track from this work order so an incorrect inventory edit cannot also change your test expectation. The **Web promotion scoring guide** contains the worked sequence and recovery notes.

1. **Establish a baseline, 2 points.** Record both course repository IDs, signature settings and key source. Capture the installed httpd version and a passing blue response. Identify which guest receives the HTTP request. 2. **Preview the change, 2 points.** Edit the single track value in group_vars. Show the proposed differences on dispatch and prove that the live endpoint still reports blue after the preview. Explain what check mode can predict here because the package and files already exist. 3. **Apply and observe, 2 points.** Use Navigator and the execution environment from the previous units. Capture both changed header tasks, the count of actual reload-handler invocations, and the independent green response. Run the play again and account for its change count. 4. **Repair service drift, 2 points.** On the dedicated dispatch practice VM stop and disable only httpd.service. Capture both failed acceptance conditions. Reapply the play, verify green, and show whether the header files or the reload handler were needed for that repair. 5. **Prove boot persistence, 2 points.** Record dispatch’s boot ID, reboot that VM, then verify a different boot ID and a passing green response **before applying anything**. Show a final zero-change play. On dispatch verify the previous beta release note and night/off desk state. On archive confirm the day/on desk state.

Award each row when all of its requested evidence is present. The written quiz is scored separately. If the unit is active but the independent probe reports stale headers, the promotion is still incomplete. Follow the evidence to the first layer that differs.

## Replay the promotion

After confirming the blue starting state and before attempting the promotion, power off both guests. Capture it on the host with `python3 lab.py capture rhce --baseline web-blue`.

```text
> python3 lab.py capture rhce --baseline web-blue
The kit records the powered-off pair as the requested baseline. An active
guest can prevent capture.
```

For each retry use `python3 lab.py reset rhce --baseline web-blue --start --offline`.

```text
> python3 lab.py reset rhce --baseline web-blue --start --offline
The selected kit baseline is restored and the guests start with offline
networking. Check the consoles after boot.
```

The controller project and managed service both return to blue. Copy your evidence outside the guests before you reset.

```assignment
lab: promote-web-service-evidence
```

lessons.title: Give a service account read-only access
topics: Give a service account read-only access
lessons.body:
Dispatch needs a collector that reads its own settings. A person still administers the server through the learner account. Give the collector a separate Unix identity so it can read its configuration while other ordinary users cannot. Across this unit you will build three small plays and hand their combined result to the next shift.

## Start with the two consoles

In Erudior Desktop, open the practice terminal beside this lesson. The client is your control node. The server is dispatch. Finish the SSH and inventory lessons first. Keep both guests running. A manual pair from the AlmaLinux practice kit works too.

On the **client**, create a fresh project. Reuse the verified inventory and host keys from the web unit. From now on, run project commands from this directory as learner. If sudo on your pair asks for a password, add `-K` to playbook runs.

```text
> umask 077
No output. Newly created files in this shell are private by default.

> mkdir -p ~/rhce-collector/{ssh,templates}
No output. The project directories named on the command line now exist.
```

```text
> cd ~/rhce-collector
No output. The shell now works in the named project directory.

> cp ~/rhce-web/{ansible.cfg,inventory.ini} .
No output. The named project files have been copied into the destination
directory.
```

```text
> cp ~/rhce-web/ssh/known_hosts ssh/
No output. The named project files have been copied into the destination
directory.

> eval "$(ssh-agent -s)"
Agent pid followed by a number. This shell now knows the agent's socket.
```

```text
> ssh-add -t 4h ~/.ssh/erudior_rhce
Identity added followed by the lab key path. A protected key prompts for its
passphrase.

> ansible web --list-hosts
Only dispatch should appear in the web group's host list.
```

```text
> ansible web -m ansible.builtin.ping
dispatch reports SUCCESS with ping set to pong.
```

The list should contain exactly **dispatch** and ping should return pong. Stop and fix the inventory or trust entry if either check differs. This unit uses ansible-playbook on the control node. Its modules ship with ansible-core.

At the **server console**, run `id erucollect`, `getent group eruread` and `ls -ld /etc/erudior-collector`.

```text
> id erucollect
Before provisioning, id reports no such user. Afterward look for erucollect
with primary group eruread.

> getent group eruread
A group record for eruread after provisioning. An unused name gives no
output.
```

```text
> ls -ld /etc/erudior-collector
The directory is absent before provisioning. Afterward look for drwxr-x---
and root eruread.
```

On the first attempt all three objects should be absent. If you find a pre-existing identity with an unrelated purpose, switch to a fresh practice pair. During a repeat run the objects belong to this exercise.

## Separate identity from access

Save **identity.yml** on the client. The group must exist before it can become the account's primary group. The parent directory belongs to root. Members of eruread may traverse and list it. Only root can replace entries in it. A non-login shell suits a service that never needs an interactive session.

```yaml
---
- name: Give the dispatch collector a read-only identity
  hosts: web
  become: true
  gather_facts: false
  tasks:
    - name: Create the reader group
      ansible.builtin.group:
        name: eruread
        system: true
        state: present

    - name: Create the service identity
      ansible.builtin.user:
        name: erucollect
        group: eruread
        system: true
        create_home: false
        shell: /sbin/nologin
        state: present

    - name: Set the configuration directory boundary
      ansible.builtin.file:
        path: /etc/erudior-collector
        state: directory
        owner: root
        group: eruread
        mode: '0750'
```

Run `ansible-playbook --syntax-check identity.yml` and then `ansible-playbook identity.yml` twice.

```text
> ansible-playbook --syntax-check identity.yml
A successful syntax check identifies the playbook. A syntax error instead
identifies the affected file and location.

> ansible-playbook identity.yml
On a fresh guest the play creates the group, account and directory. The next
run reports changed=0.
```

On a fresh pair expect the first run to create three objects and the second to report changed=0. A check-mode run against an empty server cannot create prerequisite groups for downstream tasks.

## Check access as the consumer

On **dispatch**, inspect the name, primary group, shell and directory. Predict each test result before running it.

```text
> getent passwd erucollect
A passwd record for erucollect ending with its non-login shell.

> id erucollect
Before provisioning, id reports no such user. Afterward look for erucollect
with primary group eruread.
```

```text
> stat -c '%U:%G %a %n' /etc/erudior-collector
root:eruread 750 /etc/erudior-collector

> sudo -u erucollect test -x /etc/erudior-collector && echo can-traverse
can-traverse
```

```text
> sudo -u erucollect test ! -w /etc/erudior-collector && echo cannot-replace-entries
cannot-replace-entries

> sudo -u nobody test ! -x /etc/erudior-collector && echo ordinary-user-excluded
ordinary-user-excluded
```

A service can run under this UID even with a non-login shell. The supervisor sets its identity directly. If the directory were group-writable, a reader could replace a root-owned file by renaming another entry over it. This is why the directory and the files need separate checks.

[Ansible documentation](https://docs.ansible.com/projects/ansible/latest/collections/ansible/builtin/user_module.html)

lessons.title: Render a policy and reject a broken candidate
topics: Render a policy and reject a broken candidate
lessons.body:
The operations desk wants a machine-readable policy. Dispatch identifies itself by its inventory alias and initially polls every 60 seconds. Write that policy once as a Jinja template. Supply the interval as data so the next shift can change it without rewriting the task.

## Give each value an owner

In **~/rhce-collector** on the client, save **policy.yml**. The public policy can be reviewed in ordinary source control. Keep the number unquoted so it remains a YAML integer.

```yaml
---
collector_interval: 60
```

Save **templates/collector.json.j2**. The controller resolves each expression for the targeted host. The to_json filter supplies JSON quoting and escaping for the desk name. The interval becomes a JSON number.

```jinja
{
  "desk": {{ inventory_hostname | to_json }},
  "interval_seconds": {{ collector_interval }}
}
```

Save **render.yml**. Read the assertion as the contract for the input. The validate step runs the target's JSON parser on a temporary candidate before Ansible installs it at its destination. The percent-s placeholder is the temporary filename.

```yaml
---
- name: Render the dispatch collector policy
  hosts: web
  become: true
  gather_facts: false
  vars_files:
    - policy.yml
  tasks:
    - name: Require a polling interval from 10 through 300 seconds
      ansible.builtin.assert:
        that:
          - collector_interval is integer
          - 10 <= collector_interval <= 300

    - name: Install syntactically valid JSON for the collector
      ansible.builtin.template:
        src: templates/collector.json.j2
        dest: /etc/erudior-collector/policy.json
        owner: root
        group: eruread
        mode: '0640'
        validate: /usr/bin/python3 -m json.tool %s
```

Run the following command twice.

```text
> ansible-playbook render.yml
The policy is installed on dispatch if different. On an unchanged repeat the
recap has changed=0.
```

On dispatch, read the result with `sudo -u erucollect python3 -m json.tool /etc/erudior-collector/policy.json`.

```text
> sudo -u erucollect python3 -m json.tool /etc/erudior-collector/policy.json
Formatted JSON containing the dispatch alias and the requested interval.
Invalid JSON produces a parser error.
```

Look for the literal desk name **dispatch** and the numeric interval **60**. A zero-change run is useful only after the intended consumer has read the intended values.

## Reject a bad candidate

Record `sudo sha256sum /etc/erudior-collector/policy.json` on dispatch.

`sha256sum` calculates a digest from file contents. Matching digests let you check that the same bytes survived a copy or reboot.

```text
> sudo sha256sum /etc/erudior-collector/policy.json
A 64-character digest and the policy path. The digest should remain stable
when the candidate is rejected.
```

On the controller temporarily remove the comma after the desk expression in the template and run render.yml normally. Expect the validation task to fail. Compare the installed file's checksum with the one you recorded. Restore the comma, run again and expect changed=0. This is a checksum of public policy only.

Now try `ansible-playbook render.yml -e '{"collector_interval":5}'`.

```text
> ansible-playbook render.yml -e '{"collector_interval":5}'
The range assertion fails before rendering. The live policy's checksum
should be unchanged.
```

The assertion should stop the play before the template task. Explain the difference between these failures. A parser recognizes valid JSON, including a perfectly well-formed interval of 5. The assertion enforces the desk's operating rule.

[Ansible documentation](https://docs.ansible.com/projects/ansible/latest/collections/ansible/builtin/template_module.html)

lessons.title: Deploy a credential without exposing it in a diff
topics: Deploy a credential without exposing it in a diff
lessons.body:
The collector also needs a dispatch token. It must be available to the service on the target, but a teammate reviewing the project must see only ciphertext. Use two independent, made-up values for this lab: a Vault password that opens the source file and a disposable token that the collector consumes. Keep both out of your notes, command arguments and screenshots.

## Create the encrypted source

On the client, in **~/rhce-collector**, run the following. The editor is vi with its initialization, swap and persistent history disabled for this lab. Enter a fresh practice Vault password at the prompts, then use the editor to create one YAML mapping.

```text
> umask 077
No output. Newly created files in this shell are private by default.
```

`ansible-vault` creates and edits encrypted Ansible variable files using a vault password.

```text
> EDITOR='vi -u NONE -n -i NONE' ansible-vault create vault.yml
Vault prompts for a new vault password and confirmation, then opens the
editor. Saving produces encrypted vault.yml.
```

In the buffer enter `vault_dispatch_token:` followed by a space and a quoted, invented token of 16–64 letters, digits, underscores or hyphens. Press Escape and type `:wq` followed by Enter. Run the following command.

```text
> head -n 1 vault.yml
Only the Vault format header beginning with $ANSIBLE_VAULT; appears.
```

It should begin with `$ANSIBLE_VAULT;`. Store the lab password separately from the project. An encrypted file may go into Git. The password, editor backups and decrypted copies do not belong there.

Save **secret.yml**. Only the tasks that handle the secret suppress logs. Public policy can still produce a useful diff. Keep the credential as a separate file so a JSON formatting error or a policy review never prints it.

```yaml
---
- name: Deliver the dispatch credential
  hosts: web
  become: true
  gather_facts: false
  vars_files:
    - vault.yml
  tasks:
    - name: Confirm the presence and form of the credential
      ansible.builtin.assert:
        that:
          - vault_dispatch_token is string
          - vault_dispatch_token is match('^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{16,64}\\Z')
      no_log: true

    - name: Install one line readable by the collector
      ansible.builtin.copy:
        content: "{{ vault_dispatch_token }}\n"
        dest: /etc/erudior-collector/token
        owner: root
        group: eruread
        mode: '0640'
      no_log: true
      diff: false
```

Run the following command twice.

```text
> ansible-playbook --ask-vault-pass secret.yml
A Vault password prompt followed by a recap for dispatch. The credential
task suppresses sensitive detail.
```

Type the Vault password at the prompt. Expect the deployment to change the first time and settle on the second. If decryption fails, check the password and the encrypted file you selected. If the assertion fails after decryption, use ansible-vault edit to check the variable name, type and allowed characters.

## Verify without printing the credential

On dispatch, use the **Collector acceptance checks** reference. It compares the deployed bytes with the token you enter privately at the prompt. It also checks that the service account can read the file and that the unprivileged account `nobody` is denied. Keep the pass/fail messages as evidence.

Vault protects the source on disk. The deployed token is plaintext because the consuming service needs it. Directory permissions, ownership and file mode protect that copy. A quiet Ansible task cannot repair an overly broad group or a writable parent directory by itself.

[Ansible documentation](https://docs.ansible.com/projects/ansible/latest/vault_guide/vault.html)

lessons.title: Repair permission drift and rotate just the credential
topics: Repair permission drift and rotate just the credential
lessons.body:
A handoff is easier when the operator can apply the complete collector policy in one run. The identity controls access, the JSON describes behavior, and the token authorizes the consumer. Changing one should leave the other two alone.

## Assemble the three plays

Save **site.yml** in the project. Each import loads a complete play. Order matters on a fresh target because the later file tasks refer to an account, group and directory that the first play creates.

```yaml
---
- ansible.builtin.import_playbook: identity.yml
- ansible.builtin.import_playbook: render.yml
- ansible.builtin.import_playbook: secret.yml
```

Before changing the inputs, run these commands. At each password prompt supply the Vault password. If the preceding lessons are complete the full run should report changed=0.

```text
> ansible-playbook --ask-vault-pass --syntax-check site.yml
A successful syntax check identifies the playbook. A syntax error instead
identifies the affected file and location.

> ansible-playbook --ask-vault-pass --list-hosts site.yml
The target list contains only dispatch for the collector plays.
```

```text
> ansible-playbook --ask-vault-pass site.yml
After the Vault password prompt, only drift should be repaired. An immediate
unchanged repeat should report changed=0.
```

## Rehearse a permission repair

On **dispatch** temporarily set `sudo chmod 0600 /etc/erudior-collector/token`.

```text
> sudo chmod 0600 /etc/erudior-collector/token
No output. The service group has lost read permission on the token.
```

Check that `sudo -u erucollect test -r /etc/erudior-collector/token` now exits 1.

```text
> sudo -u erucollect test -r /etc/erudior-collector/token
No output. Status is nonzero under the intentional 0600 fault and zero after
restoring group read access.
```

This is a restrictive fault. The file never becomes broadly readable. On the client, run the full play in check mode with `--check --diff --ask-vault-pass`. Expect a proposed change to the credential task and no secret value. Repeat the read test on dispatch. It should still fail because check mode did not apply the change.

Apply site.yml normally. The credential task should change and the read test should succeed. Neither the identity nor the public policy should need a change. Run the play once more and look for changed=0.

## Rotate one piece of data

On the client use `EDITOR='vi -u NONE -n -i NONE' ansible-vault edit vault.yml` and replace only the disposable token.

```text
> EDITOR='vi -u NONE -n -i NONE' ansible-vault edit vault.yml
Vault prompts for the password and opens the decrypted content in the
configured editor. Saving re-encrypts it.
```

Preserve the Vault password. Before deployment, the original value should still pass the server's private comparison. Apply site.yml and run the comparison twice. The new token should pass and the old token should fail. Record the outcomes without recording either value. If both comparisons appear to pass, check that you actually used two distinct values and that your evidence came from dispatch.

Changing the Vault password with ansible-vault rekey would change who can decrypt the project. It would leave the service token inside the file untouched. Explain which operation an on-call engineer needs when the application credential itself must change.

lessons.title: Independent practical: hand the collector to the evening shift
topics: Independent practical: hand the collector to the evening shift
lessons.body:
## Work order

Dispatch is handing the collector to the evening shift. Its new polling interval is **90 seconds**. Replace its service credential with a fresh disposable token. Only root and the collector's reader group should have access to the credential. Archive is outside the change window. Work from the existing collector project and leave earlier web and desk configuration in place.

Begin with the 60-second policy, a working current token and a zero-change run. Keep the starting token and the replacement privately available to you for comparison. This is a self-scored practical. Set aside 35 minutes. Attempt it using the work order and checklist before opening the worked handoff.

| Evidence to collect | Points |
| --- | ---: |
| Show the single inventory target. On dispatch record its boot ID, effective service identity, 60-second policy and a successful private comparison with the current token. On archive establish that the collector path is absent. | 2 |
| Change the source policy and encrypted token. Preview the change. Show the proposed public policy, the absence of a token diff, and the still-active original policy and token before application. | 2 |
| Apply once. Use the independent checker with interval 90. Prove the replacement token passes and the original fails. Show that the collector can read both files and cannot overwrite them. | 2 |
| With root on dispatch remove only group-read access from the token. Confirm the consumer loses access. Repair through the saved play and account for the changed task. Demonstrate a zero-change repeat. | 2 |
| Reboot **dispatch only**. Show the changed boot ID and rerun the independent checks before any playbook runs. Verify the replacement still passes, the collector path remains absent on archive, and the next full play has changed=0. | 2 |

Award a row only when you can produce all its observations. A zero-change play can faithfully preserve an incorrect interval. A successful root read can hide a broken service account. Keep the independent checks and the run recap together.

## Repeating the work order

For a quick replay, restore 60 in policy.yml and set another disposable starting token with ansible-vault edit. Apply once and verify the starting state on both guests. If you use the manual host launcher, a powered-off snapshot of both guests at that baseline can also restore the work order. Erudior Desktop's **Reset disks** returns its practice pair to the installed base. Copy any evidence you want to keep off the guests before a disk reset.

```assignment
lab: collector-handoff-evidence
```

lessons.title: Trace the route from the client to the green page
topics: Trace the route from the client to the green page
lessons.body:
Dispatch already serves the green shift report to a monitor on the server. Now the operator at the client console needs to read it across the private network. The work order authorizes inbound HTTP on the course link. SSH must keep working throughout. The server's other interface is outside the change window.

## Trace one request on paper

On the course pair the client is **192.168.77.20**, and dispatch is **192.168.77.10**. An HTTP request leaves the client, arrives on a server interface, passes that interface's firewall rules, then reaches an Apache listening socket. A [[Firewall zone]] groups rules for incoming traffic. A [[Listener address]] determines which local addresses a process accepts connections on. You need evidence at both layers.

Start after the green web promotion and collector handoff. Use the standard AlmaLinux 10.3 pair and its course addresses. Keep the server and client consoles open. The examples use the control node's native Ansible installation and the trusted SSH configuration you already built. Run project commands as learner on the client. Add `-K` to playbook runs if sudo on dispatch needs a password.

```text
> mkdir -p ~/rhce-firewall/ssh && cd ~/rhce-firewall
The new project directory is now your working directory.

> cp ~/rhce-web/{ansible.cfg,inventory.ini} . && cp ~/rhce-web/ssh/known_hosts ssh/
The project now has the web inventory and its verified host keys.

> ansible web --list-hosts
One host, dispatch.

> ansible web -m ansible.builtin.ping
Dispatch returns pong. Ansible authenticated and ran Python there.
```

If SSH asks about a changed key, compare it at the server console using the earlier trust lesson. If the agent has expired, reload your course key as in the web unit.

## Identify the private zone at the server console

`ip route get` asks the kernel how it would reach one address. Read the device after **dev** and local address after **src**. `firewall-cmd` reads or changes firewalld policy. Without `--permanent` a query describes the running firewall. With it, a query describes what is saved for the next start or reload.

```text
> ip -4 route get 192.168.77.20
The route uses the course interface with src 192.168.77.10.

> sudo firewall-cmd --get-active-zones
The private interface appears under internal. Record the second interface and its zone if present.

> sudo firewall-cmd --get-default-zone
On the standard kit this differs from internal.

> sudo firewall-cmd --zone=internal --list-interfaces
The single interface from the private route.

> sudo firewall-cmd --zone=internal --list-sources
An empty line. The kit assigns this zone by interface.

> sudo firewall-cmd --zone=internal --query-service=http
no on the fresh, closed baseline. A negative query exits 1.

> sudo firewall-cmd --permanent --zone=internal --query-service=http
no on the saved baseline.
```

The kit's NetworkManager profile **lab-private** binds this interface to **internal**. If the address, zone or membership differs, inspect the guest's setup using the AlmaLinux setup reference before applying this work order. Also inspect the zone details for existing broad accepts, direct HTTP ports or rich rules. Use the unmodified course baseline for this exercise. Capture the other zone's runtime and saved settings for comparison at handoff.

```text
> sudo firewall-cmd --zone=internal --list-all
The private interface, its services and any additional rules.

> ss -H -4ltn 'sport = :80'
The green web baseline shows 127.0.0.1:80 only.

> curl --noproxy '*' -fsS -D - http://127.0.0.1/erudior-status.txt
HTTP 200, the green and support headers, and the desk=dispatch line.
```

Back on the **client**, use a short connection timeout and bypass any HTTP proxy. The client and server have different loopback addresses. Keep this result beside the successful SSH check.

```text
> curl --noproxy '*' --connect-timeout 3 --max-time 6 -sS -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' http://192.168.77.10/erudior-status.txt
The closed baseline gives a connection error and HTTP code 000.
```

**Predict the next observation.** Suppose Apache begins listening on the private address while the firewall stays closed. The server can then see a second socket. A new client HTTP connection should still fail, and SSH should still work. That change gives you a way to test one layer at a time.

lessons.title: Add one private listener while keeping the firewall closed
topics: Add one private listener while keeping the firewall closed
lessons.body:
The status page, green release header and support team header already exist. The new requirement changes where the same page can be reached. Keep Apache's existing loopback listener and add a second exact IPv4 address. A wildcard such as 0.0.0.0 would bind the server's other IPv4 addresses as well.

## Add the private listener

From **~/rhce-firewall** on the client, save the following as **listener.yml**. The first task checks that the address belongs to dispatch. Apache reads files in **conf.d** alongside its main configuration. A systemd drop-in orders Apache after network startup because Apache now binds an address assigned by NetworkManager. Keep the prepared guest's NetworkManager wait-online service enabled.

```yaml
---
- name: Serve the dispatch status page on the course network
  hosts: web
  become: true
  tasks:
    - name: Verify the private address belongs to this server
      ansible.builtin.assert:
        that:
          - inventory_hostname == 'dispatch'
          - "'192.168.77.10' in ansible_facts.all_ipv4_addresses"

    - name: Add a listener for the private address
      ansible.builtin.copy:
        dest: /etc/httpd/conf.d/erudior-private-listen.conf
        content: "Listen 192.168.77.10:80\n"
        owner: root
        group: root
        mode: '0644'
      notify: Restart Apache

    - name: Create the service override directory
      ansible.builtin.file:
        path: /etc/systemd/system/httpd.service.d
        state: directory
        mode: '0755'

    - name: Wait for configured networking at boot
      ansible.builtin.copy:
        dest: /etc/systemd/system/httpd.service.d/erudior-network.conf
        content: |
          [Unit]
          Wants=network-online.target
          After=network-online.target
        mode: '0644'
      notify: Restart Apache

    - name: Test the assembled Apache configuration
      ansible.builtin.command: /usr/sbin/httpd -t
      changed_when: false

  handlers:
    - name: Restart Apache
      ansible.builtin.systemd_service:
        name: httpd
        daemon_reload: true
        state: restarted
```

The two configuration files notify the same handler. A handler runs once at the end of the play when a notifying task changed. Here a restart makes Apache bind the full new socket set. The existing web unit's reload handler still handles later header changes. The parser test reports a failure before the restart if the assembled configuration has a syntax error.

```text
> ansible-playbook listener.yml --syntax-check
Ansible names listener.yml after parsing it.

> ansible-playbook listener.yml
Dispatch receives the listener and boot ordering. Look for one Restart Apache handler.

> ansible-playbook listener.yml
The recap has changed=0 and failed=0. The syntax test still runs.
```

On **dispatch**, read the socket table again. `ss` shows kernel sockets. The HTTP response proves which content Apache is serving.

```text
> ss -H -4ltn 'sport = :80'
Two local addresses on port 80, 127.0.0.1 and 192.168.77.10. No wildcard listener.

> curl --noproxy '*' -fsS -D - http://127.0.0.1/erudior-status.txt
HTTP 200, X-Erudior-Release green, X-Erudior-Team support, and desk=dispatch.

> systemctl is-enabled httpd NetworkManager-wait-online.service
Both units are enabled on the prepared lab server.
```

Save **check-private.sh** from the **Private HTTP acceptance checks** reference on the client. Its **open** check compares the status, two response headers and exact page bytes. Its **closed** check accepts a refused or timed-out connection with no HTTP response. Run it from the client so the packet traverses the private link.

```text
> bash check-private.sh closed
Curl reports a connection error, followed by PASS: no private HTTP connection.

> ansible web -m ansible.builtin.ping
Dispatch still returns pong over SSH.
```

**Explain the result.** The server has the correct sockets and page. The client can reach the server using SSH. The client cannot yet retrieve HTTP. At this point, changing the page or restarting Apache again would leave the missing inbound rule untouched.

lessons.title: Apply and verify a zone-scoped firewall policy
topics: Apply and verify a zone-scoped firewall policy
lessons.body:
The private listener is ready. You can now open one named service in one zone. The AlmaLinux DVD supplies the `rhel-system-roles` package. Its firewall role accepts a list of requested rules. We will enable **http** in **internal**, preserve SSH and leave the default zone's rules alone.

## Load the role on the control node

On the **client**, use the signed DVD repositories from the AlmaLinux setup. A role is a packaged group of automation tasks. Its fully qualified name identifies its collection and the role inside it. The role runs from the native control-node installation for this unit.

```text
> sudo dnf --disablerepo='*' --enablerepo='erudior-dvd-*' install rhel-system-roles
DNF identifies the signed package and any dependencies. Review the transaction and confirm it.

> ansible-galaxy collection list redhat.rhel_system_roles
The installed collection appears with its path and version.

> less /usr/share/doc/rhel-system-roles/firewall/README.md
The installed role's options and examples open. Search for runtime and permanent. Press q to exit.
```

On **dispatch**, firewalld is already installed and running from kit preparation. Verify `sudo firewall-cmd --state` reports **running**. The role checks its packages on dispatch, even during a preview. On **dispatch**, run `sudo dnf --disablerepo='*' --enablerepo='erudior-dvd-*' repolist` and verify that **erudior-dvd-baseos** and **erudior-dvd-appstream** appear. Leave the DVD attached. The play's package defaults limit that check to these two signed repositories, so the isolated pair can work offline.

The role's **runtime** setting acts on the live rule set. **permanent** writes the saved rule. Setting both to true makes today's access and the next boot agree. Setting **state** to disabled removes this service allowance from the selected zone.

## Preview, then publish

Save **firewall.yml** on the client. The first read returns the route as JSON. The play extracts the interface name from the first route, reads its zone and rejects an unexpected topology. In an Ansible check-mode run the read-only queries still run because they set `check_mode: false`. They never write settings. The parameter **http_access** defaults to enabled. A command-line extra variable can override it for the maintenance exercise.

```yaml
---
- name: Maintain HTTP access on the isolated dispatch network
  hosts: web
  become: true
  gather_subset:
    - '!all'
    - min
  module_defaults:
    ansible.builtin.package:
      disablerepo: '*'
      enablerepo:
        - erudior-dvd-baseos
        - erudior-dvd-appstream
  vars:
    http_access: enabled
  pre_tasks:
    - name: Find the interface on the route back to the client
      ansible.builtin.command: ip -j -4 route get 192.168.77.20
      register: course_route
      changed_when: false
      check_mode: false

    - name: Read the zone serving the private address
      ansible.builtin.command:
        argv:
          - firewall-cmd
          - "--get-zone-of-interface={{ (course_route.stdout | from_json | first).dev }}"
      register: private_zone
      changed_when: false
      check_mode: false

    - name: Read the interfaces and sources sharing the internal zone
      ansible.builtin.command:
        argv: [firewall-cmd, --zone=internal, "{{ item }}"]
      loop: [--list-interfaces, --list-sources]
      register: members
      changed_when: false
      check_mode: false

    - name: Read the default zone
      ansible.builtin.command: firewall-cmd --get-default-zone
      register: default_zone
      changed_when: false
      check_mode: false

    - name: Check the requested scope before changing rules
      ansible.builtin.assert:
        that:
          - inventory_hostname == 'dispatch'
          - http_access in ['enabled', 'disabled']
          - (course_route.stdout | from_json | first).prefsrc == '192.168.77.10'
          - private_zone.stdout == 'internal'
          - members.results[0].stdout.split() == [(course_route.stdout | from_json | first).dev]
          - members.results[1].stdout | trim == ''
          - default_zone.stdout != 'internal'

  roles:
    - role: redhat.rhel_system_roles.firewall
      vars:
        firewall:
          - zone: internal
            service: http
            state: "{{ http_access }}"
            runtime: true
            permanent: true
```

```text
> ansible-playbook firewall.yml --syntax-check
The play parses and the control node can resolve the installed role.

> ansible-playbook firewall.yml --check --diff
The recap predicts a change on dispatch. Review the proposed internal HTTP allowance.

> bash check-private.sh closed
The client still sees a connection failure after the preview.

> ansible-playbook firewall.yml
The role applies the requested change on dispatch.

> bash check-private.sh open
PASS: private HTTP 200, expected headers and exact page bytes

> ansible-playbook firewall.yml
The second live run reports changed=0 and failed=0.
```

On **dispatch**, run both queries again. Check that the other interface's zone settings match the original capture. On the client, run the SSH ping once more.

```text
> sudo firewall-cmd --zone=internal --query-service=http
yes in the running firewall.

> sudo firewall-cmd --permanent --zone=internal --query-service=http
yes in the saved configuration.
```

**Diagnose a split result.** A remote HTTP 200 today with a runtime yes and a permanent no means a reload or reboot can close the service. A permanent yes paired with a runtime no means the saved allowance has not reached today's client. Reconcile the named rule with the saved play and check each layer independently.

[Firewall system role documentation](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/red_hat_enterprise_linux/10/html/automating_system_administration_by_using_rhel_system_roles/configuring-firewalld-by-using-rhel-system-roles) · [Runtime and permanent firewalld configuration](https://firewalld.org/documentation/configuration/runtime-versus-permanent.html)

lessons.title: Independent practical: reopen the private dispatch desk
topics: Independent practical: reopen the private dispatch desk
lessons.body:
The night supervisor wants a private status endpoint that survives a reboot. First demonstrate a maintenance window in which remote readers lose HTTP while local monitoring and SSH keep working. Then reopen it, diagnose a single runtime fault, and hand the repaired service to the next shift.

Use the two AlmaLinux guests, the green dispatch page, and your firewall project. Begin with the open, converged state from the previous lesson. Set aside 35 minutes. This is a self-scored practical. Collect the evidence before reading the **Private service handoff scoring guide**.

| Work order | Evidence to retain | Points |
| --- | --- | ---: |
| Identify the change boundary. | Record dispatch's boot ID and the route/interface and zone on the private link. Capture both internal HTTP query results, loopback HTTP, client HTTP, SSH and the other zone's settings. | 2 |
| Close for maintenance. | Use the saved play with http_access disabled. Both HTTP allowance queries say no. Client HTTP fails with no HTTP response. Loopback still returns the green report, and SSH still works. | 2 |
| Reopen and repair drift. | Apply the normal enabled policy. Remove only the **runtime** internal HTTP allowance at the dispatch console. Explain the two query results and the client failure. Repair using the play, pass the client check and show a zero-change repeat. | 2 |
| Prove persistence. | Reboot dispatch only. Before running any configuration play, show a different boot ID, the two expected listeners, both HTTP query results and the correct page from the client. | 2 |
| Hand off the boundary. | The other zone's runtime and permanent settings match the baseline. SSH still works. A final run has changed=0. Explain why an HTTP 404 is different from the closed maintenance result. | 2 |

A zero-change recap proves that rerunning the same instructions made no further change. It cannot tell you whether the client received the intended page. Award each row when you can reproduce all of its observations. If a row fails, record which observation narrowed the fault and repeat that row.

To replay, start from a passing open state. To return to the earlier web unit's loopback-only checker, use the rollback in the scoring guide.

```assignment
lab: handoff-private-firewall-evidence
```

lessons.title: Author one duty-record role for two desks
topics: Author one duty-record role for two desks
lessons.body:
Dispatch and archive both need an owner record. A maintainer copied the same three tasks into two playbooks, then fixed the file mode in only one. Move the policy into one role. Let each desk supply its shift while the role owns the layout, validation and permissions.

## Give the role a small contract

On the client, copy the two-desk project's inventory and SSH configuration into a new project. Start the same limited-lifetime SSH agent as in **Give two managed hosts different policies** if the earlier agent has expired. Verify both fingerprints before continuing. If the authorized learner account needs a sudo password, add -K to privileged playbook and ad hoc runs throughout these units and enter the lab password at the prompt. The staged pair must accept the authorized credential on both hosts.

```text
> mkdir -p ~/rhce-ops && cd ~/rhce-ops
The new project is the working directory.

> cp -r ~/rhce-desks/{ansible.cfg,inventory.ini,ssh} .
The inventory and the project's verified host keys are available here.

> mkdir -p roles/desk_record/{defaults,tasks,templates,meta} host_vars
The role has a separate location for each kind of input.

> ansible desks -m ansible.builtin.ping
Both dispatch and archive return pong over SSH.
```

In **host_vars/archive.yml**, set `desk_owner: night`. Dispatch inherits the role default. A role default gives a caller a value to override. A hardcoded value in a task would force the two desks to agree.

**roles/desk_record/defaults/main.yml**

```yaml
---
desk_owner: day
desk_record_dir: /etc/erudior-record
```
**roles/desk_record/templates/owner.j2**

```jinja2
desk={{ inventory_hostname }}
owner={{ desk_owner }}
```
**roles/desk_record/tasks/main.yml**

```yaml
---
- name: Reject an unknown shift before writing
  ansible.builtin.assert:
    that: desk_owner in ['day', 'night']

- name: Create the public record directory
  ansible.builtin.file:
    path: "{{ desk_record_dir }}"
    state: directory
    owner: root
    group: root
    mode: '0755'

- name: Render the duty record
  ansible.builtin.template:
    src: owner.j2
    dest: "{{ desk_record_dir }}/owner"
    owner: root
    group: root
    mode: '0644'
```
**roles/desk_record/meta/main.yml**

```yaml
---
dependencies: []
```
**records.yml**

```yaml
---
- name: Issue duty records to the two desks
  hosts: desks
  become: true
  gather_facts: false
  roles:
    - desk_record
```

## Predict and test

Run `ansible-playbook records.yml` twice from this project. On each guest read `cat /etc/erudior-record/owner` and `stat -c '%U:%G %a' /etc/erudior-record/owner`. Expect the inventory alias, the correct shift, and root:root 644. The second play should report zero changes on both hosts. Change the archive host variable to an unsupported shift. Predict which host will fail and whether its old file will change. Limit the play to archive, verify the old bytes, and restore the variable. The assertion runs before either write. Keep the passing project for the next lesson.

lessons.title: Install a standalone role in a clean project
topics: Install a standalone role in a clean project
lessons.body:
A second team wants to use your role without giving its playbook access to the author's working tree. Package a known version, install it into a clean consumer project, then change the author's copy and explain which version the consumer will run.

## Package a standalone role

In `~/rhce-ops` create a local distribution directory. The archive contains the role directory at its top level, including **meta/main.yml**. Treat a released archive as immutable. The checksum identifies the received bytes; when exchanging it, obtain the expected digest through a trusted channel.

```text
> mkdir -p dist && tar -czf dist/desk_record-1.0.0.tar.gz -C roles desk_record
The archive contains the standalone role. No target system has changed.

> (cd dist && sha256sum desk_record-1.0.0.tar.gz > SHA256SUMS)
The distribution directory now includes a digest for this release.

> mkdir -p ~/rhce-consumer && cp -r ansible.cfg inventory.ini ssh host_vars records.yml dist ~/rhce-consumer/
The consumer has the playbook, inventory and archive. Its roles directory does not yet exist.

> cd ~/rhce-consumer && (cd dist && sha256sum -c SHA256SUMS)
The archive must report OK.
```

Save **role-requirements.yml** in the consumer. Run the installer from that directory so the relative archive path resolves. Naming the installed role keeps the consumer play independent of the archive filename.

```yaml
---
roles:
  - name: desk_record
    src: ./dist/desk_record-1.0.0.tar.gz
```

```text
> ansible-galaxy role install -r role-requirements.yml -p ./roles
Galaxy extracts desk_record from the local archive.

> ansible-galaxy role list -p ./roles
The project role directory contains desk_record.

> ansible-playbook records.yml
Both desks retain their expected records. Previously converged desks report zero changes.
```

Add a comment to the author's role source. Use `diff` to compare the author's task file with the installed one. Editing the producer does not update the consumer. Explain what must be rebuilt, authenticated and reinstalled for the consumer to get a new release. If an older role is already installed, stage a fresh consumer directory to prove the new artifact works before switching the working project.

lessons.title: Build, install and inspect an offline collection
topics: Build, install and inspect an offline collection
lessons.body:
A standalone role is enough for one reusable policy. A collection gives related roles, modules and plugins a common namespace and version. Build a small collection from the role you already understand, then investigate a collection whose modules you will need on the storage desk.

## Build locally and consume by full name

Use the native **client shell**. Start in `~/rhce-ops`. The scaffold supplies galaxy.yml, a README and the default version 1.0.0. Check the version before building. The role files go inside the collection's roles directory.

```text
> mkdir -p src dist && ansible-galaxy collection init erudior.ops --init-path src
Galaxy creates src/erudior/ops.

> mkdir -p src/erudior/ops/roles && cp -r roles/desk_record src/erudior/ops/roles/
The collection source includes the tested role.

> ansible-galaxy collection build src/erudior/ops --output-path dist
The build creates dist/erudior-ops-1.0.0.tar.gz.

> cp dist/erudior-ops-1.0.0.tar.gz ~/rhce-consumer/dist/ && cd ~/rhce-consumer
The consumer now has a collection archive in addition to the standalone role.

> ansible-galaxy collection install ./dist/erudior-ops-1.0.0.tar.gz -p ./collections --offline
Galaxy installs erudior.ops under collections/ansible_collections.

> ansible-galaxy collection list -p ./collections erudior.ops
The project path and version 1.0.0 should appear together.
```

**collection.yml**

```yaml
---
- name: Issue records with the installed collection
  hosts: desks
  become: true
  gather_facts: false
  roles:
    - erudior.ops.desk_record
```

Run `ansible-playbook collection.yml`. The three-part role name selects the collection copy even though a standalone copy is also installed. Try an invented namespace in a temporary copy of the play and run its syntax check. The loader should report an unresolved role before connecting to a managed host.

## Stage the storage modules before disconnecting

Continue in `~/rhce-consumer`. Save the following requirements. These training pins require ansible-core 2.18 or later. Check `ansible --version` in the runtime being used. For an older native installation, stage a separate controller on a connected AlmaLinux 10 x86_64 machine with the same Python 3.12 interpreter. Run `python3 -m pip download --only-binary=:all: --dest wheels ansible-core==2.21.6` there and transfer the complete wheels directory. If pip is missing, install python3-pip from the signed DVD repositories. On the client run `python3 -m venv ~/rhce-core`, then `~/rhce-core/bin/python -m pip install --no-index --find-links wheels ansible-core==2.21.6`. Activate it in each new shell with `source ~/rhce-core/bin/activate`. Check `ansible --version` and use these tools for subsequent native plays. Keep the original system installation available for roles supplied by the RPM. Retain the versions and paths you actually used.

**requirements.yml**

```yaml
---
collections:
  - name: ansible.posix
    version: '2.2.2'
  - name: community.general
    version: '13.5.1'
```

```text
> ansible-galaxy collection download -r requirements.yml -p vendor
On a connected preparation system Galaxy downloads the pinned archives, dependencies and an offline requirements.yml.

> (cd vendor && ansible-galaxy collection install -r requirements.yml -p ../collections --offline)
On the client, local archives install into the consumer project. Copy the entire vendor directory first if you staged it elsewhere.

> ansible-doc --playbook-dir . community.general.filesystem
Find the meaning of force and the accepted filesystem types. Quit the pager with q.

> ansible-doc --playbook-dir . ansible.posix.mount
Compare mounted, present and ephemeral. Record which state changes both the live mount and the boot configuration.
```

From the release project's prepared execution environment, use `ansible-navigator collections` to inspect available collections. Run `ansible-navigator doc ansible.builtin.stat -m stdout` in the same runtime, locate the follow parameter and explain how a symbolic link changes the interpretation of a stat result. A project collection must be visible in the playbook's mounted workspace if the container will use it. Run the native play and the container's module lookup from their intended directories. Record a path and a version from each runtime. The lists can differ.

lessons.title: Reject a bad candidate and preserve the active record
topics: Reject a bad candidate and preserve the active record
lessons.body:
Dispatch just received an invalid shift. The operator needs three things from the play: keep the last accepted record, remove the candidate file, and return a failure to the release job. Merely printing a rescue message would let an upstream job treat a handled failure as success.

## Exercise the rejected path

Work in the consumer project after applying **collection.yml**. Capture the current digest on dispatch with `sha256sum /etc/erudior-record/owner`. In the play below, the block stages one public file. A failing assertion transfers control to rescue; the explicit fail reports rejection. The always section removes the transient file. A syntax error or an unreachable host cannot be handled like a failed task on a reachable machine.

**recover.yml**

```yaml
---
- name: Accept or reject an incoming shift
  hosts: dispatch
  become: true
  gather_facts: false
  vars:
    proposed_shift: day
    spool: /etc/erudior-record
  tasks:
    - name: Stage and check the candidate
      block:
        - name: Stage the proposed public record
          ansible.builtin.copy:
            content: "desk={{ inventory_hostname }}\nowner={{ proposed_shift }}\n"
            dest: "{{ spool }}/incoming"
            mode: '0600'

        - name: Accept only the supported shifts
          ansible.builtin.assert:
            that: proposed_shift in ['day', 'night']

        - name: Promote the checked candidate
          ansible.builtin.copy:
            src: "{{ spool }}/incoming"
            remote_src: true
            dest: "{{ spool }}/owner"
            owner: root
            group: root
            mode: '0644'

      rescue:
        - name: Report the failed step to the release operator
          ansible.builtin.fail:
            msg: "Release rejected in {{ ansible_failed_task.name }}. Inspect the active record."

      always:
        - name: Remove the temporary candidate
          ansible.builtin.file:
            path: "{{ spool }}/incoming"
            state: absent
```

```text
> ansible-playbook recover.yml -e proposed_shift=twilight
The validation task fails on dispatch, rescue reports rejection, cleanup runs, and the process returns a nonzero status.

> echo $?
A nonzero number if this immediately follows the rejected run.
```

On dispatch compare the active digest with the saved value, and run `sudo test ! -e /etc/erudior-record/incoming && echo clean`. Expect the same digest and clean. The archive desk received no tasks. Reapply with `-e proposed_shift=night` and inspect the active record. It should now say night. Reapply **collection.yml** to return dispatch to its normal policy.

## Read the recap in context

The staging play creates and removes a temporary file on every invocation. Its changed count can be positive even when the final bytes agree. Use the role play for the zero-change convergence test. For the rejected run record the failure status, omitted promotion, cleanup and protected live bytes. Describe what would happen if the network disappeared during the copy. An interrupted connection needs independent inspection on reconnection.

lessons.title: Independent practical: deliver a versioned duty collection
topics: Independent practical: deliver a versioned duty collection
lessons.body:
## Work order

You are the receiving operator. A teammate provides only the 1.0.0 collection tarball, a trusted digest, the project inventory and the two shift values. Start in a new project directory, outside the producer. Give dispatch the night record and archive the day record. Keep verified host keys and the authorized lab login. Do not edit either guest's active file to achieve the handoff.

1. Verify the archive against the handed-off digest and install it locally. Show the loaded collection path and version.
2. Author a new caller play using the collection-qualified role. Inspect both guests independently, including file modes, and save the results with the commit ID of the caller.
3. Submit an unsupported shift on dispatch. Keep its active checksum and the other guest unchanged. Show the candidate disappears and the release command reports failure.
4. Reapply the accepted caller twice. Explain the changes on each run and where the effective host values came from. Save enough instructions for a third operator to reproduce the release offline.

Score each row in the assignment against the observed states. Repeat only the failed work after you have recorded its cause. Restore day on dispatch and night on archive for the storage unit.

```assignment
lab: release-handoff-evidence
```

lessons.title: Identify the authorized disk before writing
topics: Identify the authorized disk before writing
lessons.body:
Dispatch needs a place to keep evidence files across reboots. Its system disk, two practice disks and installer media are all visible to Linux. A device name tells you how the kernel attached something on this boot. It does not authorize you to format it.

## Build the work order at the guest console

Use the course's disposable RHCE pair. The server guest is **dispatch**, the client guest is **archive**. Use the standard kit hostnames server and client for this unit. If you chose different names earlier, export the project and use a freshly prepared standard pair before provisioning. The guard checks the real hostname as well as the inventory alias. The kit attaches a 30 GiB operating-system disk followed by two 2 GiB practice disks. This exercise reserves the first practice disk on dispatch, **/dev/vdb**, for an ext4 file system. The second disk and the entire archive guest are outside the storage work order. Keep a saved baseline with your project exported before starting.

```text
> hostname -s
At the dispatch console expect server.

> sudo lsblk -b -o NAME,TYPE,SIZE,FSTYPE,LABEL,MOUNTPOINTS
```
