```text
Locate the system disk by its children and root mount. The first practice disk must be a whole disk of 2147483648 bytes.

> sudo wipefs --no-act /dev/vdb
On the fresh practice disk there are no signatures. Existing signatures require investigation.

> findmnt --mountpoint /srv/desk-evidence
On a fresh system this returns no matching mount and a nonzero status.
```

Also inspect `sudo ls -la /srv/desk-evidence` if the directory already exists. Mounting over a populated directory would hide its files. Inspect `/etc/fstab` for an earlier entry at this path. Preserve existing data and use a fresh disposable pair if the layout is ambiguous. Capture the second disk's signature listing as your negative control.

## Predict the decision

A disk with a child partition and an empty FSTYPE on the parent can still contain someone's data. A blank label on the whole disk is insufficient. Read the device tree, signature list and current mounts together. A peer presents **/dev/vdc**, blank and exactly 2 GiB: write one sentence explaining why it fails this work order. On a later run an ext4 label of ERUD_EVIDENCE is acceptable only when the host, device, original work order and purpose also agree. Record the resulting UUID on first provision and compare it on subsequent maintenance.

lessons.title: Mount the evidence volume and prove it survives a reboot
topics: Mount the evidence volume and prove it survives a reboot
lessons.body:
A live mount makes the directory usable now. A boot-time entry tells the next system how to reconstruct it. Dispatch needs both. Format the verified practice disk once, record its UUID, and let the play own its mount point.

## Apply on dispatch

From the consumer project, confirm the pinned collections are installed. On dispatch verify that `command -v mkfs.ext4 blkid wipefs lsblk` lists all four tools. If mkfs.ext4 is missing, install **e2fsprogs** from the two signed DVD repositories as in the package unit. Complete the guest-console identity checks in the preceding lesson before the first run. Do not apply this exercise to a workstation disk.

**storage.yml**

```yaml
---
- name: Provision the dedicated dispatch evidence disk
  hosts: dispatch
  become: true
  gather_facts: true
  vars:
    device: /dev/vdb
    evidence_mount: /srv/desk-evidence
  tasks:
    - name: Read the candidate and its children from the kernel
      ansible.builtin.command:
        argv: [lsblk, --bytes, --json, --output, NAME,TYPE,SIZE,FSTYPE,LABEL,MOUNTPOINTS, "{{ device }}"]
      register: disk_report
      changed_when: false
      check_mode: false

    - name: Read every signature known to wipefs without writing
      ansible.builtin.command:
        argv: [wipefs, --no-act, --noheadings, --output, TYPE, "{{ device }}"]
      register: signatures
      changed_when: false
      check_mode: false

    - name: Identify the authorized whole disk and existing state
      vars:
        disk: "{{ (disk_report.stdout | from_json).blockdevices | first }}"
      ansible.builtin.assert:
        that:
          - inventory_hostname == 'dispatch'
          - ansible_facts['hostname'] == 'server'
          - device == '/dev/vdb' and disk.name == 'vdb'
          - disk.type == 'disk' and disk.size | int == 2147483648
          - disk.children | default([]) | length == 0
          - (disk.mountpoints | reject('none') | list | difference([evidence_mount]) | length) == 0
          - >-
            ((signatures.stdout | trim == '') and (disk.fstype is none)) or
            ((signatures.stdout | trim == 'ext4') and disk.fstype == 'ext4' and disk.label == 'ERUD_EVIDENCE')
        fail_msg: "Identity or existing use differs from the practice order. Stop and inspect the guest."

    - name: Confirm the destination and any saved entry belong to this disk
      ansible.builtin.shell: |
        set -eu
        dev={{ device | quote }}
        target={{ evidence_mount | quote }}
        test ! -L "$target"
        if mountpoint -q "$target"; then
          test "$(findmnt -rn -M "$target" -o MAJ:MIN)" = "$(lsblk -dnro MAJ:MIN "$dev")"
        elif test -e "$target"; then
          test -d "$target"
          test -z "$(ls -A -- "$target")"
        fi
        saved=$(awk -v p="$target" '$1 !~ /^#/ && $2 == p {print $1}' /etc/fstab)
        if test -n "$saved"; then
          uuid=$(blkid -s UUID -o value "$dev")
          test "$saved" = "UUID=$uuid"
        fi
      changed_when: false
      check_mode: false

    - name: Create the exercise file system on the verified disk
      community.general.filesystem:
        dev: "{{ device }}"
        fstype: ext4
        opts: -L ERUD_EVIDENCE
        force: false

    - name: Read its stable filesystem identity
      ansible.builtin.command:
        argv: [blkid, -s, UUID, -o, value, "{{ device }}"]
      register: fs_uuid
      changed_when: false

    - name: Mount now and record the boot-time mount
      ansible.posix.mount:
        path: "{{ evidence_mount }}"
        src: "UUID={{ fs_uuid.stdout | trim }}"
        fstype: ext4
        opts: defaults
        dump: '0'
        passno: '2'
        state: mounted
```

On the client run `ansible-playbook storage.yml --list-hosts` and `ansible-playbook storage.yml --syntax-check`. Expect only dispatch. Run the play live. A first-run check-mode preview cannot discover the UUID of a file system that has not been created yet. Use the read-only preflight for a fresh disk.

```text
> findmnt --mountpoint /srv/desk-evidence -o TARGET,SOURCE,FSTYPE
Run on dispatch. The exact mount point names the dedicated block device and ext4.

> sudo blkid -s UUID -o value /dev/vdb
Record the UUID. Find the same UUID and destination in /etc/fstab.

> findmnt --verify --verbose
Inspect the saved mount table and resolve any reported errors before a reboot.
```

Reapply. An unchanged file system and mount should both report ok. Leave a uniquely named marker on the mounted disk, capture its checksum and the guest's boot ID. Reboot dispatch using its console. Before applying again, compare boot IDs, mount source, UUID and marker checksum. An ordinary directory at the same path could also hold a marker; the mount identity is part of the evidence. If the reboot check fails, use the console, inspect the saved entry and the mount unit's journal, and return to the saved practice baseline when needed.

lessons.title: Archive a single record and prove it can be restored
topics: Archive a single record and prove it can be restored
lessons.body:
A completed archive command is only half of a backup. The next operator must be able to recover the intended file, and an interrupted write must leave the last good archive readable. The dispatch record is public in this exercise. The Vault token from the collector unit is outside the archive's scope.

## Trace a small shell worker

In the consumer project, save this script under **files**. It will run on dispatch as root. Before installing it, predict the behavior if the disk is unmounted, the source is missing, or verification of the candidate fails.

**files/save-record**

```bash
#!/bin/bash
set -euo pipefail
umask 077
dst=/srv/desk-evidence
/usr/bin/mountpoint -q "$dst"
tmp=$(/usr/bin/mktemp "$dst/.owner.XXXXXXXX")
trap 'rm -f -- "$tmp"' EXIT
/usr/bin/tar -czf "$tmp" -C /etc/erudior-record owner
/usr/bin/tar -tzf "$tmp" >/dev/null
/usr/bin/mv -f -- "$tmp" "$dst/owner.tar.gz"
```

The mount check prevents writes into the system disk underneath an absent mount. A unique temporary file in the destination directory keeps incomplete bytes away from the stable name. A successful rename on the same file system replaces the old name atomically. The restrictive umask protects new files. tar changes to the source directory, so the stored member is the relative name **owner**. The exit trap removes a leftover temporary file, including after an ordinary command failure.

From `~/rhce-consumer`, run `ansible dispatch -b -m ansible.builtin.copy -a 'src=files/save-record dest=/usr/local/sbin/erudior-save-record owner=root group=root mode=0755'`. On dispatch, execute the worker, list the members and extract into a new temporary directory.

```text
> sudo /usr/local/sbin/erudior-save-record
Success is silent. The stable archive should now exist on the evidence disk.

> sudo tar -tzf /srv/desk-evidence/owner.tar.gz
The listing contains exactly owner.

> restore_dir=$(mktemp -d)
A new empty private directory is available for the restore exercise.

> sudo tar -xzf /srv/desk-evidence/owner.tar.gz -C "$restore_dir"
The named member is now present inside the temporary directory.

> sudo cmp "$restore_dir/owner" /etc/erudior-record/owner && echo verified
verified indicates that the restored and source bytes match at this point.
```

Now read the script again as a change reviewer. Which line prevents a partial replacement? Which line would stop the worker before it even creates a temporary file? Repeating a backup creates new archive output by design. Running the play that installs the worker should converge independently of how often the job executes.

## Deliver a one-time handoff with an Ansible module

The timer needs a local worker so it can operate with the controller powered off. For an operator-requested snapshot, the controller can also invoke the archive module on dispatch. Its single-file default can produce a compressed stream; force_archive requests a tar container so a receiver can enumerate and restore members. Use a separate destination so the scheduled recovery copy remains available.

**archive-once.yml**

```yaml
---
- name: Package the accepted record for an operator
  hosts: dispatch
  become: true
  gather_facts: false
  tasks:
    - name: Require the exact evidence mount before writing
      ansible.builtin.command: mountpoint -q /srv/desk-evidence
      changed_when: false
      check_mode: false

    - name: Create a tar archive containing one record on dispatch
      community.general.archive:
        path: /etc/erudior-record/owner
        dest: /srv/desk-evidence/handoff.tar.gz
        format: gz
        force_archive: true
        owner: root
        group: root
        mode: '0600'
```

Apply with `ansible-playbook archive-once.yml`. At the dispatch console use `sudo tar -tzf /srv/desk-evidence/handoff.tar.gz` to inspect the member name. Expect **owner**. Recover it with `sudo tar -xOzf /srv/desk-evidence/handoff.tar.gz owner | cmp - /etc/erudior-record/owner && echo verified`. Explain on which host the source and result live and why this on-demand archive alone cannot fulfill the daily schedule.

lessons.title: Schedule the archive and inspect the worker result
topics: Schedule the archive and inspect the worker result
lessons.body:
The handoff says “save daily at 18:15 UTC, including recovery after downtime.” A systemd timer starts a oneshot service. The service owns the command and its exit status. The timer owns the calendar and boot enablement. The manual service run below lets you verify the action without waiting for the next scheduled event.

**files/desk-save.service**

```ini
[Unit]
Description=Archive the current shift record
RequiresMountsFor=/srv/desk-evidence

[Service]
Type=oneshot
ExecStart=/usr/local/sbin/erudior-save-record
```
**files/desk-save.timer**

```ini
[Unit]
Description=Save the dispatch record daily

[Timer]
OnCalendar=*-*-* 18:15:00 UTC
Persistent=true

[Install]
WantedBy=timers.target
```
**schedule.yml**

```yaml
---
- name: Install the dispatch archive job
  hosts: dispatch
  become: true
  gather_facts: false
  tasks:
    - name: Publish the worker and unit files
      ansible.builtin.copy:
        src: "{{ item.src }}"
        dest: "{{ item.dest }}"
        owner: root
        group: root
        mode: "{{ item.mode }}"
      loop:
        - {src: save-record, dest: /usr/local/sbin/erudior-save-record, mode: '0755'}
        - {src: desk-save.service, dest: /etc/systemd/system/desk-save.service, mode: '0644'}
        - {src: desk-save.timer, dest: /etc/systemd/system/desk-save.timer, mode: '0644'}
      notify: Refresh the timer

    - name: Load changed definitions before checking timer state
      ansible.builtin.meta: flush_handlers

    - name: Ensure the timer is active and enabled
      ansible.builtin.systemd_service:
        name: desk-save.timer
        enabled: true
        state: started

  handlers:
    - name: Refresh the timer
      ansible.builtin.systemd_service:
        name: desk-save.timer
        daemon_reload: true
        state: restarted
```

Keep all three files from this and the previous lesson under the same project **files/** directory. Run `ansible-playbook schedule.yml` from the client. A change to a unit notifies the handler; its reload makes systemd read the new file and its restart makes the timer use the new schedule. The final task restores an inactive or disabled timer even when no source file has changed.

```text
> systemd-analyze calendar '*-*-* 18:15:00 UTC'
On dispatch the normalized expression and next occurrence identify the schedule.

> systemctl list-timers --all desk-save.timer
The NEXT and UNIT columns identify the loaded timer. Displayed times can use the guest's local time zone.

> sudo systemctl start desk-save.service
The oneshot runs to completion. A subsequent inactive state can be normal.

> systemctl show desk-save.service -p Result -p ExecMainStatus
Expect Result=success and ExecMainStatus=0 after the manual run.

> sudo journalctl -u desk-save.service -n 12 --no-pager
The journal shows the service invocation; check the archive separately.
```

Persistent=true catches up a missed calendar activation when the timer becomes active again. Several missed intervals can produce a single catch-up. It is still possible for the worker to fail. Record the timer's enabled and active states, then recover the actual member and verify its bytes. If the service reports a permission error, check file mode, executable path and the SELinux context with `ls -Z`. Use `matchpathcon -V /usr/local/sbin/erudior-save-record` to test the policy default and `sudo restorecon -v /usr/local/sbin/erudior-save-record` if the label drifted. Keep enforcement enabled.

lessons.title: Independent practical: recover the evidence desk
topics: Independent practical: recover the evidence desk
lessons.body:
## Work order

Dispatch reports that backups stopped after maintenance. Preserve its most recent verified archive while returning the daily timer to service. Start with a working archive and note its digest, the member digest, the evidence disk UUID, both guests' boot IDs and the second disk's signatures.

1. On dispatch stop and disable only **desk-save.timer**. From the controller establish whether the timer, service definition, or storage failed. A manual invocation that succeeds while the timer is disabled narrows the problem.
2. Repair drift through the schedule play. Show a zero-change repeat, the loaded UTC expression, and a successful manual service invocation. Restore the member into a new directory and verify its contents.
3. With the timer temporarily stopped and the archive known good, rename only the disposable source record to **owner.held** on dispatch. Invoke the worker. Save the nonzero result and show the existing archive's digest is unchanged. Restore the source name immediately, reapply the accepted plays and repeat the restore check.
4. Reboot dispatch. Show a new boot ID, the same UUID mounted at the exact destination, and a live enabled timer before applying a repair. Archive's boot ID, its duty file and the spare practice disk must still match the baseline.

Submit the diagnosis and the evidence table. A saved unit file alone cannot demonstrate a working schedule; a readable archive alone cannot establish that tomorrow's timer will fire.

```assignment
lab: evidence-handoff-evidence
```

lessons.title: Final practical A: build the replacement desks
topics: Final practical A: build the replacement desks
lessons.body:
## Independent practical A · Build the replacement desks

Allow 100 minutes for this Erudior exercise. Use a fresh disposable pair with the RHCE kit profile. Export your project, dependency archives, trusted release digests and encrypted practice values **outside both guests** before resetting a pair. Keep lab-only SSH keys outside Git. Verify the new guests' SSH host keys from their consoles, establish authorized learner access and configure both inventory aliases. Restore your controller workspace from the exported repository. Provide the DVD repositories, local collection archives and pre-staged runtime from the earlier units. The practice remote from the Git unit lives on dispatch, so resetting the pair also removes it. Before the reset, in the client’s Git checkout use `git bundle create handoff.bundle --all` and export the bundle off the guests. After reset copy it to the server as learner, run `mkdir -p ~/repos` and `git clone --bare /path/to/handoff.bundle ~/repos/handoff.git` there, substituting the saved bundle path. On the client use the verified SSH route to clone `learner@192.168.77.10:repos/handoff.git` into a fresh project. Compare its commit with the pre-reset ID. For multiple repositories repeat the bundle/restore per project. Start without the previous managed configuration.

The operations lead wants dispatch to publish a green status report on the private link. Archive must keep the night record while dispatch owns the day record. The collector must read its credential after reboot. Both desks must be reproducible from a named Git commit.

| Deliverable | Acceptance evidence |
| --- | --- |
| Reviewed source | Work from a fresh clone, record its commit, inventory graph and each verified host identity. In VS Code edit and commit one public policy value on a branch, push it to the practice remote and run the review play in the prepared development container. |
| Reusable policy | Install the versioned duty collection locally. Use its role on both desks. Run a native play and a play with Navigator in the appropriate staged runtime. Report each runtime and use its local documentation to identify one module parameter. |
| Dispatch service | Use package, repository, file, handler and service tasks to deploy /erudior-status.txt with HTTP 200, the exact line desk=dispatch ending in a newline, X-Erudior-Release set to green and X-Erudior-Team set to support. Verify the complete expected page locally and from the private client. Open HTTP only in the intended zone. Preserve existing SSH access and the other zone's baseline. |
| Service identity | Use erucollect with shell /sbin/nologin and primary group eruread, root:eruread mode 0750 on /etc/erudior-collector and 0640 on both policy.json and token. Set desk to dispatch and interval_seconds to the integer 90. Render its public policy, deploy a made-up Vault-protected value and verify that the identity can read it while an unrelated account cannot. Use the Collector acceptance checks reference: run `bash ~/check-collector 90` and perform its hidden-input comparison as erucollect against the intended disposable token, including its final newline. Repeat both checks after reboot before reapplying the play. Keep the evidence free of secret values. |
| Persistence and repeatability | Reboot dispatch. Before applying, verify a new boot ID and test the actual consumers again. Compare both records on the correct guests. Reapply the desired-state plays and capture a zero-change recap. |

Your submission is the reproducible project revision and a redacted record of observations. Use the EX294 evidence map for the matching prerequisite lessons after attempting the work. The knowledge quiz checks your interpretation of evidence. The assignment records practical performance separately.

```assignment
lab: final-build-evidence
```

lessons.title: Final practical B: recover the evidence desk
topics: Final practical B: recover the evidence desk
lessons.body:
## Independent practical B · Recover the evidence desk

Allow 75 minutes. Start with a second fresh target or a restored snapshot made before storage was provisioned. Supply verified controller dependencies, the two authorized inventory identities, the collection, and a known-good duty record on each desk. Keep the score for this form separate from the service-build exercise.

A work order reserves the first blank 2 GiB practice disk on dispatch. The spare disk and archive guest must be untouched. Dispatch must archive its own record at 18:15 UTC, keep the old good archive on a failed run, and recover without a manual mount or timer restart after reboot.

1. Collect evidence for the disk decision and the excluded resources. Build an ext4 volume labelled **ERUD_EVIDENCE** on the approved device. Mount it by UUID at **/srv/desk-evidence** now and at boot.
2. Install a worker, service and persistent timer from versioned source. Produce an archive containing only the relative member **owner**. Restore it in an empty directory and compare bytes with the accepted record. With the timer paused, reproduce one failed worker run as in the evidence handoff. Compare the stable archive digest before and after, then restore the source and timer.
3. Reject a deliberately unsupported shift through the play's failure path. Record the prior and resulting active-file digests, the nonzero status and removal of the transient candidate. Explain the different response if SSH itself is unavailable.
4. Stop and disable the timer as the controlled fault. Diagnose it from the guest and repair it with the same play. Verify a zero-change repeat. Reboot dispatch and verify storage, timer, archive restore, SSH and exclusion boundaries before running any repair.

Submit the project commit, a before/after record with boot IDs, the first failed observation, its cause, and a short handoff explaining how to restore the last good copy. The practical rubric awards points for independent evidence on the correct machines. Use your returned work to repeat the failed criteria on another clean target.

```assignment
lab: final-repair-evidence
```

banks.title: Ansible foundations and applied automation
banks.description: Knowledge checks assess interpretation of automation and target evidence. Practical assignments use their own observation-based rubrics.

sections.name: Software sources, packages, services and handlers
Release reusable automation and recover from failure
Provision storage, archive records and schedule recovery

questions.topic: Translate a support ticket into a testable state
questions.stem: A replacement server has just arrived. Which deliverable most directly helps the next shift reproduce the original configuration?
choices: A saved playbook and its source file, with the desired owner, group and mode specified
An SSH session transcript that ends with “success”
The original server’s running process list
questions.explanation: The next shift can run the saved instructions against the replacement and check the resulting state. A transcript may explain how someone worked, but a success message records no required state.

questions.topic: Translate a support ticket into a testable state
questions.stem: Two runs leave two identical shift lines where the work order calls for exactly one. Which condition failed?
choices: The server must have refused privilege escalation.
The update failed to converge on the requested contents.
The inventory must contain the same host twice.
questions.explanation: Appending another line changes the file each time. The requested state is one line after the first run and after every later run.

questions.topic: Translate a support ticket into a testable state
questions.stem: You are installing software on the two lab guests. Which arrangement supports the planned job?
choices: A Git server on each guest and no Python on the server
Ansible on the server only and the private key on both machines
Ansible on the client, with SSH access to a usable Python interpreter on the server
questions.explanation: The client interprets the play. The managed server accepts the connection and runs the Python modules used in this unit.

questions.topic: Prove who is on each end of SSH
questions.stem: The server VM was rebuilt. SSH now presents a changed host key at its old address. What evidence identifies the replacement?
choices: The old entry in authorized_keys on the client
A matching fingerprint obtained through the new server’s trusted console
The learner account password still works on the client
questions.explanation: A host key identifies the SSH server. A comparison with the independent console distinguishes an expected rebuild from a connection to the wrong machine.

questions.topic: Prove who is on each end of SSH
questions.stem: A batch-mode SSH login prints learner. A separate sudo id -u is denied. Which layer needs investigation?
choices: Authorization for the remote learner to use sudo
The private virtual network address
Whether the SSH transport can reach port 22
questions.explanation: The login already ran a command as learner. The refusal came later, when sudo evaluated that account’s privileges.

questions.topic: Prove who is on each end of SSH
questions.stem: The server uses a key-only cloud image. What should its learner account receive through the VM console?
choices: The client’s SSH agent socket
The client’s passphrase-protected private key
The public line from erudior_rhce.pub in authorized_keys
questions.explanation: The server stores public keys authorized for that account. Proof of possession comes from the private key, which stays on the controller.

questions.topic: Select the right machines before running a task
questions.stem: Ansible warns that the host pattern did not match. What is the most informative next step?
choices: Retry with sudo on the control node
Inspect the active configuration path and inventory graph, then list the intended group
Install the ping module on the managed node
questions.explanation: Pattern resolution happens on the controller before a remote task can start. Confirm its data source and which host aliases the group contains.

questions.topic: Select the right machines before running a task
questions.stem: The graph lists node1 beneath ops. The private IP changes. What edit preserves the play’s target expression?
choices: Change the ansible_host value for node1 and verify the host key at the new destination
Replace hosts: ops in every play with the old IP address
Rename the controller to ops
questions.explanation: The inventory alias and group describe a logical target. ansible_host gives SSH the address. A move still calls for verification of the remote identity.

questions.topic: Select the right machines before running a task
questions.stem: ansible ops -m ansible.builtin.ping returns pong. What still needs a separate test?
choices: Whether ops exists anywhere in the parsed inventory
Whether the managed node could run this Python module
Whether the remote account can install a root-owned file under /etc
questions.explanation: The ping module ran as the login user. Nothing in that successful task requested privileged access.

questions.topic: Deploy the shift notice and repair drift
questions.stem: Check mode reports changed=1 and the server path is still absent. What follows for the copy task?
choices: Investigate a missing write before trying a live run
Run the play without --check to apply the predicted change
Add the same task a second time and rerun in check mode
questions.explanation: This module predicts a change without writing the destination in check mode. A live run is required to create the file.

questions.topic: Deploy the shift notice and repair drift
questions.stem: The remote bytes already match, but the mode is 0600. What should the guided play do?
choices: Correct the mode to 0644, then report no further change on the next run
Report zero changes because file bytes match
Remove the file because its current mode is unexpected
questions.explanation: The task declares metadata as well as content. The access mode is part of the requested state.

questions.topic: Deploy the shift notice and repair drift
questions.stem: The controller reports that it cannot find files/shift.conf. Where should you inspect first?
choices: The /etc directory on node1
The server login user’s home directory
The playbook project and its files directory on the controller
questions.explanation: By default copy reads src on the controller. A remote destination path can be correct even when the controller-side source is missing.

questions.topic: Independent practical: the morning handoff
questions.stem: Which observation demonstrates that the handoff file survived a reboot?
choices: A green check-mode run before reboot
A different boot ID and correct remote bytes and permissions before reapplying
A successful repair play run immediately after startup followed by a correct file
questions.explanation: Comparing boot IDs proves a new kernel boot occurred. Inspecting state before remediation distinguishes persistence from a fresh repair.

questions.topic: Independent practical: the morning handoff
questions.stem: cat shows queue=morning on screen, yet the exact-byte comparison fails. What could explain it?
choices: The final newline is missing.
The owning group is root.
The inventory name is an alias.
questions.explanation: Two files can look alike on the terminal but differ by a newline. cmp checks bytes. Ownership and inventory naming cannot alter those bytes.

questions.topic: Independent practical: the morning handoff
questions.stem: Your morning play works, but the evening file now contains the morning queue. Which acceptance requirement catches this?
choices: Checking that the morning playbook parses
Recording only changed=0 on a second run
Comparing both files with their own expected contents and modes
questions.explanation: Idempotence can preserve the wrong state too. Checking the earlier evening contract exposes unintended effects outside the new work order.

questions.topic: Hand a reproducible project to a teammate
questions.stem: You stage a playbook, then fix a typo in the working file and commit without staging it again. Which version enters the commit?
choices: The file at the moment it was staged
The file as it looked when push was run
Both versions in two commits
questions.explanation: A commit snapshots the index. The later fix remains in the working tree until it is staged and committed.

questions.topic: Hand a reproducible project to a teammate
questions.stem: Why initialize a bare Git repository on the operations server for this lab?
choices: To start a play automatically on every push
To receive and serve versioned history without a checked-out project
To make a local uncommitted file visible to peers
questions.explanation: The SSH remote stores Git objects and branch pointers. Deploying a play requires a separate action.

questions.topic: Hand a reproducible project to a teammate
questions.stem: Which file can another checkout use to verify the identity of the lab server?
choices: A copy of the controller’s private key
A file containing the sudo password
ssh/known_hosts containing the verified public host key
questions.explanation: The public host key can be checked against a trusted console fingerprint and shared. The user’s private key stays under their control.

questions.topic: Identify the Ansible runtime that will execute your play
questions.stem: A colleague pulled the image with sudo. Navigator as learner uses pull policy never and cannot find it. What should the colleague try first?
choices: Disable SSH host-key checking
Inspect the learner’s rootless Podman store and pull or load the specified image there
Install Ansible on node1
questions.explanation: The launcher uses the image store for its operating-system user. SSH and the managed node have not been reached.

questions.topic: Identify the Ansible runtime that will execute your play
questions.stem: Which observation identifies the version of ansible-core that will interpret the play inside the selected EE?
choices: The result of ansible-navigator exec -- ansible --version
The Git release tag of the playbook project
The hostname printed on the managed node
questions.explanation: The exec subcommand runs a program inside the configured execution environment. The launcher and remote node report different software.

questions.topic: Identify the Ansible runtime that will execute your play
questions.stem: A teammate reports the same tag, but a different manifest digest for the same architecture. What first needs to be established?
choices: Whether the managed node accepts sudo
Whether the staging area is empty
Which image manifest each machine actually has
questions.explanation: A tag can be reassigned. The digest identifies an exact manifest. Compare image identity before attributing the difference to the playbook.

questions.topic: Prove a fresh checkout can deploy the release
questions.stem: The play works in the author’s tree. In a fresh clone, copy cannot find files/release.txt. Which check best tests the most direct explanation?
choices: List the project’s tracked files at the tested commit
Restart the server’s SSH service
Run the same task as root
questions.explanation: A local source can remain untracked in the author’s tree. A clone contains only content in the fetched history.

questions.topic: Prove a fresh checkout can deploy the release
questions.stem: A containerized preview reports changed for node1. How can you distinguish a prediction from actual delivery?
choices: Only check the playbook syntax
Inspect the path on the server before the live run, then compare the remote bytes after applying
Compare the two controller directories
questions.explanation: A check-mode prediction can occur while the destination is still absent. Reading the managed node after a live run supplies independent evidence.

questions.topic: Prove a fresh checkout can deploy the release
questions.stem: Why can this task deliver the alpha notice without become?
choices: A rootless container grants root privileges on every SSH target
A Git commit grants remote write access
The learner login owns the destination home directory and can create this file
questions.explanation: The remote account’s filesystem permissions decide whether the write succeeds. The local image user and Git history cannot grant remote rights.

questions.topic: Author and run an inspection play in VS Code
questions.stem: Your new VS Code terminal reports /workspaces/rhce, and the play recap says node1. Where did the stat task examine the file?
choices: Inside the editor container
On the node matched by the ops inventory group
On the workstation that draws the editor window
questions.explanation: The playbook process starts in the editor container. Its hosts pattern directs the stat module to the managed server.

questions.topic: Author and run an inspection play in VS Code
questions.stem: Inside the development container, ssh-add -l reports no loaded identities. The project contains the trusted host key. What should you check next?
choices: The client’s dedicated agent socket and whether the lab key is loaded
Whether the target file is mode 0644
Whether you have pushed the editor settings
questions.explanation: The host key authenticates the server. A loaded user identity in the mounted agent is needed for the client side of login.

questions.topic: Author and run an inspection play in VS Code
questions.stem: After pushing review/beta, the remote main still points to alpha. Why is this expected?
choices: The container wrote only to RAM
Git drops a playbook if it has no changed tasks
A push to a separate branch updates that reference without moving main
questions.explanation: Both branch names can refer to different commits. Promotion of main is a separate, deliberate step.

questions.topic: Independent practical: promote a tested revision
questions.stem: A teammate pushes another commit onto review/beta while you test. Which ID should main represent after the promotion you can justify?
choices: Whichever review commit is newest at the time you push
The exact commit whose play and resulting state passed your checks
The previous alpha commit in all cases
questions.explanation: Evidence applies to a specific revision. If a newer revision is desired, test it before promoting it.

questions.topic: Independent practical: promote a tested revision
questions.stem: The diff predicts alpha will become beta. Which observation belongs immediately after preview and before applying?
choices: The server still has the exact alpha line
Main already points to the beta commit
The remote path is absent
questions.explanation: The previous live release was alpha. Check mode should leave those bytes in place while describing the candidate change.

questions.topic: Independent practical: promote a tested revision
questions.stem: A fast-forward-only promotion is refused after main and the candidate diverged. How should the operator proceed?
choices: Discard the remote main reference
Mark the earlier preview as evidence for the combined history
Fetch, inspect both histories, reconcile on a review branch and test the resulting commit
questions.explanation: The refusal preserves changes on each branch. Reconciliation produces a new revision that needs its own verification.

questions.topic: Give two managed hosts different policies
questions.stem: The OS hostname is server, but its inventory name is dispatch. Which file supplies a host-specific pager setting in this project?
choices: host_vars/dispatch.yml
group_vars/server.yml
host_vars/192.168.77.10.yml
questions.explanation: The host_vars plugin looks up the inventory alias. The connection address and the hostname gathered after login serve different purposes.

questions.topic: Give two managed hosts different policies
questions.stem: Both desks inherit desk_shift: day. Only archive has desk_shift: night in host_vars. What will the play normally see?
choices: Night on both because archive was defined last
Day on dispatch and night on archive
A conflict that prevents inventory parsing
questions.explanation: The host-specific value takes precedence over its group value for archive. Dispatch keeps the group setting.

questions.topic: Give two managed hosts different policies
questions.stem: You inspect archive with a day-shift extra variable, then repeat the inspection without it. Why does night return?
choices: The server rebooted and restored its hostname
The inventory plugin wrote a second YAML file
The extra variable applied only to the first invocation
questions.explanation: A command-line override can change a resolved value for that invocation. It does not edit the inventory source.

questions.topic: Separate requested policy from observed state
questions.stem: Dispatch has desk_pager: true and prior_pager.stat.exists is false. What do those two values establish?
choices: The play reached archive by mistake
The host requests a pager notice and the inspected path is absent
Ansible cannot use authentication on this host
questions.explanation: Inventory describes the desired duty. The stat result measures the current path. The mismatch is well-defined work for a later task.

questions.topic: Separate requested policy from observed state
questions.stem: The assertion rejects desk_pager even though the screen shows the word false. Which input explains the rejection?
choices: desk_pager: 'false'
desk_pager: false
A false stat.exists field
questions.explanation: Quoted false is a string. The is boolean assertion accepts actual booleans, including false, and rejects strings.

questions.topic: Separate requested policy from observed state
questions.stem: A stat task registers prior_pager on both guests. Dispatch has the file and archive does not. What should each host see in the next task?
choices: The result from whichever SSH request finished last
One shared result combining the paths from both guests
Its own prior_pager.stat.exists value
questions.explanation: Ansible associates registered task results with each inventory host during the run. The two observations can legitimately differ.

questions.topic: Deploy and repair a list of files
questions.stem: For archive on night shift and the roster item, which controller source does the copy task select?
choices: files/roster-night.txt
files/archive-roster.txt
files/board-night.txt
questions.explanation: The source expression combines the current item’s name with the effective shift for this host.

questions.topic: Deploy and repair a list of files
questions.stem: One copy task changes board and roster on dispatch. The other tasks only read state. What change count should the dispatch recap report?
choices: Two because two files changed
One because a single looped task had changed iterations
Zero because the changes were inside a loop
questions.explanation: The play recap counts changed tasks. Inspect the registered per-item results to see both affected files.

questions.topic: Deploy and repair a list of files
questions.stem: Only the dispatch roster changed, and its text is identical to yesterday’s. What evidence would most directly explain that change?
choices: The printed operating-system distribution on archive
The number of names in the desks group
The old and requested file mode for that iteration
questions.explanation: A copy task also manages the declared mode. Correct content with incorrect metadata is still drift.

questions.topic: Make both branches reach the requested state
questions.stem: A task creates a pager file only when desk_pager is true. Why does a notice remain after the desk goes off call?
choices: A skipped creation task leaves the existing file in place
Changing a boolean always triggers a reboot
Ansible can only delete files that Git tracks
questions.explanation: The play needs an explicit off-call branch that declares the notice absent.

questions.topic: Make both branches reach the requested state
questions.stem: On an off-call host, pager_before.stat.exists is false. How is the two-condition removal task evaluated?
choices: It runs because the first condition is true
It is skipped because the list requires both conditions to be true
It fails because false is not a valid stat result
questions.explanation: The notice is already absent. The first condition is satisfied and the observed-existence condition is false.

questions.topic: Make both branches reach the requested state
questions.stem: A directory is unexpectedly found at the course pager path. What outcome does the supplied pager task list produce?
choices: It turns the directory into a pager file
It deletes the directory and records one change
It fails the file-type assertion before either pager branch acts
questions.explanation: The stat result identifies the unexpected object. The type check protects that path while the operator investigates.

questions.topic: Independent practical: rotate duty across two desks
questions.stem: Which first live step maintains pager assignment while transferring duty from dispatch to archive?
choices: Apply the incoming archive change and verify its notice while dispatch is still on call
Remove the dispatch notice and wait before applying archive
Use check mode on archive and treat its predicted new notice as available
questions.explanation: Bringing the incoming desk on call first provides a verifiable overlap. A preview does not create a live notice.

questions.topic: Independent practical: rotate duty across two desks
questions.stem: A two-host run rejects archive’s invalid boolean at the shared preflight. What evidence demonstrates the requested failure behavior?
choices: The inventory graph contains both hosts
The run fails at validation and independent checks still match the entire starting state on both guests
The controller source files have a recent modification time
questions.explanation: A validation message identifies the rejection. Comparing the remote states demonstrates the attempted change had no effect on either desk.

questions.topic: Independent practical: rotate duty across two desks
questions.stem: The full play now reports zero changes. Which independent observations establish success for the final work order?
choices: Both hosts are reachable and both have a pager file
The playbook parses and Git reports a clean tree
Dispatch checks as night/off and archive as day/on, with exact file bytes, ownership and modes
questions.explanation: Repeatability can preserve an incorrect policy. Testing each guest against the requested outcomes establishes that the stable state is also the right one.

questions.topic: Define trusted software sources for dispatch
questions.stem: The repository preview reports a change. What should you see on a fresh dispatch before the live apply?
choices: Two installed httpd RPMs
No course repository file on disk
A running Apache service
questions.explanation: The repository task in check mode predicts the new definitions. Verify absence on dispatch before making the live change.

questions.topic: Define trusted software sources for dispatch
questions.stem: Both course repository sections have enabled=0. How can the package lab use them?
choices: Select their repository IDs explicitly for the DNF transaction
Disable RPM signature checking
Copy the RPM database from the Ansible client
questions.explanation: A transaction can enable specific configured entries temporarily while their on-disk defaults remain disabled.

questions.topic: Define trusted software sources for dispatch
questions.stem: A repository responds successfully, but the RPM signature cannot be verified. What should the operator investigate?
choices: Whether httpd starts at boot
Whether the playbook uses enough forks
The RPM source and the AlmaLinux key trusted by the guest
questions.explanation: Reachability confirms a network path. Signature verification also depends on a trusted signing key and authentic package bytes.

questions.topic: Install a package from the approved repositories
questions.stem: The work order asks for httpd to be installed. The existing version satisfies that policy. Which declaration fits?
choices: state: absent
state: latest
state: present
questions.explanation: Present declares that a package must exist. A newer candidate in a catalog does not by itself require a change.

questions.topic: Install a package from the approved repositories
questions.stem: The package is missing from the restricted candidate list. Which observation comes first?
choices: Which repositories are enabled for this query and whether AppStream offers httpd
The web service’s process ID
The owner of the status page
questions.explanation: DNF resolves candidates using the repositories participating in the transaction. A web process and document root can be examined separately after installation.

questions.topic: Install a package from the approved repositories
questions.stem: After install, rpm -q succeeds, and systemctl reports disabled and inactive. What does the evidence support?
choices: A signature check failed
The package is installed and the service still needs its runtime and boot policies
The server will serve the page after any reboot
questions.explanation: Installing RPMs, starting a process and enabling a unit are distinct changes.

questions.topic: Trace a request through systemd and Apache
questions.stem: The checker requests 127.0.0.1 from an SSH session on dispatch. Which machine receives the HTTP request?
choices: The SSH client workstation
Dispatch, through its own loopback interface
Every host in the web inventory group
questions.explanation: The HTTP client runs inside the remote shell. Its loopback address belongs to dispatch.

questions.topic: Trace a request through systemd and Apache
questions.stem: An extra directive passed to httpd -t -C is unknown. Why can an ordinary httpd -t immediately afterward succeed?
choices: The extra directive applied only to the first parser invocation
Every parser failure removes all conf.d files
The failed test restarted the service with defaults
questions.explanation: The command-line directive exercised the parser without altering the installed configuration.

questions.topic: Trace a request through systemd and Apache
questions.stem: The unit is active but disabled. What can you conclude from those two observations?
choices: Its response already has the green release header
Every later boot will start it automatically
It runs now, while enablement for the normal boot target is absent
questions.explanation: Active describes its current state. Disabled describes its native enablement setting. Check actual boot behavior with a reboot and an independent probe.

questions.topic: Reload Apache when its configuration changes
questions.stem: Two separate header-file tasks change on dispatch and notify Reload Apache before a single flush. How many times should that handler run there?
choices: Twice, once per file
Once for dispatch at that flush
Once for each incoming HTTP connection
questions.explanation: Repeated notifications for one handler on a host are combined before the next flush.

questions.topic: Reload Apache when its configuration changes
questions.stem: An operator changes only the static status page. Which repair should appear when the play runs?
choices: A package upgrade followed by a reboot
Two changed header files and a reload
One changed page copy, followed by a successful probe without a reload
questions.explanation: Apache can serve the repaired file on the next request. The page task does not notify the configuration handler.

questions.topic: Reload Apache when its configuration changes
questions.stem: Why place flush_handlers before the live HTTP check?
choices: To make a queued reload take effect before evaluating the new headers
To write the new inventory variables into the RPM database
To suppress all subsequent HTTP requests
questions.explanation: With a pending reload, disk configuration and the running response can temporarily describe different releases.

questions.topic: Independent practical: promote and recover the status service
questions.stem: Check mode predicts green header files. Which independent result should still pass immediately afterward?
choices: A live green/support response
A blue/operations response from dispatch
A connection to port 80 on the Ansible client
questions.explanation: The preview predicts disk and handler changes. The blue response remains live until the change is actually applied.

questions.topic: Independent practical: promote and recover the status service
questions.stem: With valid green header files already in place, someone stops and disables httpd. Which action repairs both faults?
choices: The systemd task that requests state started and enabled true
Editing the release color a second time
Rerunning only the repository definition
questions.explanation: The ordinary service task controls current and boot state on every application. Existing valid header files need no reload to start the service.

questions.topic: Independent practical: promote and recover the status service
questions.stem: Which evidence most directly proves this service met the boot-persistence requirement?
choices: A successful syntax check before the reboot
A green response after running the repair play following a reboot
A different boot ID and correct green response before any post-boot play
questions.explanation: An independent observation before any repair distinguishes successful startup at boot from a service restored afterward by Ansible.

questions.topic: Give a service account read-only access
questions.stem: A process cannot write a file but can rename a replacement over it. Which permission matters first?
choices: Group write and traversal on its parent directory
The file owner’s login shell
The permission to list a parent without traversal
questions.explanation: Renaming replaces a directory entry. Control write and search access to its parent as well as permissions on the file.

questions.topic: Give a service account read-only access
questions.stem: Which test uses the same file access decision the collector will receive?
choices: Read the file with sudo cat
Inspect the encrypted source on the controller
Run test -r on the file under the collector UID
questions.explanation: The kernel checks the process identity, group memberships and all components of the path. Root can read files denied to the consumer.

questions.topic: Give a service account read-only access
questions.stem: A fresh run fails while creating a user whose primary group does not exist. What should the play establish first?
choices: An empty file owned by the account
The required group on the target
An SSH key for the service identity
questions.explanation: The group must already resolve on the target when the user module assigns it as the primary group.

questions.topic: Render a policy and reject a broken candidate
questions.stem: The OS hostname is server, but the JSON needs the inventory name dispatch. What should the template render?
choices: The control node’s hostname
The target’s kernel hostname
inventory_hostname
questions.explanation: The inventory alias identifies the desk independently of its kernel hostname or current IP address.

questions.topic: Render a policy and reject a broken candidate
questions.stem: A malformed template candidate fails the JSON parser supplied to validate. What should the learner find on dispatch?
choices: The last valid destination is intact
A truncated file has replaced the policy
The previous file moves automatically to .bak
questions.explanation: Validation examines the temporary candidate before the module replaces its destination. Compare the deployed public file with its earlier checksum.

questions.topic: Render a policy and reject a broken candidate
questions.stem: A polling interval of 5 is legal JSON but the desk requires 10 through 300. Which check expresses that requirement?
choices: Check the owner of the template
Assert the type and allowed interval before rendering
Have json.tool check for a trailing newline
questions.explanation: Structural JSON validity and a valid business value are different conditions. The assertion checks the input against the desk policy.

questions.topic: Deploy a credential without exposing it in a diff
questions.stem: Which copy is directly protected by encrypting vault.yml?
choices: The deployed plaintext token
The controller source file on disk
Every process that reads the target file
questions.explanation: Vault protects the encrypted source at rest. Target permissions and access checks protect the delivered bytes.

questions.topic: Deploy a credential without exposing it in a diff
questions.stem: A reviewer needs public changes and a recap while the token stays private. How should the author structure the work?
choices: Turn off output for the entire project
Store the token inside a public template with diff enabled
Use a separate credential task with no_log and diff disabled
questions.explanation: Task-scoped output control preserves useful public evidence. The credential also needs restrictive permissions on the managed node.

questions.topic: Deploy a credential without exposing it in a diff
questions.stem: A mode check passes after rotation. Which additional check proves the intended token was installed?
choices: Privately compare all target bytes against the independently supplied expected token
Show the encrypted file changed length
Verify the target file is nonempty
questions.explanation: Different tokens can have identical lengths and permissions. Compare the actual content without displaying it.

questions.topic: Repair permission drift and rotate just the credential
questions.stem: A check-mode run predicts a permission repair. What will the consumer see immediately afterward?
choices: A repaired mode because metadata changes in check mode
The earlier mode until a normal run applies the repair
A different token because the file was opened
questions.explanation: The preview reports a proposed change. An independent access check distinguishes that prediction from an actual repair.

questions.topic: Repair permission drift and rotate just the credential
questions.stem: The Vault password changes while the token inside stays identical. What should a content-based copy do on the next run?
choices: Generate a new application token
Recreate the service account
Leave a correct destination unchanged
questions.explanation: Vault rekey changes the encryption credential. The copy module compares decrypted desired content and requested file attributes with the target.

questions.topic: Repair permission drift and rotate just the credential
questions.stem: A repair of one wrong file mode also changes the public policy on every run. What evidence should you inspect next?
choices: The task-level diff for nondeterministic content or unexpected variables
Only the final unreachable count
Whether the Vault password contains a digit
questions.explanation: An unchanged public policy should render identically. Inspect the specific task and its inputs to explain the extra churn.

questions.topic: Independent practical: hand the collector to the evening shift
questions.stem: The managed host passes every check. What additional observation supports the scope requirement?
choices: The controller can decrypt vault.yml
Archive is reachable with SSH
The collector path remains absent on archive
questions.explanation: A good result on dispatch does not establish that an unintended second host escaped the change. Check the explicitly excluded host.

questions.topic: Independent practical: hand the collector to the evening shift
questions.stem: When should the learner perform the post-reboot acceptance checks?
choices: After changing the desired interval again
