references.title: Course path and practicals
references.body:
## From RHCSA to the final handoffs

Entry skills are those practiced in Zero to RHCSA: use a shell and editor, read Unix permissions, manage a systemd service and identify a guest's network address. This first unit takes you from that point to a verified configuration change over SSH. The development tools unit then puts the project in Git and rehearses a release from a fresh clone. In the third unit you use both existing VMs as SSH targets and rotate pager duty using host-specific data. In the fourth unit you install a signed Apache package on dispatch, promote a local status endpoint, repair a stopped service and test a real reboot. The fifth unit gives a service its own identity and verifies public policy and a Vault-protected credential as that identity. The sixth unit extends the green web service to the private network, uses the packaged firewall role, and verifies an actual client request after a reboot.

| Stage | Practical outcome | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Automation foundations | Select a target, authenticate, deploy a file, detect drift, repair it and prove persistence on AlmaLinux 10 | Included |
| Ansible development tools | Maintain project history in Git, configure ansible-navigator, launch a playbook in an execution environment and use the VS Code development container | Included |
| Variable-driven plays | Separate host data from tasks, gather facts, register results, loop and branch on observations | Included |
| Package and service automation | Configure signed-package repositories, install Apache, apply configuration with a handler and prove the service survives a reboot | Included |
| Managed users and service content | Create a reader identity, deploy a validated template, rotate a vaulted credential and verify its access after reboot | Included |
| Firewall automation | Publish a service only on the intended private network and verify the runtime and saved rules | Included |
| Reusable automation | Build and consume roles, install collections, use local documentation and recover from task failures | Included |
| RHCSA work at scale | Automate storage, file systems, archiving, schedules and security settings on the two authorized practice guests | Included |
| Independent practicals | Apply original multi-host work orders to fresh targets, reboot and evaluate the resulting systems | Included |

Finish by installing your own role and collection, testing rejected releases, provisioning a dedicated ext4 disk, restoring an archive and enabling a daily timer. Practical A asks for a replacement service deployment. Practical B asks for an independently verifiable storage recovery. Keep both projects off the guests before resetting them and use the Assignments tab to retain the evidence.

Red Hat calls EX294 the Red Hat Certified Advanced System Administrator in Ansible exam. Passing it counts toward the RHCE in Ansible credential. EX294 uses Ansible Automation Platform. This course uses the public objectives to guide its practice tasks. The opening unit uses AlmaLinux's ansible-core package. The development tools unit uses community images for both Navigator runs and the VS Code workbench. The practice rubric belongs to Erudior.

[EX294 study objectives and format](https://www.redhat.com/en/services/training/ex294-red-hat-certified-engineer-rhce-exam-red-hat-enterprise-linux)

references.title: Practical answer and scoring guide
references.body:
## One working implementation

In the same controller project, create the new source with `printf 'queue=morning\n' > files/handoff.conf`.

```text
> printf 'queue=morning\n' > files/handoff.conf
No output. The source file contains queue=morning followed by a newline.
```

Save the play below as **handoff.yml**. The morning notice has its own source and destination, so a later edit to the evening notice cannot change it by accident.

```yaml
---
- name: Maintain the morning handoff
  hosts: ops
  gather_facts: false
  become: true
  tasks:
    - name: Deploy the handoff for the morning queue
      ansible.builtin.copy:
        src: files/handoff.conf
        dest: /etc/erudior-handoff.conf
        owner: root
        group: root
        mode: '0640'
```

## Compare your work

| Evidence | Result earning 2 points |
| --- | --- |
| Scope and preview | Only node1 is listed. On a clean target check mode predicts one change. The path is still absent. |
| Deployment | One changed task. Exact morning bytes, root:root 640. Evening bytes and root:root 644 still match. |
| Repeatability | The second live run lists node1, changed=0, failed=0 and unreachable=0. |
| Recovery | Preview identifies the changed line. Applying restores it. The independent byte comparison succeeds and mode is 640. |
| Persistence | Two different boot IDs. Both files pass the remote checks before reapplying. The final run has zero changed, failed or unreachable tasks. |

For deployment and recovery, run `ansible-playbook -K --check --diff handoff.yml` to preview and `ansible-playbook -K handoff.yml` to apply.

```text
> ansible-playbook -K --check --diff handoff.yml
On a fresh target, a predicted copy diff. The handoff file is still absent
after check mode.

> ansible-playbook -K handoff.yml
The first apply creates or repairs the morning notice. A repeat on a
matching file has changed=0.
```

The diff displays the deliberately public practice text; reserve this option for data appropriate to show in a terminal log. An equally correct play may use another suitable module and produce different task totals. Grade the state, the lack of changes on the second live run, and your observations.

references.title: Beta promotion answer and scoring guide
references.body:
## Prepare the candidate

In the editor container's terminal, from the project root on the review branch, update the controller-side input, inspect the staged change, then push it. The server should still contain the alpha file.

```text
> printf 'release=beta\n' > files/release.txt
No output. The tracked release source now contains release=beta.

> git add files/release.txt
No output. Git staged the current versions of the named files for the next
commit.
```

```text
> git diff --cached
A diff of the staged changes that the next commit would record. Press q if a
pager opens.

> git commit -m 'Prepare the beta release note'
A commit summary with branch, abbreviated commit ID and message. Save the ID
for comparison.
```

```text
> git push origin review/beta
Git reports the updated remote branch or that it is already up to date.
Compare the destination branch with the intended one.

> git ls-remote origin refs/heads/main refs/heads/review/beta
Two remote refs, each with its commit ID, after the review branch has been
pushed.
```

## Rehearse and promote

Return to a terminal **on the AlmaLinux client**. Activate the Navigator venv and point this terminal at the dedicated agent if needed. Use the clean second checkout. On a repeat attempt where a local review branch already exists, switch to it and fast-forward it to the fetched remote commit.

```text
> source ~/.venvs/rhce-nav/bin/activate
No routine output. The shell now resolves Python and pip through the virtual
environment.

> export SSH_AUTH_SOCK="$HOME/.local/share/erudior-rhce-agent/socket"
No output. SSH clients launched from this shell now use the specified
socket.
```

```text
> cd ~/rhce-rehearsal
No output. The shell now works in the named project directory.

> git fetch origin
Git fetches new remote refs, or finishes quietly if they are already
current.
```

```text
> git switch --track origin/review/beta
Git switches to a local review/beta branch tracking origin/review/beta.

> git rev-parse HEAD
The full commit ID currently checked out in this directory.
```

```text
> git ls-remote origin refs/heads/review/beta
A full commit ID followed by the requested remote branch ref.

> ansible-navigator inventory -i inventory.ini --graph
The execution environment's inventory graph with node1 under @ops.
```

```text
> ansible-navigator run release.yml --check --diff
A predicted diff from the current release note to the tracked candidate. The
target file is untouched by this copy preview.
```

Check the bytes at the server console while the file should still be alpha. Then run the following command from the client.

```text
> ansible-navigator run release.yml
An absent or different release note gives changed=1. A second successful run
on the same commit gives changed=0.
```

Check the resulting bytes and metadata on the server, and run the same play again on the client. The following checks belong on the **server** after applying.

```text
> printf 'release=beta\n' | cmp - ~/erudior-release.txt && echo beta-ok
beta-ok

> stat -c '%U:%G %a' ~/erudior-release.txt
learner:learner 644
```

```text
> printf 'shift=evening\n' | cmp - /etc/erudior-shift.conf && echo evening-ok
evening-ok

> printf 'queue=morning\n' | sudo cmp - /etc/erudior-handoff.conf && echo morning-ok
morning-ok
```

The course VMs should report `learner:learner 644`, all three success messages, then `changed=0`, `failed=0` and `unreachable=0` for the repeated play. A [[Fast-forward]] moves the branch pointer to a descendant commit without creating a merge commit. After the tests pass, run on the rehearsal **client**:

```text
> git switch main
Git reports that the current branch is main.

> git merge --ff-only review/beta
A fast-forward report or Already up to date. Divergent histories cause a
refusal.
```

```text
> git push origin main
Git reports the updated remote branch or that it is already up to date.
Compare the destination branch with the intended one.

> git rev-parse HEAD
The full commit ID currently checked out in this directory.
```

```text
> git ls-remote origin refs/heads/main
A full commit ID followed by the requested remote branch ref.
```

The two final IDs should equal the candidate you tested. If main advanced on the server, fetch and inspect `git log --oneline --graph --all`.

```text
> git log --oneline --graph --all
A graph of commits with an abbreviated ID and subject per line.
```

Reconcile competing changes on a review branch and retest the resulting commit before promotion. This protects the other operator's work.

references.title: Desk state checker
references.body:
## Check the guest independently

Save this script as **check-desk.sh** in `~/rhce-desks` on the client. It checks exact bytes including the newline, numeric permissions, ownership, file type and the required absence of the optional notice. It reports the first failed check and returns a nonzero exit status.

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -eu

shift_name=${1:-}
pager_state=${2:-}
case "$shift_name" in day|night) ;; *) echo 'Expected day or night' >&2; exit 2 ;; esac
case "$pager_state" in on|off) ;; *) echo 'Expected on or off' >&2; exit 2 ;; esac

fail() { printf 'FAIL %s\n' "$1" >&2; exit 1; }

check_file() {
  local path=$1 line=$2 mode=$3
  [[ -f $path && ! -L $path ]] || fail "$path is not a regular file"
  printf '%s\n' "$line" | cmp - "$path" || fail "$path content"
  [[ $(stat -c '%U:%G %a' "$path") == "learner:learner $mode" ]] || fail "$path ownership or mode"
}

check_file "$HOME/rhce-board.txt" "board=$shift_name" 644
check_file "$HOME/rhce-roster.txt" "roster=$shift_name" 640
if [[ $pager_state == on ]]; then
  check_file "$HOME/rhce-pager.txt" 'duty=on-call' 600
else
  [[ ! -e $HOME/rhce-pager.txt && ! -L $HOME/rhce-pager.txt ]] || fail 'pager notice still present'
fi
printf 'PASS %s shift=%s pager=%s\n' "$(hostname -s)" "$shift_name" "$pager_state"
```

From the **client project root**, define this shell function. It uses your trusted project keys for the SSH server and the loaded lab identity for login. Substitute your private addresses if needed.

```text
> check_desk() {
>   local guest=$1 shift_name=$2 pager_state=$3
>   ssh -o BatchMode=yes -o StrictHostKeyChecking=yes \
>     -o UserKnownHostsFile=./ssh/known_hosts "learner@$guest" \
>     bash -s -- "$shift_name" "$pager_state" < check-desk.sh
> }
No output after the closing brace. The check_desk helper is defined for this
shell.
```

| Checkpoint | Dispatch command | Archive command |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Starting state, after invalid policy, and after limited preview | `check_desk 192.168.77.10 day on` | `check_desk 192.168.77.20 night off` |
| After limited apply | `check_desk 192.168.77.10 day on` | `check_desk 192.168.77.20 day on` |
| After full rotation and repeat | `check_desk 192.168.77.10 night off` | `check_desk 192.168.77.20 day on` |

If an expected-absent check fails, inspect the path with `ls -ld`. If a content check fails, compare the exact expected text, including its newline. For a metadata failure, inspect `stat -c '%U:%G %a' filename` on that guest. Keep the command output with the matching checkpoint.

references.title: Duty rotation answer and scoring guide
references.body:
## Change the data and prove the scope

Under **host_vars/dispatch.yml** set `desk_shift: night` and remove the former pager override. The group default supplies false. In **host_vars/archive.yml** remove the old night-shift override so the group day shift takes effect. Start the negative test with `desk_pager: 'true'` on archive. Run `ansible-playbook desks.yml`: the boolean assertion should fail on archive before either host enters the deployment tasks.

```text
> ansible-playbook desks.yml
The first run repairs differences on the targeted desks. An immediate repeat
should report changed=0 and failed=0 for both.
```

The failing test supplies evidence for the rejection row. Correct that file to `desk_pager: true` before continuing.

The final **host_vars/dispatch.yml** is:

```yaml
---
desk_shift: night
```

The final **host_vars/archive.yml** is:

```yaml
---
desk_pager: true
```

## Observe each transition

Run from `~/rhce-desks` on the client with the lab key loaded. Use the checker reference at each boundary.

```text
> ansible-inventory --host dispatch
JSON showing the variables resolved for this inventory alias. Compare
desk_shift and desk_pager with the host's policy.

> ansible-inventory --host archive
JSON showing the variables resolved for this inventory alias. Compare
desk_shift and desk_pager with the host's policy.
```

```text
> ansible-playbook desks.yml --limit archive --check --diff
A predicted change only for archive. Dispatch should be absent from the
recap.
```

At this point the old state should still pass on both machines. Apply the limited change, then test both dispatch and archive for day/on. This overlap is the handoff checkpoint. If the incoming desk fails, the outgoing desk still has its pager notice.

```text
> ansible-playbook desks.yml --limit archive
The live archive host changes to its incoming duty state. Verify its notice
before changing dispatch.
```

With the approved exercise sequence complete on archive, run on both guests. Use the same image and Navigator config that you brought over from the previous unit.

```text
> source ~/.venvs/rhce-nav/bin/activate
No routine output. The shell now resolves Python and pip through the virtual
environment.

> ansible-navigator run desks.yml
Both desk aliases appear in the recap. Expect changed=0 on a repeat after
the requested state is correct.
```

```text
> ansible-playbook desks.yml
The first run repairs differences on the targeted desks. An immediate repeat
should report changed=0 and failed=0 for both.
```

On the first full run, archive should have zero changes. Dispatch should report two changed tasks. The loop installs two night-shift files, and the removal task retires the old pager notice. Confirm dispatch is night/off and archive is day/on. The final run should report `changed=0`, `failed=0` and `unreachable=0` for each host. At the server console, `printf 'release=beta\n' | cmp - ~/erudior-release.txt && echo previous-release-ok` verifies the earlier release.

```text
> printf 'release=beta\n' | cmp - ~/erudior-release.txt && echo previous-release-ok
previous-release-ok
```

If dispatch still has a pager file, inspect the resolved boolean and the removal condition. If the archive roster has the day text but the wrong mode, inspect the roster list entry. Those are different causes even if both end-state checks fail.

references.title: Web service checker
references.body:
## Test the server as a local HTTP client

Save this script as **check-web.sh** in the learner home on **dispatch**. Run `bash ~/check-web.sh blue` before promotion and `bash ~/check-web.sh green` after it.

```text
> bash ~/check-web.sh blue
The RPM version and a PASS line for loopback HTTP 200 with the requested
release and team.

> bash ~/check-web.sh green
The RPM version and a PASS line for loopback HTTP 200 with the requested
release and team.
```

It uses tools already on the practice guest. Supply the expected release from the ticket. The checker queries the RPM database, asks systemd about both unit states, checks every port 80 listening address, and sends a new HTTP request. It exits with a nonzero status at the first failed check.

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -eu
track=${1:-}
case "$track" in
  blue) team=operations ;;
  green) team=support ;;
  *) echo 'Usage: bash check-web.sh blue|green' >&2; exit 2 ;;
esac
rpm -q httpd
systemctl is-enabled --quiet httpd.service
systemctl is-active --quiet httpd.service
socket=$(ss -H -ltn 'sport = :80' | awk '{print $4}')
[[ $socket == 127.0.0.1:80 ]] || { echo "Unexpected port 80 listener: $socket" >&2; exit 1; }
python3 - "$track" "$team" <<'PYCODE'
import http.client
import sys
conn = http.client.HTTPConnection("127.0.0.1", 80, timeout=5)
conn.request("GET", "/erudior-status.txt")
response = conn.getresponse()
observed = (response.status, response.read(), response.getheader("X-Erudior-Release"),
            response.getheader("X-Erudior-Team"))
expected = (200, b"desk=dispatch\n", sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2])
if observed != expected:
    raise SystemExit(f"Unexpected HTTP result: {observed!r}")
print(f"PASS loopback HTTP 200, release={sys.argv[1]}, team={sys.argv[2]}")
PYCODE
```

A successful output includes the installed RPM version and a PASS line. For a silent failure before the HTTP output, inspect `systemctl is-enabled httpd` and `systemctl is-active httpd` separately, or run `bash -x ~/check-web.sh green`.

```text
> systemctl is-enabled httpd
disabled on the prepared package-only baseline, enabled after service
configuration.

> systemctl is-active httpd
inactive before the service is started, active after the service play
succeeds.
```

```text
> bash -x ~/check-web.sh green
The shell traces the nonsecret web checks, ending with PASS if the green
response matches.
```

An unexpected-listener failure prints the actual endpoints. An HTTP mismatch shows the observed status, body and headers.

You can also save the script on the **client** and send its contents over the same trusted SSH connection used earlier. Run this from the web project root and use dispatch’s actual private address.

```text
> ssh -o BatchMode=yes -o StrictHostKeyChecking=yes \
>   -o UserKnownHostsFile=./ssh/known_hosts learner@192.168.77.10 \
>   bash -s -- green < check-web.sh
The RPM version and a PASS line for loopback HTTP 200 with the requested
release and team.
```

The HTTP connection still originates on dispatch. Its loopback address has the same meaning from its console and from its remote SSH session.

references.title: Web promotion scoring guide
references.body:
## Baseline and preview

From the client, use the **rhce-web** project with the lab key loaded. At the server console, inspect **/etc/yum.repos.d/erudior-web.repo**. The two IDs should be erudior-baseos and erudior-appstream, with package signature checking enabled and the AlmaLinux 10 key from /etc/pki/rpm-gpg. Check `rpm -q httpd`, run the checker for blue, and capture the working blue/operations headers.

```text
> rpm -q httpd
The installed httpd version, or package httpd is not installed on the fresh
baseline.
```

In **group_vars/web.yml** change only `release_track: blue` to `release_track: green`. Leave the team mapping as authored. On the client, run the preview.

```text
> cd ~/rhce-web
No output. The shell now works in the named project directory.

> ansible-playbook site.yml --check --diff
A diff predicts the requested release change. The currently served release
remains available until apply.
```

Find both header file differences. A predicted handler line is possible in check mode. On dispatch a separate blue checker must still pass.

## Apply and recover

Use the Navigator environment already staged on the client. For a sudo policy that requires authentication, pass `-K` and supply the become password interactively.

```text
> source ~/.venvs/rhce-nav/bin/activate
No routine output. The shell now resolves Python and pip through the virtual
environment.

> ansible-navigator run site.yml
The running service reflects the tracked release. A follow-up apply with the
same inputs has changed=0.
```

```text
> ansible-playbook site.yml
The first apply reports changes needed for the web policy. An immediate
repeat on the correct server reports changed=0, failed=0.
```

For the controlled blue-to-green transition the first recap should report three changed tasks on dispatch. Two write different header snippets and a single handler reloads the service. The second recap should have zero changes. On the server, prove green/support with the independent checker. A stable **MainPID** across a graceful reload is compatible with success. The live response demonstrates which settings took effect.

At the **dispatch console** create the practice fault. Record the results of both systemctl queries, including their nonzero statuses if scripting the exercise.

```text
> sudo systemctl disable --now httpd.service
The service stops now and its enablement link is removed for the deliberate
recovery exercise.

> systemctl is-enabled httpd.service
disabled on the prepared package-only baseline, enabled after service
configuration.
```

```text
> systemctl is-active httpd.service
inactive before the service is started, active after the service play
succeeds.
```

On the client run the following command again.

```text
> ansible-playbook site.yml
The first apply reports changes needed for the web policy. An immediate
repeat on the correct server reports changed=0, failed=0.
```

The task that declares enabled and started should repair both properties. With the header files intact, this single changed task is sufficient. The named reload handler should have no invocation. On dispatch run the following command again.

```text
> bash ~/check-web.sh green
The RPM version and a PASS line for loopback HTTP 200 with the requested
release and team.
```

## Prove the reboot result before repair

On dispatch, copy the first boot ID into your notes, then reboot the **dispatch VM**. The Ansible client stays up.

```text
> cat /proc/sys/kernel/random/boot_id
A boot identifier with five groups of hexadecimal characters. Compare it
with your earlier reading to detect a reboot.

> sudo systemctl reboot
The guest restarts. Reconnect, then compare its new boot ID with the one
recorded earlier.
```

Reconnect to dispatch after it boots. Run the following before another deployment. Use the earlier **Desk state checker** in place of check-desk.sh if you saved it under another path.

```text
> cat /proc/sys/kernel/random/boot_id
A boot identifier with five groups of hexadecimal characters. Compare it
with your earlier reading to detect a reboot.

> bash ~/check-web.sh green
The RPM version and a PASS line for loopback HTTP 200 with the requested
release and team.
```

```text
> printf 'release=beta\n' | cmp - ~/erudior-release.txt && echo previous-release-ok
previous-release-ok
```

Check dispatch with `check_desk 192.168.77.10 night off` and archive with `check_desk 192.168.77.20 day on` using the function and script from the previous unit, from **~/rhce-desks** on the client.

```text
> check_desk 192.168.77.10 night off
A PASS line naming the guest and requested shift and pager state. A mismatch
returns FAIL with the affected check.

> check_desk 192.168.77.20 day on
A PASS line naming the guest and requested shift and pager state. A mismatch
returns FAIL with the affected check.
```

Finish back in **~/rhce-web** with `ansible-playbook site.yml`.

```text
> ansible-playbook site.yml
The first apply reports changes needed for the web policy. An immediate
repeat on the correct server reports changed=0, failed=0.
```

The expected recap is zero changed, failed and unreachable for dispatch.

If reboot brings back the service but an HTTP header is stale, capture the live response and inspect the two managed snippets. If an old service never started at all, use `systemctl status httpd`, `journalctl -u httpd -b`, and `sudo /usr/sbin/httpd -t` on the server to identify the failure before changing inventory.

```text
> systemctl status httpd
The HTTP service's loaded and active states plus recent messages.

> journalctl -u httpd -b
This boot's journal for httpd, including starts, reloads or failures.
```

```text
> sudo /usr/sbin/httpd -t
Syntax OK
```

Award two points per completed evidence row in the work order, up to ten.

references.title: Set up and reset the AlmaLinux 10.3 lab
references.body:
# AlmaLinux 10.3 practice lab for RHCSA and RHCE in Ansible

Use one official installer for both courses. The smaller **Erudior-setup.iso** in this kit is a second, read-only disc with the guest configuration scripts. The host launcher attaches both discs. Keep the four scripts and the setup disc together with **lab.py** after extracting the ZIP.

**Already using Erudior's graded RHCSA desktop exam?** Open the completed attempt, save its result, select **Reset exam disks**, then **Prepare machines** for a fresh attempt. Use **Begin** when ready for the timer. The desktop app supplies its own guest identities, exercises and isolated overlays. See “Graded desktop template” below for its one-time image setup. The host commands below manage the separate manual practice pair.

## 1.

Get and verify the installation DVD

[Download AlmaLinux 10.3 x86_64 DVD ISO](https://repo.almalinux.org/almalinux/10.3/isos/x86_64/AlmaLinux-10.3-x86_64-dvd.iso) · [Signed checksums](https://repo.almalinux.org/almalinux/10.3/isos/x86_64/CHECKSUM) · [Release notes and signing fingerprint](https://wiki.almalinux.org/release-notes/10.3) · [AlmaLinux signing key](https://repo.almalinux.org/almalinux/RPM-GPG-KEY-AlmaLinux-10)

Use the full DVD for the standard x86_64 architecture. It carries BaseOS and AppStream for the offline installation and package labs. Its exact size is **10,824,908,800 bytes**. The SHA-256 digest is **f74ae9c4a8e7e3e70147534856ea276f71649d16c70b7d3ec80d0905a7b93982**. The host launcher checks both before creating any lab disks.

The kit also includes the upstream signed CHECKSUM and public key. To inspect them with GnuPG from the kit directory on Linux:

```text
> keyring=$(mktemp -d)
No output. keyring holds a new temporary directory for this verification.
```

`gpg` inspects keys and verifies signatures. A separate --homedir confines this exercise's key material to the chosen directory.

```text
> gpg --homedir "$keyring" --show-keys --with-fingerprint RPM-GPG-KEY-AlmaLinux-10
The key's fingerprint and identity. Compare the entire fingerprint with the
trusted published value.

> gpg --homedir "$keyring" --dearmor --output "$keyring/alma.gpg" RPM-GPG-KEY-AlmaLinux-10
No normal output. alma.gpg is written inside the temporary directory.
```

```text
> gpg --homedir "$keyring" --no-default-keyring --keyring "$keyring/alma.gpg" --verify CHECKSUM
Look for Good signature from the verified AlmaLinux key. A bad signature
fails this check.

> sha256sum ~/Downloads/AlmaLinux-10.3-x86_64-dvd.iso
A 64-character hexadecimal digest and the ISO path. Compare every character
to the signed checksum.
```

Match the full primary fingerprint **EE6D B7B9 8F5B F5ED D9DA 0DE5 DEE5 C11C C2A1 E572** against the release notes. Look for a good signature, then match the computed digest to the exact DVD filename in CHECKSUM. If the distribution moves the point release to its archive, use an official AlmaLinux mirror with that same filename and digest.

## 2.

Create the two manual guests

Use a Linux desktop host with Python 3.9+, QEMU system x86 with a graphical display, and qemu-img. On Fedora install `sudo dnf install python3 qemu-system-x86 qemu-img qemu-ui-gtk`.

```text
> sudo dnf install python3 qemu-system-x86 qemu-img qemu-ui-gtk
A package transaction for the requested host or guest tools, or confirmation
they are already installed.
```

On Debian install `sudo apt install python3 qemu-system-x86 qemu-system-gui qemu-utils`.

`apt` installs packages on a Debian-based host.

```text
> sudo apt install python3 qemu-system-x86 qemu-system-gui qemu-utils
A package transaction for the requested host or guest tools, or confirmation
they are already installed.
```

Windows users can run the Linux launcher inside a graphical WSL 2 distro with WSLg. Store its VM disks on the distro's Linux filesystem. On macOS the Erudior graded desktop route uses Lima. For this manual launcher use a graphical Linux VM with sufficient resources. KVM acceleration is used on eligible x86_64 hosts with accessible /dev/kvm. Software emulation uses QEMU's max CPU. Allow at least 8 GiB for the pair plus memory for the host and enough disk for the DVD, both installed systems, and a standalone copy at each saved baseline.

| Setting | Server | Client |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Virtual CPU and memory | 2 vCPUs, 4 GiB | 2 vCPUs, 4 GiB |
| Install destination | 30 GiB system disk | 30 GiB system disk |
| Practice storage after installation | Two blank 2 GiB disks | Two blank 2 GiB disks |
| Private host address | 192.168.77.10/24 | 192.168.77.20/24 |
| RHCE role | Managed node | Ansible control node |
| Virtual network | Private link plus a separate NAT uplink | Same private link, independent NAT uplink |

The private link uses a loopback socket on host port 25763 for RHCSA or 25764 for RHCE. Guest traffic stays off the physical LAN. Port 25763/25764 must be free on the host. Use the local guest consoles. The launcher creates its disks inside **~/Erudior-Practice/rhcsa** or **~/Erudior-Practice/rhce**. Use one track at a time if memory is limited. Keep each track directory at its original path because qcow2 overlays reference absolute baseline paths.

From the extracted kit directory on the host, substitute **rhce** for **rhcsa** throughout if building the automation pair.

```text
> python3 lab.py init rhcsa ~/Downloads/AlmaLinux-10.3-x86_64-dvd.iso
The kit prepares disposable disk images and records the installer location
for the chosen profile.

> python3 lab.py install rhcsa server
The named guest starts with the installer. Its installation screen appears
in the VM console.
```

In the installer choose **Minimal Install**, automatic partitioning of the single 30 GiB disk, a local user **learner**, a password you choose, and **administrator** membership. Complete installation and reboot from the system disk. Leave the server VM running for the client’s private-network connection. If you closed it, run the following command first.

```text
> python3 lab.py start rhcsa server
The selected VM or pair starts. Wait for the installed guest login prompts.
```

```text
> python3 lab.py install rhcsa client
The named guest starts with the installer. Its installation screen appears
in the VM console.
```

Make the same installation choices on the client. After both installations, power off both from their consoles with `sudo systemctl poweroff`.

```text
> sudo systemctl poweroff
The guest shuts down. Its console stops accepting input after shutdown.
```

Run the following command on the host.

```text
> python3 lab.py start rhcsa
The selected VM or pair starts. Wait for the installed guest login prompts.
```

This normal boot attaches both storage-practice disks to each machine and starts the server before the client. Only the system disk was present during installation.

## 3.

Configure and check the guests

At each guest console, as learner, mount the supplied setup disc. The installer DVD stays attached for packages. The setup script selects the private NIC by the MAC assigned by the launcher.

```text
> sudo mkdir -p /mnt/erudior-tools
No output. The media mountpoint exists.

> sudo mount -o ro /dev/disk/by-label/ERUDIORLAB /mnt/erudior-tools
The medium is mounted read-only. A read-only notice is normal for optical
media.
```

| Where to run it | RHCSA | RHCE |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Server console | `sudo bash /mnt/erudior-tools/prepare-guest.sh rhcsa server` | `sudo bash /mnt/erudior-tools/prepare-guest.sh rhce server` |
| Client console | `sudo bash /mnt/erudior-tools/prepare-guest.sh rhcsa client` | `sudo bash /mnt/erudior-tools/prepare-guest.sh rhce client` |

For offline RHCE web-package labs, set the playbook repository base URL to `file:///mnt/erudior-dvd/{{ item }}/` on the managed server. Keep the exercise’s repository IDs, signing key, GPG checks and explicit repository selection. The installed DVD supplies both the catalogs and signed RPMs.

Both profiles enable SSH, the firewall and chrony, use AlmaLinux's trusted key for RPM packages, and require enforcing SELinux. The course DVD repositories are disabled by default and explicitly selected for setup. On later offline package exercises use `sudo dnf --disablerepo='*' --enablerepo='erudior-dvd-*' list --available`.

```text
> sudo dnf --disablerepo='*' --enablerepo='erudior-dvd-*' list --available
Available RPMs from the DVD repositories.
```

The guest mounts the attached installer DVD on demand after reboot.

**RHCSA.** The server supplies a read-only NFS marker restricted to the client and an initially stopped, disabled maintenance unit. The client has an empty repository catalog for the repository exercise. The practice disks, learner account tasks, automount configuration, storage layouts and service-repair work are left for the learner. After both machines are configured run `sudo bash /mnt/erudior-tools/check-guest.sh rhcsa server` on the server and `sudo bash /mnt/erudior-tools/check-guest.sh rhcsa client` on the client.

```text
> sudo bash /mnt/erudior-tools/check-guest.sh rhcsa server
The kit reports its checks for that guest. Resolve any failed check before
capturing a baseline.

> sudo bash /mnt/erudior-tools/check-guest.sh rhcsa client
The kit reports its checks for that guest. Resolve any failed check before
capturing a baseline.
```

The client check mounts and reads the actual NFS export, then unmounts it.

**RHCE.** From the server console display the fingerprint with `sudo ssh-keygen -lf /etc/ssh/ssh_host_ed25519_key.pub`.

```text
> sudo ssh-keygen -lf /etc/ssh/ssh_host_ed25519_key.pub
A SHA256 fingerprint and algorithm. Compare the full fingerprint through the
trusted console.
```

As **learner on the client**, run the following command, compare the fingerprint when prompted, and enter the credentials you chose.

```text
> bash /mnt/erudior-tools/pair-control.sh
Follow the fingerprint prompt, then verify key-based access from the control
node to the server.
```

The helper creates or reuses the dedicated learner key, verifies the remote hostname, runs an Ansible ping and requests sudo to confirm UID 0. It ends the temporary SSH agent. Run `sudo bash /mnt/erudior-tools/check-guest.sh rhce server` and `sudo bash /mnt/erudior-tools/check-guest.sh rhce client` on the corresponding guests.

```text
> sudo bash /mnt/erudior-tools/check-guest.sh rhce server
The kit reports its checks for that guest. Resolve any failed check before
capturing a baseline.

> sudo bash /mnt/erudior-tools/check-guest.sh rhce client
The kit reports its checks for that guest. Resolve any failed check before
capturing a baseline.
```

For the Navigator and editor practicals, keep NAT online during one-time preparation. As **learner on the RHCE client**, run the following command.

```text
> bash /mnt/erudior-tools/stage-rhce-tools.sh
The staging script prepares the Navigator tools and execution image for
later offline use.
```

This stages the course’s pinned Navigator version, rootless Podman execution image and development image, then executes Ansible in the locally stored runtime. Open the course’s VS Code Dev Containers workspace once while online to stage the editor components and establish the workspace mounts. Use the course's **Identify the Ansible runtime** and **Author and run an inspection play in VS Code** lessons to verify the actual editor and playbook workflow. Retain the previous unit's inputs when capturing a later practical's baseline. Red Hat uses RHEL 10 for EX200 and Red Hat Ansible Automation Platform for EX294. These are Erudior practice profiles.

## 4.

Capture once and reset for each attempt

Reboot once and confirm the expected private addresses, SELinux state and peer access. Remount the setup disc to run the checks again if needed. Save your baseline **after preparation and before solving the test**. At each guest console use `sudo systemctl poweroff`.

```text
> sudo systemctl poweroff
The guest shuts down. Its console stops accepting input after shutdown.
```

On the **host**, run the command for your track:

```text
> python3 lab.py capture rhcsa
The kit records the powered-off pair as the requested baseline. An active
guest can prevent capture.
```

**For the separately prepared automation pair**

```text
> python3 lab.py capture rhce
The kit records the powered-off pair as the requested baseline. An active
guest can prevent capture.
```

For your **next fresh attempt** use one host command:

```text
> python3 lab.py reset rhcsa --start --offline
The selected kit baseline is restored and the guests start with offline
networking. Check the consoles after boot.
```

**Or**

```text
> python3 lab.py reset rhce --start --offline
The selected kit baseline is restored and the guests start with offline
networking. Check the consoles after boot.
```

Reset gracefully powers off any running guests on that track, switches all six disks to fresh overlays of the saved baseline as one operation, and optionally starts the pair. `--offline` restricts the new guests' NAT uplinks and keeps their private connection. Omit it for lessons that need external downloads. Without `--start`, the reset pair stays off. Changes since capture are discarded, including guest-local Git commits and assessment evidence. Save work you want to keep outside the VMs first. After a cold boot, reload any passphrase-protected key into your terminal’s SSH agent. The key and its trust records on disk return with the baseline.

A **named baseline** is useful when a practical starts partway through the course. For the RHCE web promotion, first complete the blue deployment, run the blue endpoint checker, and shut down both guests. Then use:

```text
> python3 lab.py capture rhce --baseline web-blue
The kit records the powered-off pair as the requested baseline. An active
guest can prevent capture.

> python3 lab.py reset rhce --baseline web-blue --start --offline
The selected kit baseline is restored and the guests start with offline
networking. Check the consoles after boot.
```

```text
> python3 lab.py status rhce
The kit reports the status of both guests and their profile.
```

Reusing an existing capture name is refused. Resetting one track leaves the other track and all saved baselines alone. If a broken guest cannot handle ACPI shutdown, `python3 lab.py reset rhce --force-off --start --offline` requests an immediate power-off of that track’s disposable VMs before restoring them. Use the correct track and baseline name. The launcher refuses a reset when no such baseline exists. A preparation failure leaves the current disk set selected. Close any external program that has opened a practice disk before retrying.

## Graded desktop template

Use the combined RHCSA course's **First-time setup** for its Linux provider (Linux directly, WSL 2 or Lima). The desktop runner expects a standalone BIOS-bootable qcow2 with NoCloud support and a serial console. Obtain the standard [AlmaLinux 10.3 x86_64 Generic Cloud image and checksums](https://repo.almalinux.org/almalinux/10.3/cloud/x86_64/images/), work on a separate copy and attach the verified installer DVD and the supplied setup disc. In that temporary guest mount ERUDIORLAB as above and run the following command.

```text
> sudo bash /mnt/erudior-tools/prepare-guest.sh desktop-template
The guest preparation script configures the disposable desktop template.
```

This installs the engine prerequisites and enables the ttyS0 serial login. The runner configures each attempt's user, addresses, private link and task fixtures.

Check NoCloud support, enforcing SELinux, and serial login. Remove provisioning-only credentials from the template copy, run the following command and power it off.

```text
> sudo cloud-init clean --logs --machine-id
No routine output. Cloud-init state is cleared for the dedicated template's
next first boot.
```

Flatten the powered-off image with `qemu-img convert -O qcow2 SOURCE.qcow2 almalinux-10-rhcsa.qcow2` to a new destination. `qemu-img info --backing-chain almalinux-10-rhcsa.qcow2` should show one standalone disk.

`qemu-img` creates, converts and inspects virtual disk images.

```text
> qemu-img info --backing-chain almalinux-10-rhcsa.qcow2
The image format and backing chain. Verify the exported image stands on its
own.
```

Install it inside the provider's **~/.local/share/erudior-vm-labs/images/** directory, or its configured XDG data directory. Keep any older base image while attempts still refer to it. Follow the combined course's image profile and use its normal **Prepare machines / Begin / Save exam result / Reset exam disks** controls. A manual lab reset has no access to desktop exam records.

[Red Hat EX200 objectives](https://www.redhat.com/en/services/training/ex200-red-hat-certified-system-administrator-rhcsa-exam) · [Red Hat EX294 objectives](https://www.redhat.com/en/services/training/ex294-red-hat-certified-engineer-rhce-exam-red-hat-enterprise-linux)
